meta.title: Rome 100 AD to the Transistor: dependency tree

nodes.name: Three geographically separated academies
nodes.note: Alexandria (dry, preserves papyrus), a western site, an eastern site. The Third Century Crisis will destroy at least one. Redundancy is the only defence and it is not optional. CALENDAR FLOOR is set by diffusion, not by construction: the economy needs roughly a generation to train the trades, form the capital and build the suppliers. Money cannot buy this down. THE STATE WILL ACTIVELY RESIST THIS. A large private association operating across several provinces is precisely what Roman government fears: a faction. Trajan refuses Pliny even a licensed fire brigade at Nicomedia for this reason (Ep. 10.34). You need senatorial or imperial cover before you attempt it, and you should site the three houses under three different patrons so that it does not look like one organisation.

nodes.name: Adulteration law and enforcement
nodes.note: The Pure Food Act that created food inspection; enforcement scale determines whether regulation reduces fraud

nodes.name: Artificial insemination in cattle
nodes.note: Timing ovulation by oestrus observation and the catheter technique that reaches the cervix without trauma

nodes.name: Balanced ration
nodes.note: The Wolff-Lehmann standard that calculates feed units by proximate analysis, not arbitrary eye assessment

nodes.name: Baler
nodes.note: The double-screw compression mechanism that packs dense bales and the knotter that wraps twine on the fly

nodes.name: Basic slag
nodes.note: A recycling of blast-furnace slag waste that becomes a double amendment of phosphate and lime simultaneously

nodes.name: Battery poultry
nodes.note: Birds never see soil or natural light; welfare costs are paid years later in disease epidemic risk

nodes.name: Biological control
nodes.note: The discipline of rearing and release timing, and the risk that introduced enemies become pests themselves

nodes.name: Bone meal
nodes.note: Steam processing and fine grinding that makes phosphorus available on a 3-5 year curve instead of 20 years

nodes.name: Bordeaux mixture
nodes.note: The precise ratio of copper to lime and the timing relative to rain that prevents phytotoxicity

nodes.name: Botanic garden as instrument of empire
nodes.note: The staggered shipments from multiple botanical gardens ensuring a crop could not be lost in a single voyage

nodes.name: Bottling
nodes.note: Bottle standardisation and cork sealing that prevents oxidation and breakage

nodes.name: Budding
nodes.note: Timing the bark slip in spring and the healing period through summer before growth resumes in spring

nodes.name: Butter
nodes.note: The inversion of emulsion where fat phase becomes continuous and buttermilk phase separates out

nodes.name: Canning
nodes.note: Botulism toxin prevention by adequate temperature and time, plus the headspace air displacement

nodes.name: Caterpillar track
nodes.note: The idler and tensioner that keep tracks tight over soft mud, and the steering clutch for each side

nodes.name: The centrifugal machine for sugar
nodes.note: Vibration that prevents sugar from caking against the screen and the automated discharge timer

nodes.name: Chaff cutter
nodes.note: Simple but the blade speed and feed rate determine length consistency and safety

nodes.name: Cheese families
nodes.note: Hard cheeses start with cut curd cooked high, soft with whole milk curdled low - technique differences are vast

nodes.name: Coffee cultivation after voyage
nodes.note: Shade trees and altitude matching matter; three years to first harvest after planting

nodes.name: Cold store
nodes.note: Insulation thickness, air circulation path, and humidity control that prevents condensation and drip

nodes.name: Column still
nodes.note: Rectifying columns that eliminate headache-causing congeners, producing neutral spirits from any fermented base

nodes.name: Combine harvester
nodes.note: The drum-and-concave threshing, chaffer separation, and power-driven grain elevator all working at forward speed

nodes.name: Composting
nodes.note: Temperature control and moisture management that turns putrefaction into complete decomposition in months not years

nodes.name: Condensed milk
nodes.note: Vacuum boiling at low temperature prevents caramelisation; sugar saturation prevents crystallisation

nodes.name: Contour ploughing
nodes.note: Discipline to follow contours accurately and the knowledge that it trades steeper fields for water retention

nodes.name: Controlled pollination
nodes.note: The emasculation technique that prevents self-pollination and the timing that ensures pollen viability

nodes.name: Coulter
nodes.note: Not the plough itself but the cutting disc that precedes it

nodes.name: Cream separator
nodes.note: Bowl speed critical - too slow leaves cream in skim, too fast shatters fat globules into foam

nodes.name: Crown cork
nodes.note: Cork lining that seals without cracking, serrated edge that grips bottle rim without slipping

nodes.name: Cultivator
nodes.note: The adjustable parallelogram linkage that keeps tines parallel and depth constant despite ground variation

nodes.name: DDT
nodes.note: Persistence is the point and the peril: it accumulates in wildlife fat and breaks eggshells decades later

nodes.name: Double seam can
nodes.note: The pressure-sealing geometry and tool wear that prevents leakage during handling and retort pressure

nodes.name: Erosion control - wind breaks and mulch
nodes.note: The spacing of shelterbelts for protection depth and the depth of mulch that protects soil without smothering germination

nodes.name: Evaporated milk
nodes.note: The homogenisation that prevents cream separation during long shelf life and the heat-shock that stabilises casein

nodes.name: Fanning mill
nodes.note: The combination of vibrating screens, fan speed modulation, and multiple air streams that grade by size and weight in one pass

nodes.name: Fat hydrogenation
nodes.note: Temperature control to avoid polymerisation; partial hydrogenation creates trans-fats unknowingly

nodes.name: Fermentation control
nodes.note: Acetobacter infection control by nitrogen blanking and acid production, removing risk of vinegar accident

nodes.name: Food laboratory and testing
nodes.note: Gravimetric fat and protein, acidimetry for pH, microscopy for moulds - methods that define food standards

nodes.name: Ammonium sulphate from gasworks
nodes.note: The first synthetic nitrogen fertiliser, 20% nitrogen, soluble and available within weeks of application

nodes.name: Grafting
nodes.note: The cambium contact and timing that determine success, and which combinations produce fertile trees

nodes.name: Gravity and pump irrigation
nodes.note: The weir and sluice design that manages flow, and the laterals spaced to avoid either drowning or drought

nodes.name: Green manure
nodes.note: The timing of ploughing in clover before seed maturity to fix nitrogen but before decay makes it plant-unusable

nodes.name: Guano
nodes.note: Soluble enough to leach in rain, requiring application in late spring with incorporation, not spreading months ahead

nodes.name: Harrow
nodes.note: Pre-dates heavy machinery but the tine geometry and angle of attack matter for heavy clay

nodes.name: Herd book
nodes.note: Progeny performance, not body scores, is what a herd book records to identify prepotent sires

nodes.name: Hopping
nodes.note: Alpha acid isomerisation by boil time, late additions for aroma - extraction curves that changed brewing

nodes.name: Horse hoe
nodes.note: The wheel-guided design with depth control that lets one person steer the hoe between rows at the right depth

nodes.name: Hybrid maize
nodes.note: The discovery that yield doubles across the board because hybrid plants show superior root and kernel density

nodes.name: Hybridisation
nodes.note: The inbreeding of pure lines to extinction and then the crossing that resurrects vigour through heterozygosis

nodes.name: The hydrometer
nodes.note: The alcohol yield calculation from gravity drop and the fermentation stop point you can read precisely

nodes.name: Layering
nodes.note: Moss-wrapping or soil-mounding that maintains moisture while roots form in 1-2 seasons

nodes.name: Lead arsenate
nodes.note: Insoluble so it clings to leaves without running off rain; concern about residue on harvested fruit emerges late

nodes.name: Lime sulphur
nodes.note: The boiling time that converts sulfur to polysulphide and the heat stability on cold mornings

nodes.name: Liming
nodes.note: Knowledge that clay binds up phosphorus and lime unlocks it, plus calculation of dose per acre-inch depth

nodes.name: Maize from the New World
nodes.note: Flint varieties travelled farther north than dent varieties; indigenous varieties per region arose within decades

nodes.name: Malting
nodes.note: Enzyme activation by moisture and temperature, then kiln-drying to halt germination at the right time

nodes.name: Marling
nodes.note: The recognition that marl beds contain both lime and clay that improve different defects simultaneously

nodes.name: Mashing
nodes.note: Temperature holds and rests that allow amylase and protease to complete hydrolysis without denaturing

nodes.name: Milking machine
nodes.note: The pulsation cycle that prevents sphincter closure, and rubber teat cups that don't lacerate

nodes.name: Mower
nodes.note: The sickle action copied from grain reaping but adapted for the softer stems and different height of hay

nodes.name: Nicotine as pesticide
nodes.note: Extracted from tobacco waste and sulphate salt for solubility; neurotoxin that works on insects before mammals notice

nodes.name: Nitrite curing
nodes.note: Nitrous acid formation and its bacteriostatic action; N-nitrosamine formation during storage is carcinogenic

nodes.name: The nitrogen cycle as knowledge
nodes.note: The distinction between nitrogen already in manure versus nitrogen fixed from air, explaining why legumes restore soil

nodes.name: Norfolk four-course rotation
nodes.note: The insight that turnips fed to stalled cattle in winter meant no fallow was needed, so four crops per four years beats three

nodes.name: Oil pressing
nodes.note: Cold press preserves flavour but hot press from preheated seeds extracts more oil at cost of quality

nodes.name: Pasteurisation
nodes.note: Temperature-time curves for pathogens versus spores; cooled rapidly to limit cooked flavour

nodes.name: Plant quarantine
nodes.note: The isolation period that allows disease symptoms to manifest and the inspection criteria that catch pests

nodes.name: Pot still distillation
nodes.note: Copper construction prevents sulphide buildup; distiller skill is in heads-hearts-tails cut timing

nodes.name: Potash
nodes.note: The dose-response curve showing modest rates boost yield but excessive rates cause soil salinisation

nodes.name: Potato lifter
nodes.note: The tine spacing and angle that lifts potatoes and shakes soil without burying them again

nodes.name: Potato from the New World
nodes.note: One successful voyage and it propagates forever via tubers; varieties diverge by latitude and day length

nodes.name: Power take-off shaft
nodes.note: The universal joint coupling that lets the shaft angle without binding, the clutch that disengages without stopping the engine

nodes.name: Progeny testing
nodes.note: A bull can appear muscular but produce weak calves; progeny testing separates appearance from breeding value

nodes.name: Pure line selection
nodes.note: The counterintuitive insight that inbreeding purifies traits and makes them transmissible even as vigour drops

nodes.name: The purifier
nodes.note: Tapers in the air chamber that separate by density without leaving flour dust in the exhaust

nodes.name: Pyrethrum
nodes.note: Grown in highlands and dried for extract; rapidly degraded in sunlight so evening spray timing matters

nodes.name: Reaper
nodes.note: The eccentric cam driving the sickle bar at the right frequency and the gathering platform timing, not just a rotating blade

nodes.name: Reaper-binder
nodes.note: The knotter mechanism that wraps and ties twine at speed without human hands, the crux of the patent

nodes.name: Record-keeping and breeding selection
nodes.note: The disciplines of isolating traits, preventing cross-pollination from other varieties, and multi-year observation

nodes.name: Refrigerated ship
nodes.note: Engine-driven compressor that maintains holds at -15C during weeks at sea; odour and cross-contamination problems

nodes.name: Refrigeration - ice trade
nodes.note: Sawing, stacking with sawdust insulation, transport timing that prevents melt before delivery

nodes.name: The resistant variety
nodes.note: The test crosses that confirm resistance is stable, and resistance-breaking mutant pests that emerge within years

nodes.name: The retort
nodes.note: Temperature logging to confirm adequate heat penetration to the can centre, pressure gauge accuracy

nodes.name: Rhizobia and legume nodulation
nodes.note: The observation that nodules appear only on legumes, contain bacteria, and contain fixed nitrogen not atmospheric

nodes.name: Ridging plough
nodes.note: The symmetrical double-board design that builds ridges for root crops

nodes.name: Roller
nodes.note: Weight and bearing design determine how much clod-breaking it achieves without crushing the soil

nodes.name: Roller milling
nodes.note: Multiple roller pairs at increasing pressure produce granulated flour in a single pass without reheating

nodes.name: Root cutter
nodes.note: The blade angle and spacing that produces small chips without clogging or requiring hand-feeding

nodes.name: Rootstocks as knowledge
nodes.note: The phenotypic differences between rootstock types that a grower can match to field conditions and desired tree size

nodes.name: Seed certification
nodes.note: The standard germination test and the genetic purity test that confirm seed meets specifications before sale

nodes.name: Seed drill
nodes.note: Not just broadcasting but timed metering per revolution, spacing seed 4-6 inches in straight rows at depth

nodes.name: The seed trade
nodes.note: The isolation fields that prevent cross-pollination, the testing plots that verify purity before sale

nodes.name: Sheep dip
nodes.note: Temperature, immersion duration, and replenishment frequency that kill parasites without poisoning wool

nodes.name: Silage and the silo
nodes.note: Lactobacillus fermentation that produces lactic acid; pH drop halts spoilage at 3.8-4.0 in 3-6 weeks

nodes.name: Soil testing
nodes.note: Gravimetric nitrogen determination and acid-extraction phosphate giving farmers concrete data instead of guesswork

nodes.name: The sprayer
nodes.note: Nozzle geometry and pressure that produce droplet size fine enough to coat leaves without dripping waste

nodes.name: Subsoiler
nodes.note: The innovation is running deep without a mould-board, shattering without inversion

nodes.name: Cane and beet sugar refining
nodes.note: Multiple crystallisations from A, B, C molasses requiring skill in grain size and temperature management

nodes.name: Sugar cultivation after voyage
nodes.note: Once a few cuttings establish, perpetual harvest with harvest planning and burn timing to prevent disease

nodes.name: Superphosphate
nodes.note: The acid digestion that solubilises phosphorus years ahead of bone meal, yielding 15-20% phosphate instead of 3%

nodes.name: Tea cultivation after voyage
nodes.note: Tea requires high altitude, shade trees, and careful plucking timing; four years to first harvest after planting

nodes.name: Tedder
nodes.note: The timing of tine speed to forward motion so hay is tossed upward and backward evenly

nodes.name: Terracing
nodes.note: The crucial detail is the slight inward slope that keeps water on the bench instead of running off the outer edge

nodes.name: Three-point linkage
nodes.note: The lower-link depth control that automatically adjusts based on soil resistance, freeing the driver to steer

nodes.name: Threshing machine
nodes.note: The drum-concave spacing and surface texture that strikes hard enough to separate grain but gentle enough not to crack seeds

nodes.name: Tile drainage
nodes.note: The layout pattern of mains and laterals, the gradient calculation, and the filter cloth to prevent silting

nodes.name: Steam tractor
nodes.note: The compound cylinder efficiency and the differential gear that lets rear wheels turn at different speeds on curves

nodes.name: Cattle tuberculin test
nodes.note: The Mantoux reaction size threshold that distinguishes sensitised from non-sensitised animals

nodes.name: Urea as fertiliser
nodes.note: The first fertiliser that is pure chemical rather than a byproduct or mined mineral, concentrated and easily stored

nodes.name: Vacuum pan for sugar
nodes.note: Vacuum reduces boiling point; precise temperature and duration that makes small crystals without burning sugar

nodes.name: Veterinary vaccination
nodes.note: Rinderpest vaccine and foot-and-mouth challenge - which diseases are vaccinated determines flock health risk

nodes.name: The Wardian case
nodes.note: The sealed ecosystem that recycles condensation, keeping tropical cuttings alive for months at sea

nodes.name: White flour and vitamin loss
nodes.note: The discovery correlating white bread dominance with beriberi and pellagra epidemics in refined-grain populations

nodes.name: Winnower
nodes.note: The air velocity and direction relative to grain size and density that separates good grain from light chaff

nodes.name: Yeast culture
nodes.note: Pure culture ferments faster, cleaner flavour, lower acetobacter infection rate, consistent results

nodes.name: Aerial bombing
nodes.note: Drop bombs from an aircraft onto targets below. Early bombs were heavy artillery shells with impact fuses. Later, purpose-designed bombs with light cases and heavy charges. Extremely dangerous for the pilot (instability, wind drift, primitive aiming). Devastatingly effective against stationary targets. The State will demand this.

nodes.name: Aerial photography
nodes.note: Mount a camera on an aircraft and photograph the ground below. Vertical photographs from height show cities, fields, fortifications with complete clarity and no perspective distortion. Absolutely invaluable for military reconnaissance and mapping. The camera must be light and the aircraft must be stable.

nodes.name: Aerial reconnaissance
nodes.note: An aircraft with a trained observer flies over enemy territory, notes positions of troops and defenses, and reports back. The observer is fast, covering in hours what a scout takes weeks to do. The State will fund this immediately. Requires pilot and observer to work in concert and to return safely.

nodes.name: Aerodrome (landing field)
nodes.note: An open field of level ground, grass or gravel, at least 500 meters long and 100 meters wide. Aircraft need room to take off into wind and to land without hitting obstacles. A brick or gravel surface prevents mud. Early aerodromes were called flying grounds. They must be maintained and guarded.

nodes.name: Cambered aerofoil section
nodes.note: Cayley's central discovery: a curved (cambered) plate lifts far better than a flat plate at the same angle of attack. The reason is non-obvious and requires experiment: curved surfaces create lower pressure on the back side. A wing with a cambered section can generate substantial lift at shallow angles. This is not merely a geometry trick; it is the foundation of mechanical flight. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.] [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Aileron for roll control
nodes.note: Small hinged surfaces at the wing trailing edge, operated by pilot cables. When one goes up, the other goes down, creating differential lift without twisting the main wing. Simpler than warping and less stressful on structure. The aileron is a later refinement, but does the same job. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Airspeed indicator
nodes.note: A pitot tube measures dynamic pressure, which is velocity squared. Display it on a dial. A pilot cannot fly safely by feel; speed is invisible. This is the most important instrument. Early versions used a simple gauge; later ones an anemometer-style rotor. Without it, powered flight is nearly impossible. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Altimeter (aneroid barometer)
nodes.note: An aneroid capsule responds to atmospheric pressure. As altitude increases, pressure drops, the capsule expands slightly, and a mechanical linkage moves a dial. Needs to be calibrated carefully and compensated for temperature. Essential for instrument flying; a pilot cannot judge altitude reliably by eye.

nodes.name: Artificial horizon (gyroscopic)
nodes.note: A rapidly spinning gyroscope maintains its orientation regardless of aircraft motion. Mount a ball or card inside the gyroscope's frame so the pilot sees whether wings are level and nose is up or down. Requires extreme precision in bearing design and high spin speeds. Essential for flying through clouds or darkness.

nodes.name: Autogyro (powered rotor-wing)
nodes.note: A propeller on the nose for forward thrust, and a rotor overhead spinning freely (autogiro: self-turning). As the aircraft moves forward, air flowing through the rotor keeps it spinning, generating lift. Simpler than a helicopter because the rotor needs no engine drive, only control linkages. Can take off and land in short distances. Invented much later than the helicopter.

nodes.name: Ballast and descent control
nodes.note: A balloon achieves altitude by dropping sand ballast and descends by venting gas. These are its only two controls. Altitude is controlled by these two levers exclusively. A ballast bag with a line to the basket lets the aeronaut modulate buoyancy by hand.

nodes.name: Balloon valve
nodes.note: A rope-pulled valve at the balloon's crown vents gas, allowing descent. Without it, a free balloon cannot descend safely. The valve must be airtight when closed but operate smoothly when pulled. A cone of leather over an iron frame, sealing under the weight of gas, is the only control a balloon has besides dropping ballast.

nodes.name: Biplane structure
nodes.note: Two main lifting surfaces separated vertically, braced together with struts and wire cables. This is strong, stiff, and light. All early aircraft were biplanes because they could be built from wood and wire. Drag is slightly higher than a monoplane, but the structural advantage is decisive when materials are weak. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Separation of forces: lift, drag, thrust, control
nodes.note: Cayley's single most important insight: lift and drag are separate. To fly, you need lift enough to equal weight, drag small enough that power can overcome it, thrust strong enough to overcome drag and accelerate, and control to direct the craft. These four are independent problems. Before Cayley, people treated flying as one vague problem. After him, it became engineering. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Coal gas for ballooning
nodes.note: Destructive distillation of coal produces a mixture rich in hydrogen and methane: coal gas. Vastly cheaper than chemical hydrogen. A coal-gas plant can fill balloons continuously. Requires establishing a permanent retort house and managing by-products. The lift is slightly less than pure hydrogen but the cost difference is transformative. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Compass for navigation
nodes.note: A magnetized iron needle on a silk thread points north. Rome has this. A compass in an aircraft allows navigation when landmarks are obscured. Mount it in a card marked with degrees.

nodes.name: Mounted engine under balloon
nodes.note: Suspend a small petrol engine and propeller in a wooden framework below an elongated envelope. The propeller drives air backward, creating thrust. The envelope provides lift. Requires a very light engine relative to power output and extreme care in weight balance. This is a dirigible, controllable by the pilot.

nodes.name: Elevator for pitch control
nodes.note: A hinged horizontal surface at the tail. When deflected up, the tail rises, and the nose drops. Down elevator raises the nose. This control pitch. It is the most critical: pitch controls altitude, and loss of pitch control is fatal in seconds.

nodes.name: Elongated balloon envelope
nodes.note: Instead of a sphere, make the envelope elongated, pointed at both ends. This shape reduces drag hugely when the balloon drifts. The envelope must still be sealed and symmetrical. This is the form needed for a dirigible: long, narrow, and pointed. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Flying boat
nodes.note: An aircraft whose fuselage is a boat hull. No need for an aerodrome; water launches are smooth and the hull provides flotation. Useful for long-range reconnaissance and transport. Requires excellent hydrodynamic design to minimize drag on the step and excellent corrosion control.

nodes.name: Simple glider
nodes.note: Build a wooden frame, cover with linen, add cambered wings and a tail. Tow it behind a horse or launch it downhill. It will glide and may kill the pilot if control is lost. But gliding flight teaches you what lift feels like, what turns require, and most importantly, what happens when you lose control. This is the cheap school, conducted at non-fatal altitudes.

nodes.name: Goldbeater's skin envelope
nodes.note: Goldbeater's skin, the cleaned intestine of oxen, is the best gas-tight material known. Thin, tough, airtight when sealed with alum and honey. Costs vastly more than linen but holds hydrogen. No rubber exists. This is the single choice for long-endurance gas bags.

nodes.name: Helicopter rotor system
nodes.note: Two or more large aerofoil blades rotating at high speed about a vertical axis. The blades generate lift and must be able to change pitch to control thrust direction. This is mechanically complex and unstable without careful design. A helicopter can hover and land vertically, but is harder to fly than an airplane.

nodes.name: hot_air_balloon
nodes.note: Reference technology already in vocabulary. Hot air balloon relies on density difference: warm air inside the envelope is lighter than ambient air. Foundation for all free balloons.

nodes.name: Hydrogen safety limits
nodes.note: Hydrogen is extraordinarily buoyant but ignites violently with air. A spark, a flame, static electricity, or friction will ignite any mixture between 4 percent and 75 percent hydrogen in air. This is not anecdotal: it is absolute chemistry. You cannot escape it by procedure; you mitigate by isolation (no open flames, grounding, no sparking equipment) and by accept that the risk is real and permanent. Helium does not exist. Coal gas is safer by dilution. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Hydrogen from iron and acid
nodes.note: Dilute sulfuric acid (from distillation) reacts with iron to produce hydrogen gas. Must be generated in sealed vessels with a tube fed to the envelope. Dangerous: hydrogen ignites explosively in air. Filling a balloon takes hours. This is the reliable source until coal gas is available. Rate is limited by acid strength and temperature control. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Jet engine (centrifugal compressor)
nodes.note: A centrifugal compressor spins at thousands of rpm, sucking air in at the center and throwing it outward into a combustion chamber. The challenge is not compression but surviving high temperature. Combustion temperatures are 1000C+, and metal strength drops catastrophically above 600C. Nickel alloys are essential. Even then, turbine blades fail unless cooled internally.

nodes.name: Jet engine principle
nodes.note: Newton's third law: jet out the back, thrust forward. A compressor forces air in, fuel burns in a combustion chamber, hot gas expands and exits at high velocity. No piston engine, no propeller. Much simpler mechanically than reciprocating engines but requires materials that survive continuous high temperature under pressure. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.] [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_1600 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: combustion chamber operates at sustained 1600+ C, requires regenerative furnace scale heat]

nodes.name: Kite
nodes.note: A framed silk or linen panel tied to cordage is humanity's first controlled aerofoil. Rome has all materials. The curved bow of a framed kite's sides produces lift from asymmetric air flow; this was never trivial to understand. Kites serve tethered observation, signalling and scientific experiment.

nodes.name: Light petrol engine
nodes.note: An aircraft engine must deliver high power per kilogram. This requires aluminium alloys for the crankcase, fine tolerances for bearings and pistons, and very high speeds (1000 rpm+). A typical aero engine in 1910 delivered 10-30 horsepower at 200 kg. This is a metallurgy and precision problem first, a thermodynamics problem second. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Monoplane cantilever wing
nodes.note: One wing, supported only at the fuselage, with no external bracing. This requires a wing strong enough to cantilever its own load in bending. Needs steel or aluminium spars and good materials science to avoid failure. Much less drag than biplane, but much more demanding structurally. Not practical until materials improve. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Tethered observation balloon
nodes.note: A single large envelope of stitched linen or silk, sealed with beeswax, displaces enough warm air to lift a man. Must be tethered to cordage or risk becoming uncontrolled. The State values this for reconnaissance, signalling and military observation. A man in the sky appears miraculous; mitigation is training and controlled small-scale trials, not secrecy.

nodes.name: Parachute
nodes.note: A cone of stiff linen attached to a harness. When opened in free fall, it spreads and catches air, slowing descent to survivable speeds. Requires both invention and extraordinary nerve to test. A man who falls from the sky with a cloth and lives appears either blessed or damned. The key insight is that air resistance, not upward force, saves you. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Pitot tube
nodes.note: A simple tube with an opening into the airstream and a side port. Dynamic pressure at the front is higher than static pressure at the side. The difference is proportional to velocity squared. This is purely fluid statics, not magic. [FIXED after independent audit: tier raised to match its barometer dependency.] [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Power-to-weight ratio and flight
nodes.note: A powered airplane needs enough power to overcome drag at the speed where wings produce lift sufficient for the weight. This requires roughly 5 to 10 kg of aircraft per horsepower. Achieving this needs an engine weighing very little per horsepower and an airframe weighing little. Both are metallurgy and precision problems, not power problems. Weak engines cannot overcome this limit regardless of design. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Powered aeroplane
nodes.note: An aircraft with engine and propeller that achieves sustained powered flight. Requires cambered wings tested in a wind tunnel, three-axis control, a light high-revving engine, and a structure so light it feels built from nothing. Testing kills the pilot. Only possible if all prerequisites are honest. The Wright brothers succeeded because they honored this checklist.

nodes.name: Propeller as rotating aerofoil
nodes.note: A propeller is not a screw pushing against air like a screw in water. It is a rotating wing. Each blade is an aerofoil twisted to increasing angle as you go outward. It generates lift in a rotating plane, and that lift acts as thrust. Design requires aerofoil theory and matching pitch to engine speed. Inefficiency at the tips limits diameter. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Radial engine
nodes.note: Cylinders arranged radially around a central crankshaft. Air cooling is excellent, and the engine is compact. Most effective for aircraft because the short length and small diameter reduce drag. Requires precise balancing and very strong crankshafts to handle the unbalanced forces. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Rigid airship frame
nodes.note: Instead of one envelope, build a rigid skeleton of wooden rings and longerons, then cover with fabric and fill with gas. This allows huge structures and multiple gas cells for safety. Requires aluminium or steel girders to keep weight manageable. The Zeppelin approach: rigid frame, gasbags inside, and structural load is borne by the frame, not the envelope.

nodes.name: Rotary engine
nodes.note: The entire engine block rotates with the propeller while the crankshaft stays fixed. The piston heads are cooled by rotation. High power at low weight. Much more complex than radial but delivers slightly better power. Used extensively in WWI aircraft. Requires very careful design to handle gyroscopic forces. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Rudder for yaw control
nodes.note: A hinged vertical fin at the tail. When deflected, it yaws the aircraft left or right. Essential for turning when wing warping or ailerons are used. Without it, the aircraft will slip sideways during a turn.

nodes.name: Stressed-skin fuselage
nodes.note: Instead of a skeleton covered with skin, build the skin to carry bending loads. Aluminium sheet riveted to aluminium frames creates a strong, light, rigid structure. Requires precision sheet-metal work and tens of thousands of rivets. The monocoque: a form where the outer surface is the structure. This is how modern aircraft are built. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Three-axis control: roll, pitch, yaw
nodes.note: The pilot must control three independent axes: roll (banking), pitch (nose up or down), and yaw (turning). Roll is achieved by wing warping or ailerons, pitch by elevator, yaw by rudder. A glider without all three controls is uncontrollable. Testing this kills people. But the Wright brothers realized that CONTROL, not lift or power, was the missing piece.

nodes.name: Varnished silk envelope
nodes.note: Multiple coats of shellac varnish on silk create an airtight seam-sealed envelope. Much cheaper than goldbeater's skin, almost as airtight. Handles thermal stress better than intestine. This is the practical choice for large balloons when cost matters.

nodes.name: Wind tunnel for lift and drag measurement
nodes.note: A wooden box with a powerful fan at one end and a test section. Measurement is done with a water manometer: a bent tube of glass half-filled with water, showing pressure difference as height difference. You can test aerofoil shapes, measure lift and drag without dying. This is the tool that transforms flight from experiment to engineering. Build it first, use it to learn, then design based on data.

nodes.name: Wing warping
nodes.note: Twist the entire wing by pulling cables to alter the angle of attack at wing tips. This causes differential lift and forces the aircraft to roll. No moving surfaces are needed; the wing itself twists. This is elegant and strong, but requires great care in cable routing and tensioning. The Wright brothers used this. It works. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Symbolic algebra and equation notation
nodes.note: Diophantus is c. 250 AD and syncopated; you are jumping 1400 years to Viete and Descartes.

nodes.name: Gravimetric and volumetric analysis
nodes.note: Not optional and not glamorous. Without quantitative analysis every process in your programme is a folk recipe that degrades with each retelling. This node is what makes the corpus reproducible by people you never met. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. nodes.note: Temperatures no fuel-fired furnace reaches. nodes.name: Decimal positional notation, zero, negative numbers, decimal fractions
nodes.note: Highest return on personal hours in the entire tree. Frame as recovered from Indian sources, which is even true. Sell it to bankers and the fiscus first; they will adopt it for self-interest and carry it for you.

nodes.name: Six months of listening before you act
nodes.note: OPTIONAL, and no longer a prerequisite for anything. It buys you accurate local prices, the actual law of this province, who is who, and a large reduction in early blunder risk. Skip it if you want to move fast and find out the hard way what things cost. The simulator lets you skip it, because a model that forces the cautious opening is not a model, it is an opinion.

nodes.name: Atoms, elements, atomic weights, stoichiometry, the periodic table
nodes.note: You can write the periodic table from memory on day one. It is worth roughly 150 years of chemistry. It only becomes operational once you have the analytical balance, so write it early and prove it later.

nodes.name: Analytical balance reading to 1 milligram
nodes.note: Agate or hardened steel knife edges, a beam stiff enough not to sag, damping, a draught shield, and a master weight set. This is the instrument that converts alchemy into chemistry. Nothing downstream is reproducible without it. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. nodes.note: The Torricellian space above the column is free vacuum and it will shock every philosopher in the Empire, because Aristotle says it cannot exist. nodes.note: The single highest-leverage mechanical change available to Roman metallurgy. Continuous high-volume blast is what separates a bloomery from a blast furnace. nodes.name: Cylinder boring mill
nodes.note: Wilkinson's machine, and the actual reason there was no useful steam engine before 1775. The bar must be supported at both ends so it cannot follow the existing crooked hole. Without this there is no piston that seals, and without that there is no engine. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um added by a reviewer working node by node. nodes.name: Differential and integral calculus
nodes.note: Archimedes' method of exhaustion is the nearest Roman-available foundation, and it is a good one. Present as completing Archimedes.

nodes.name: Camera obscura with lens
nodes.note: Immediate cultural value as a drawing and surveying aid, and it teaches optics to your students far faster than argument. Alhazen is 900 years away and the principle is already latent in Aristotle's pinhole observations.

nodes.name: Oxygen and hydrogen in quantity
nodes.note: Gate on the oxy-hydrogen flame, fused quartz, balloons, and the hydrogen reduction of germanium oxide.

nodes.name: Sustained 700 C (pottery kiln)
nodes.note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS. Updraught pottery kiln, wood fired. Free starting capability. Glazes, bricks, lime, glass working.

nodes.name: Sustained 1100 C (hand-blown charcoal)
nodes.note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS. Bloomery iron, bronze casting, glass melting. A man on a bellows tops out near here. Everything above this rung needs a machine.

nodes.name: Sustained 1300 C (water-blown continuous blast)
nodes.note: Liquid cast iron lives here. The jump from 1100 to 1300 is not more fuel, it is more AIR, continuously. This single rung is the difference between a bloomery civilisation and a foundry civilisation.

nodes.name: Sustained 1600 C (regenerative preheat)
nodes.note: Siemens regenerative preheat recycles flue heat into the incoming air. Crucible steel, open hearth, porcelain. You cannot get here by burning more charcoal; you must recycle the heat you are already throwing away.

nodes.name: 2000 C localised (oxy-hydrogen blowpipe)
nodes.note: A flame, not a furnace: small volume only. Fused quartz working, platinum melting, lime light.

nodes.name: 3000 C+ (electric arc / resistance)
nodes.note: No chemical flame reaches here. Calcium carbide, ferroalloys, tungsten, artificial graphite, synthetic corundum.

nodes.name: Absolute electrical units
nodes.note: A coil of known geometry and the Earth's field give absolute current with no calibrated instrument to start from. This is how the electrical metrology bootstrap escapes its own circularity.

nodes.name: Reproducible length standard
nodes.note: Master bars in bronze, in triplicate, in three cities. Without this nothing you write down survives you.

nodes.name: Interferometric length (wavelengths of light)
nodes.note: Length measured against a physical constant instead of a bar of metal.

nodes.name: Mass to 1 milligram
nodes.note: Agate knife edges. The instrument that turns alchemy into chemistry.

nodes.name: Temperature to a few degrees (liquid in glass)
nodes.note: Fixed points at melting ice and boiling water. Without a repeatable scale no thermal recipe can be transmitted to anyone not standing beside you.

nodes.name: High temperature (clay contraction and colour pyrometry)
nodes.note: Wedgwood-style contraction pyrometer plus a calibrated colour scale. You cannot control a furnace whose temperature you cannot read.

nodes.name: Time to the millisecond (chronograph, tuning fork)
nodes.note: Ballistics, engine indicating, telegraphy.

nodes.name: Time to the second (pendulum)
nodes.note: Navigation, physics, and later every electrical measurement.

nodes.name: Local electric power, kW scale
nodes.note: One dynamo on the millpond shaft you already built. Enough for arc lights, electroplating, a laboratory.

nodes.name: Grid electric power, MW scale
nodes.note: The precondition for every energy-intensive process: arc furnaces, electrolysis, aluminium, and the sustained laboratory power a purity programme eats.

nodes.name: Muscle and animal power
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. A man sustains roughly 75 W; an ox perhaps 400 W. Free, and the reason Roman industry is shaped the way it is.

nodes.name: Steam power, portable, hundreds of kW
nodes.note: Power where there is no river. Until you need that, water is cheaper and needs a far shorter prerequisite chain.

nodes.name: Water power, tens of kW on one shaft
nodes.note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS and barely uses it for anything but grinding grain. Barbegal runs 16 overshot wheels. The technology gap is imagination, not engineering.

nodes.name: Purity 99% (careful classical refining)
nodes.note: Cupellation, fire refining, recrystallisation. Rome nearly reaches this for silver and gold already.

nodes.name: Purity 99.99% (electrorefining, fractional crystallisation)
nodes.note: You cannot claim a purity you cannot measure, so this rung is gated on quantitative analysis as much as on process.

nodes.name: Purity 99.9999% (fractional distillation of volatile compounds)
nodes.note: Purify the COMPOUND, not the element. Germanium tetrachloride boils at 86 C and fractionates like brandy; germanium metal does not.

nodes.name: Purity 1 part in 1e9 (zone refining)
nodes.note: No chemistry reaches here. A travelling molten zone sweeps impurities to one end because most are more soluble in liquid than in solid. This one trick is what makes semiconductors possible at all.

nodes.name: Tolerance 0.1 micron (interferometric)
nodes.note: Measured in wavelengths of light. Optical surfaces, diffraction gratings, semiconductor lithography much later.

nodes.name: Tolerance 0.1 mm (file, scraper, gauge)
nodes.note: Needs a reference plane to scrape against and a gauge to check with. Clock wheels, lock work, decent screw threads.

nodes.name: Tolerance 0.01 mm (slide rest, lead screw, micrometer)
nodes.note: Take the tool out of the operator's hand and accuracy stops depending on his wrist. Steam pistons, interchangeable parts, precision instruments.

nodes.name: Tolerance 1 mm (skilled hand craft)
nodes.note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS, and is very good at it. Carpentry, masonry, bronze casting, the Antikythera gearwork. Free.

nodes.name: Tolerance 1 micron (lapping, grinding, optical flats)
nodes.note: Lapping with loose abrasive plus interference fringes to check. Gauge blocks, ball bearings, lens moulds, injector nozzles.

nodes.name: High vacuum, about 1e-3 torr (Sprengel mercury drop)
nodes.note: THE cheap shortcut. Falling mercury drops each trap a slug of gas and carry it out. No pistons, no seals, no tolerances. Incandescent lamps and discharge tubes live here.

nodes.name: Very high vacuum, 1e-6 torr (diffusion pump plus getters)
nodes.note: Needs a motor for the backing pump. Vacuum tubes, X-ray tubes, evaporated coatings.

nodes.name: Ultra high vacuum, 1e-9 torr (bakeable metal systems)
nodes.note: Metal gaskets, bakeout, ion pumps. Surface science and semiconductor processing.

nodes.name: Rough vacuum, about 1 torr (piston pump)
nodes.note: A leather-sealed piston pump. Barometry, the Magdeburg demonstration, condensers. Not enough for any electron device.

nodes.name: Systematic case hardening, quenching and tempering
nodes.note: Roman smiths do all of this already but inconsistently and without a temperature scale. Give them temper colours on polished steel as a repeatable index and the reject rate collapses. Cheap, immediate, militarily valuable, entirely unmagical. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.note: Bar iron packed in charcoal in a sealed chest, held at roughly 1000 C for days. Carbon diffuses in slowly, on the order of millimetres per day, so use thin bars. Consistent steel in quantity for the first time. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_1100 added by a reviewer working node by node.
