nodes.note: AC welding problematic due to arc extinction each half-cycle; carbon electrode leaves residue; metal electrode suited to steel joining. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Band-pass and notch filters tuned rejection
nodes.note: Bandwidth depends on Q of tuned circuit; notch depth limited by element losses; used for interference rejection in radio.

nodes.name: Beam tetrode output tube high power
nodes.note: High efficiency suitable for RF and audio final stage; parasitic oscillations at high frequency; requires careful circuit design. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: AC impedance bridge and LCR bridge
nodes.note: Accuracy depends on standard elements; frequency dependent; Q measurement by additional measurement or by ratio of R and L.

nodes.name: Electrolytic capacitor aluminium
nodes.note: Oxide thickness controls voltage rating; only works in one polarity; sensitive to temperature and overvolts; vastly higher C/V than paper capacitors. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Fixed mica capacitor
nodes.note: Mica splits into thin sheets cleanly; stable temperature coefficient; suitable for RF and timing circuits.

nodes.name: Fixed paper capacitor
nodes.note: Oil impregnation lowers losses and increases voltage rating; absorbs water readily so must be sealed; cheap at scale.

nodes.name: Variable air-gap capacitor
nodes.note: Arc-free air dielectric; tuning smooth and reversible; stray inductance from leads limits RF performance.

nodes.name: Cathode ray oscilloscope CRO
nodes.note: First practical CRO circa 1930s; sweep generator must have linear time base; persistence of phosphor crucial for observation.

nodes.name: Magnetic circuit breaker fast trip
nodes.note: Can be combined with thermal for dual protection; must dissipate solenoid heat continuously; coordination between devices essential.

nodes.name: Thermal circuit breaker
nodes.note: Time-current characteristic depends on heater coil; not fast; reset after cooling; can be overridden by sustained high current.

nodes.name: Industrial contactor and motor starter
nodes.note: Arc chute prevents sustained arc; overload heater coil; three-phase main contacts plus auxiliary; frame standardization aids design.

nodes.name: Counter frequency division and binary scaling
nodes.note: Used in frequency meters and timers; ripple counter has propagation delay; synchronous counter uses common clock.

nodes.name: Detector and demodulation envelope and product detection
nodes.note: Rectifier bias sets detection point; high load resistance needed for AM; product detection with local oscillator restores suppressed carrier.

nodes.name: Dielectric heating capacitor field
nodes.note: Uniform heating without contact; suitable for plastics and wood; frequency typically 5-50 MHz; capacitor loss must be managed. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Diode thermionic tube rectifier
nodes.note: Soft vacuum has gas ionisation current; hard vacuum preferred; anode heat limits rectification current; used in high-frequency radio reception. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Discriminator and FM demodulation
nodes.note: S-curve characteristic; slope at center provides deviation sensitivity; FM less noise-prone than AM for same bandwidth.

nodes.name: Compound-wound dynamo self-regulating
nodes.note: Over-compound raises voltage with load; under-compound drops voltage; exact balance requires field connection points adjustment.

nodes.name: Series-wound dynamo generator
nodes.note: Voltage rises with load if load resistance drops; dangerous behavior if load suddenly disconnected; stabilised by armature reaction.

nodes.name: Shunt-wound dynamo generator
nodes.note: Self-exciting; voltage drops with load; external load variation affects output; inherently stable at constant speed.

nodes.name: Earthing and grounding electrode system
nodes.note: Resistance depends on soil conductivity and electrode depth; seasonal variation significant; multiple electrodes reduce impedance. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electric handheld drill and motor
nodes.note: Speed varies with line voltage; brush wear limits life; rechargeable batteries later replace cord power; torque reaction requires two hands. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electric lift motor and gear reduction
nodes.note: Brake holds car at floors; motor starting torque must be limited; governors prevent overspeed; safety switches on all gates. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electric locomotive and traction motor
nodes.note: Regenerative braking possible with proper control; efficiency high compared to diesel; requires substantial electrical infrastructure. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electron microscope electromagnetic lens
nodes.note: Resolution limited by electron wavelength; lens aberrations substantial; requires very high vacuum and stability; used from late 1930s. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electroplating and electrorefining coating
nodes.note: Overvoltage for hydrogen evolution must be prevented; bath agitation improves uniformity; purity of plating metal depends on anode dissolution. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electropolishing etching and surface finish
nodes.note: Polishing action depends on electrolyte composition; mass transport controls smoothness; passivation layer prevents further attack at end. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electrostatic precipitation and dust collection
nodes.note: Corona discharge maintains ionisation; collecting electrode rapped to dislodge dust; very high efficiency; secondary effects on emissions. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Flip-flop latch and binary memory element
nodes.note: SR and JK flip-flops used for sequential logic; race conditions when setting and resetting simultaneously; trigger must be brief.

nodes.name: Fuse and wire element cartridge
nodes.note: Melt point set by wire diameter and alloy; cartridge design isolates arc; single-use requires replacement; cost nearly zero.

nodes.name: Ballistic galvanometer pulse integration
nodes.note: Must measure total swing angle; temperature coefficient of spring critical; used to measure transformer turns ratio and core losses.

nodes.name: Impedance matching transformer and L-network
nodes.note: Bandwidth limited for transformer; L-network single frequency; Smith chart aids design; unnecessary if source and load both 50 ohm.

nodes.name: Induction heating and inductive coupling
nodes.note: Frequency determines coupling and penetration depth; high frequency shallow, low frequency deep; no direct contact between heater and load.

nodes.name: Squirrel-cage induction motor
nodes.note: Torque from electromagnetic induction in rotor; starting current high; rotor skew reduces cogging torque; slot geometry critical for performance.

nodes.name: Wound-rotor induction motor adjustable speed
nodes.note: Resistor heat at reduced speed; used for high-inertia loads; speed varies with load but controlled resistance keeps current safe.

nodes.name: Air-core inductor coil
nodes.note: Inductance scales as turns squared; skin effect at high frequency; useful where DC or variable core losses unacceptable.

nodes.name: Ferrite and powdered iron core
nodes.note: Ferrite a ceramic; does not conduct eddy currents like iron sheet; high frequency inductor and transformer cores.

nodes.name: Iron-core inductor and choke
nodes.note: Saturation nonlinearity used for current limiting; core loss scales with frequency; permeability much higher than air.

nodes.name: Oil-filled bushing insulator transformer
nodes.note: Stress grading with increasing porcelain thickness reduces field; oil cooling improves thermal rating; must handle thermal cycling without cracking.

nodes.name: Porcelain pin insulator
nodes.note: Creepage distance (surface path) more critical than straight-line distance; pollution tracking and salt spray demand careful glaze design.

nodes.name: Klystron microwave amplifier and oscillator
nodes.note: Tunable by cavity dimensions; very efficient for continuous wave; used in radar transmitters from 1940s. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Lightning arrestor and gap protector
nodes.note: Horn gap spreads arc to cool it; prevents sustained arc-over; must be coordinated with fuse or breaker to isolate line if arc grounds.

nodes.name: Load dispatch center and system scheduling
nodes.note: System frequency is barometer of balance; shortage lowers frequency, surplus raises it; operator must manually adjust generation. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Loudspeaker moving coil magnetic transducer
nodes.note: Impedance matching transformer couples line-level signal to speaker; frequency response limited by cone resonance and suspension compliance.

nodes.name: RC low-pass and high-pass filters
nodes.note: Low-pass blocks high frequencies; high-pass blocks low frequencies; cutoff at -3dB point where reactance equals resistance.

nodes.name: Magnetron high-power microwave oscillator
nodes.note: Compact very high power source; anode cools quickly in pulsed mode; essential for radar; oscillation frequency determined by cavity geometry. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Megger insulation resistance tester
nodes.note: Portable field measurement of cable and winding condition; meter coil shunted by unknown resistance giving logarithmic response.

nodes.name: Electrodynamometer and wattmeter
nodes.note: Accuracy requires coil geometry; temperature drift in springs significant; must measure true power, not volt-amperes. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Energy meter integrating wattmeter
nodes.note: Billing requires reproducible accuracy; must handle leading and lagging power factor; rotor speed calibrated to meter constant.

nodes.name: Moving coil milliammeter and voltmeter
nodes.note: Current through coil creates torque; permanent magnet must be strong; Shunt resistor for ammeter, high series resistor for voltmeter.

nodes.name: Moving iron meter fixed scale
nodes.note: Works on AC and DC; square-law response means scale is crowded at low end; cheaper than moving coil; less sensitive to overload.

nodes.name: Carbon contact microphone transmitter
nodes.note: High acoustic output; requires steady biasing current; output impedance low; used in telephone handsets and early broadcast microphones.

nodes.name: Condenser microphone electrostatic capacitor
nodes.note: Excellent frequency response and low distortion; requires power supply for bias and impedance converter; sensitive to humidity. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Dynamic microphone moving coil induction
nodes.note: Output impedance high; frequency response relatively flat; robust and simple; bidirectional so can be speaker.

nodes.name: Ribbon microphone velocity transducer
nodes.note: Very low output impedance; warm sound prized for vocals; fragile to wind and impact; directional pattern used in studios.

nodes.name: Mixer frequency conversion and translation
nodes.note: Heterodyne conversion; intermediate frequency allows fixed narrowband amplification; mixer loss adds noise figure.

nodes.name: Modulator amplitude frequency and phase modulation
nodes.note: AM needs linear amplification; FM needs frequency-stable oscillator; deviation ratio determines bandwidth.

nodes.name: Rotary converter and synchronous converter AC-DC
nodes.note: Synchronous tie to AC line frequency; commutator ripple frequency same as AC frequency; largely replaced by mercury arc rectifier.

nodes.name: Multivibrator astable and monostable binary circuit
nodes.note: Astable multivibrator: relaxation oscillator; monostable: one stable state, pulse triggered; chain of multivibrators forms binary counter.

nodes.name: Negative feedback and Blacks 1927 theorem
nodes.note: Black's insight 1927: gain with feedback equals open-loop gain divided by (1 + loop gain); distortion reduced by same factor.

nodes.name: Oscillator feedback oscillation and frequency generation
nodes.note: Starting from thermal noise; loop gain must exceed unity; crystal oscillator very stable; LC oscillator easily variable frequency.

nodes.name: Oscillograph string galvanometer pen recorder
nodes.note: DC coupled; bandwidth limited by string inertia; essential for transient and power system measurements; requires continuous paper supply.

nodes.name: Pentode output and RF amplifier tube
nodes.note: Dominant output tube 1930s onwards; low output impedance suitable for audio; good linearity with suppressor biasing. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Photocell vacuum and gas photoelectric tube
nodes.note: Gas-filled faster response but shorter life; vacuum phototubes more stable; used for light measurement and object detection. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Photodiode and photoelectric cell
nodes.note: Used for exposure meters and light measurement; selenium cell slower but more sensitive than copper oxide; no amplification stage. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Photomultiplier single photon detector
nodes.note: Gain millions; extremely sensitive to light; dark current limits sensitivity; useful for weak light detection and scintillation counters. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Portable electrical plug and socket
nodes.note: Keying and grounding contacts critical; contact wear and oxidation cause heating; standardization enables interoperability.

nodes.name: Potentiometer precision voltage divider
nodes.note: Manganin wire has minimal temperature coefficient; screw drive prevents wear on track; enables bridge null detection.

nodes.name: Potentiometer method voltage comparison
nodes.note: No current drawn from unknown source; used to compare EMFs and measure internal resistance; accuracy limited by potentiometer linearity.

nodes.name: Power factor correction and reactive power compensation
nodes.note: Capacitor must be switched in steps to track load; resonance with line inductance dangerous; overshooting power factor wastes power. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Power supply rectification and smoothing
nodes.note: Capacitor input filter: ripple voltage decreases with size; inductor input: smoother initial voltage rise; transformer secondary voltage higher for same DC. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Printed circuit board etched pattern
nodes.note: Etching must be selective and reproducible; copper adhesion critical; allows mass assembly; enables high-density interconnect. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Differential protective relay overcurrent
nodes.note: Requires precise current transformer matching; time-delay prevents transient nuisance trips; restraint coil stabilises for magnetising inrush. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Quartz resonator and filter
nodes.note: Mechanical resonance; Q can exceed 10000; temperature coefficient critical; must be mounted to damp overtones without killing Q.

nodes.name: Radar pulse modulation and detection
nodes.note: Range resolution by pulse width; azimuth by antenna rotation; elevation by antenna tilt; clutter rejection critical; Doppler reveals speed.

nodes.name: Mercury arc rectifier thermionic
nodes.note: Starting requires heated filament or external ignition; arc extinction requires current reversal; phase-shift transformer enables delay control.

nodes.name: Metal layer rectifier selenium or copper oxide
nodes.note: Forward voltage drop higher than tube; efficiency adequate for small rectifiers; stack many discs for high voltage; temperature coefficient positive. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electromagnetic relay switching contacts
nodes.note: Arc damage and pitting of contacts with AC load; silvering extends life; must account for contact resistance in design. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Resistance welding spot and seam fusion
nodes.note: Electrode force and cooling critical; pressure timing and current duration must be coordinated; repeatable and no filler needed.

nodes.name: Carbon composition resistor
nodes.note: Carbon content and binder ratio set resistance; tolerance broader than wirewound but adequate for most circuits.

nodes.name: Wirewound resistor
nodes.note: Precision requires consistent wire diameter and tight winding; achromatic winding balances inductance.

nodes.name: Resonance and Q factor frequency selectivity
nodes.note: Energy storage in L and C reactances Q times energy dissipated per cycle; Q limited by resistance in practical circuits.

nodes.name: Rheostat sliding contact resistor
nodes.note: Current path through coil via moving contact; heating limits power; precision determines smoothness.

nodes.name: Ring main distribution and loop network
nodes.note: Fault location critical; relay must see direction of fault current; current sharing unequal; network analysis complex. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Servo motor with feedback control
nodes.note: Feedback must have minimum lag; damping by proportional term prevents oscillation; used in remote positioning and radar antenna drives.

nodes.name: Sonar acoustic detection and ranging
nodes.note: Frequency 20 kHz to MHz for resolution; attenuation in water limits range; multibeam arrays scan volume; target motion analysis reveals speed.

nodes.name: Weston standard cell voltage reference
nodes.note: Shielded from light and vibration; electrodes in saturated sulfate solution; used to calibrate voltmeters; temperature coefficient -0.0000406V/K.

nodes.name: Standard resistor manganin coil
nodes.note: Calibrated against international standard; typical accuracy 0.01%; stored in constant-temperature enclosure.

nodes.name: Standardised frequency 50 Hz and 60 Hz
nodes.note: Choice was engineering and politics; once locked in, changing impossible without grid shutdown; early asynchronous generators failed to synchronise. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Standardised nominal voltage and tolerance
nodes.note: Early systems had wild variance 100-250V; voltage drop in line means stepping up at source; tolerance band 10% critical for motor starting. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Permanent magnet stepper motor
nodes.note: Precise repeatable positioning; holding torque when de-energised; microstepping smooth motion at cost of torque; frequency response limited by inductance.

nodes.name: Primary substation and voltage regulation
nodes.note: Oil cooling essential for power transformers; tap changer must switch under load without arc; protection coordination paramount. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Knife switch and disconnect
nodes.note: No arc suppression; safe only at voltages below 600V or in oil bath; contact pressure from spring determines resistance.

nodes.name: Synchronous motor locked to line frequency
nodes.note: Must be brought up to speed by starting cage winding; field not self-excited; can operate at leading power factor and improve system power factor.

nodes.name: Synchroscope phase angle indicator
nodes.note: Operator closes paralleling switch when pointer is in fast-slow band; faster than stopping paralleling autotransformer for phase check. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Load tap changer under load
nodes.note: Arcing at tap change must be managed; some designs use reactor to limit current during transition. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Telephone exchange switching and network
nodes.note: Dial sends pulses; register interprets digits; selector then hunts for free trunk; crossbar matrix more elegant but slower.

nodes.name: Tetrode suppressor and screen grid tube
nodes.note: Screen grid voltage holds secondary electrons off plate; reduces Miller effect; higher gain than triode; screen current dissipation. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Thermistor temperature-sensitive resistor
nodes.note: PTC types also possible; hysteresis in temperature response; good for bias and compensation networks in amplifiers. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Three-wire distribution system neutral return
nodes.note: Neutral current must be zero if balanced; imbalance heats neutral and creates voltage shift; lightning strike on one phase dangerous. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Thyratron gas-filled switching tube
nodes.note: Grid loses control once conduction starts; acts as high-current switch; used for AC control and phase shifting. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Air-gap transformer inductive coupling
nodes.note: Loose coupling limits power transfer; useful for RF and signalling; avoids eddy loss but requires many turns.

nodes.name: Transmission line and coaxial cable propagation
nodes.note: Velocity factor less than speed of light; skin effect increases loss at high frequency; wavelength determines physical line length.

nodes.name: Travelling wave tube linear microwave amplifier
nodes.note: Distributed interaction gives broad bandwidth; lower efficiency than magnetron; used for satellite and communication links. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Triode amplifying vacuum tube
nodes.note: De Forest's 1906 audion; low internal impedance; positive feedback causes oscillation; feedback via grid-plate capacitance unavoidable. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Trolleybus overhead catenary power distribution
nodes.note: Pantograph contact must handle gaps and curves; power loss in catenary cable significant; quiet urban transport advantage. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Tuned circuit resonance tank LC
nodes.note: Resonant frequency given by 1/(2*pi*sqrt(LC)); quality factor Q equals reactance at resonance divided by resistance.

nodes.name: Universal motor AC and DC rated
nodes.note: Commutation challenges at 50-60 Hz on AC; brush wear in higher air-gap flux field limits life; small portable motors favour this design.

nodes.name: Thermionic valve voltmeter high impedance
nodes.note: Measures voltage without loading circuit; DC-coupled version drifts; AC-coupled for AC signals; useful for high-impedance transducers.

nodes.name: Varistor voltage-dependent resistor
nodes.note: Used for surge suppression and crowbar overvoltage protection; avalanche-like conduction; energy dissipation in transient. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Voltage regulation zener shunt and series regulator
nodes.note: Load regulation depends on output impedance; series regulation improves ripple rejection compared to zener; efficiency loss in pass element.

nodes.name: Waveguide rectangular and circular propagation
nodes.note: Cutoff frequency below which wave does not propagate; multiple modes possible; mode matching required at junctions.

nodes.name: X-ray tube and cathode ray production
nodes.note: Anode cooling critical; tube life limited by cathode emission; window allows X-ray exit; lead shielding required; radiation safety paramount.

nodes.name: Chlor-alkali, aluminium and industrial electrochemistry
nodes.note: Aluminium needs cryolite (Greenland) or a synthetic fluoride bath from your own hydrofluoric acid, which is the realistic route for you. Chlorine gives bleach and disinfectant, which loops back into public health. CALENDAR FLOOR is set by diffusion, not by construction: the economy needs roughly a generation to train the trades, form the capital and build the suppliers. Money cannot buy this down.

nodes.name: Electromagnet, relay, and the Wheatstone bridge
nodes.note: Iron amplifying a current's magnetism is the effect on which motors, generators, telegraphs and relays all rest. It is also the most alarming demonstration you will give: heavy iron moving at a distance with no visible cause.

nodes.name: Electroplating and electro-refining
nodes.note: Immediately and enormously profitable: silvered and gilded ware for the rich. It also gives you electrolytically pure copper, which you need for conductors, and it teaches your staff quantitative electrochemistry as a side effect.

nodes.name: Friction machine, Leyden jar, electroscope
nodes.note: Spectacular, cheap, and it produces exactly the kind of effect that gets a man tried for magic. Do it in daylight, in front of a magistrate, and explain it as a property of amber long known to the Greeks, which is even true (elektron is Greek for amber). High voltage, negligible current: useless for chemistry, excellent for persuasion. CORRECTION to an earlier version of this tree: this no longer requires electromagnetic theory. Franklin and Volta had none. Making the theory a prerequisite for the experiment put the whole of calculus on the electrical critical path, which is backwards. The State neither wants this nor forbids it. It simply looks like sorcery, which is a different and worse problem. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Electromagnetic theory
nodes.note: Write it down before you can demonstrate any of it. Faraday's and Maxwell's conclusions handed to a school that can already do calculus collapses a century into a decade.

nodes.name: Endow the institute in land, not coin
nodes.note: Roman testamentary law and the fundatio (Pliny's alimenta, Trajan's own) are durable vehicles. Coin will be debased to nothing by 270 AD. Land will not. This is how the programme outlives you.

nodes.name: Round the Cape
nodes.note: Herodotus reports Phoenicians doing this under Necho II, sailing south down the Red Sea and returning through the Pillars three years later. Contested, and physically possible. It joins your Mediterranean and Indian Ocean shipping into one system you own end to end.

nodes.name: A permanent post in the Americas
nodes.note: Seed stock of potato, maize, tomato, cassava, chilli and cacao; cinchona bark for malaria; Hevea rubber; Andean silver and Colombian platinum. A single successful voyage home with potato seed stock is worth more to European nutrition than anything else in this document. THE MORAL PROBLEM IS REAL AND IS NOT A FOOTNOTE: every historical version of this node was built on conquest, forced labour and epidemic catastrophe among people who had no immunity to anything you carry. The tree does not require you to repeat that. See the ethics note in 95_expeditions.md.

nodes.name: Cross the Atlantic
nodes.note: About 5,600 km from the Canaries to the Caribbean on the trade winds, roughly five weeks. The Canaries are already known to Rome; Pliny describes them. The voyage is well within a good Roman hull. What kills you is water, food and scurvy, which is why the provisioning node comes first.

nodes.name: Coastal voyage down West Africa
nodes.note: Hanno the Carthaginian sailed this coast around 500 BC and the account survives. It is coastal sailing, not an ocean crossing. It gets you West African gold directly instead of through Saharan middlemen, and it gets you LANDOLPHIA RUBBER, which is the answer to the supposedly unobtainable rubber problem.

nodes.name: Colonial administration and a chartered company
nodes.note: The legal and financial machinery that makes a distant post survive a bad decade: a chartered body with limited liability, a resident agent, a garrison, and a court. Rome has no corporation, so you must build one out of a societas plus a licensed collegium plus imperial charter.

nodes.name: Take the source by force
nodes.note: The option this tree refuses to pretend does not exist, because it is what actually happened. A pre-industrial society that meets one carrying firearms, iron ships and quinine does not win. Rome with a century's technical lead would take whatever it wanted. THE MODEL SCORES THIS AS AVAILABLE AND CHEAP AND ALSO AS THE SINGLE MOST DESTRUCTIVE NODE IN THE TREE. It is included so the tree is honest, not because it is recommended, and the simulator tracks a separate atrocity counter for it rather than folding it into the score.

nodes.name: An ocean-going hull
nodes.note: Roman merchantmen are already large: the Alexandrian grain ships carried on the order of a thousand tonnes. What they are built for is the Mediterranean, not the North Atlantic in winter. Skeleton-first framing, a sternpost rudder and a rig that will beat to windward turn a coaster into an ocean ship.

nodes.name: Open ocean navigation out of sight of land
nodes.note: Latitude by sun or pole star is straightforward. LONGITUDE IS A CLOCK PROBLEM and until you have a sea-going timekeeper you navigate by latitude sailing: run to the target latitude, then run east or west along it. Columbus did exactly that. It is inefficient and it works.

nodes.name: Provisioning a long voyage against scurvy
nodes.note: THE gate on every voyage over about ten weeks, and it is the cheapest thing in this branch. Scurvy killed more sailors than storms and battle combined for four centuries. You know the answer: fresh or preserved citrus, or any source of ascorbic acid, and sauerkraut works. Rome has lemons and citrons, and cabbage. Solve this and the Atlantic becomes a logistics problem instead of a death sentence.

nodes.name: Extend the existing eastern trade routes
nodes.note: Rome ALREADY trades to India annually on the monsoon and to China by relay. You do not need to discover anything: you need agents, capital and a standing order. This is the cheapest way to obtain saltpetre, shellac, cotton, wootz, camphor and pepper, and it should be one of your first commercial acts.

nodes.name: Transplanting a crop out of its homeland
nodes.note: The highest-leverage act of industrial espionage available. Sugar cane, cotton, tea, coffee, cloves, cinchona and rubber were ALL moved out of their homelands by deliberate transplant, and every one of those transplants broke a monopoly and collapsed a price. Wardian cases (a sealed glazed box) are what make live plants survive a long sea voyage, and that is a trivial thing to build.

nodes.name: Advertising as industry
nodes.note: Merchants pay to announce their goods in newspapers and on placards. Becomes major revenue source for publishers. Creates a market for attention. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Almanac and reference publication
nodes.note: Annual publication of tables, calendars, and reference data. Farmers, sailors, and merchants each buy the relevant sections. Popular and profitable. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Annona grain dole and administration
nodes.note: State purchase and distribution of grain. Requires contracts with producers, shipping, storage, and accounting.

nodes.name: Annuity and fixed income stream
nodes.note: Contract paying a fixed income for life or a fixed term. Allows the elderly to convert a lump sum into regular payments. Requires good mortality data to price.

nodes.name: Apprenticeship indenture and training contract
nodes.note: Written contract binding a youth to a master for learning a trade, usually 7 years. Controls training standards and succession but binds the apprentice to one employer.

nodes.name: Arabic numerals in commerce
nodes.note: Position notation with zero makes arithmetic dramatically faster than Roman numerals. Merchants who adopt it can calculate faster than competitors, reducing error and increasing profit.

nodes.name: Arbitrage and price equalisation
nodes.note: Buy cheap in one place and sell dear in another. Requires quick transport and communication. Drives prices toward equilibrium across locations and is profitable only when markets are fragmented.

nodes.name: Deposit bankers (argentarii)
nodes.note: Money changers and deposit takers in Rome. Accept deposits, testify to witnesses about amounts held, but do not systematically lend.

nodes.name: Assay office and hallmarking
nodes.note: Official test of precious metal fineness, with a hallmark proving the state's guarantee. Allows buyers to trust the quality without testing every item.

nodes.name: Auction and competitive bidding
nodes.note: Sale to highest bidder, used for slaves, real estate, and state contracts. Reveals market value and discourages corruption.

nodes.name: Bankruptcy law and insolvency
nodes.note: Legal process when a debtor cannot pay. Creditors receive a fraction of their claims. Without it, a debtor can simply flee or hide assets. With it, creditors have incentive to give credit in the first place.

nodes.name: Bill of exchange
nodes.note: Written order to pay a sum of money at a future date. Allows moving value across distance without moving metal through bandit-infested roads. Reduces transport cost and risk of loss.

nodes.name: Bimetallism and fixed exchange
nodes.note: Fix a legal ratio of gold to silver coins. Solves the problem of scarce gold by allowing silver to serve as backup. But if the market ratio diverges from the fixed ratio, people hoard the undervalued metal. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Bond and debt security
nodes.note: Fixed-income security representing a debt obligation. Pays coupons on schedule and returns principal at maturity. Tradeable like shares.

nodes.name: Brand and goodwill
nodes.note: Reputation for quality associated with a maker's mark. Allows the maker to charge premium prices and is valuable enough to be sold separately from the business.

nodes.name: Canal company and inland waterway
nodes.note: Company digs canal and charges tolls for passage. Massive investment but water transport is cheaper than land transport for bulk goods. Attracts industries that use water. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Cartel and market sharing agreement
nodes.note: Agreement between competitors to divide market and fix prices. Often illegal but profitable. Unstable because each member wants to cheat.

nodes.name: Census and population enumeration
nodes.note: Official counting of population by age, sex, occupation, and wealth. Enables taxation and conscription and produces economic data. Expensive but government views it as essential.

nodes.name: Central bank and monetary authority
nodes.note: Bank chartered by the state to manage the nation's monetary system. Acts as lender of last resort and regulates other banks. Threatens existing banking families with monopoly loss.

nodes.name: Chain store and multiple locations
nodes.note: Company operates identical stores in multiple cities, buying centrally and selling retail in each location. Achieves scale but requires sophisticated management and accounting.

nodes.name: Cheque and demand draft
nodes.note: Demand draft on a bank, payable on sight. Unlike a bill of exchange, it is not a promise to pay at a future date but an order to transfer immediately from the drawer's deposit.

nodes.name: Civil service examination
nodes.note: Competitive written examination for appointment to government positions. Replaces patronage with merit, reducing corruption and improving quality of administration.

nodes.name: Classified advertisement
nodes.note: Small notice for sale or hire of specific items. Much cheaper than display advertising and highly profitable because readers actively search for them. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Clearing house and interbank settlement
nodes.note: Central place where multiple banks settle debts to each other by netting. A merchant from bank A pays a merchant from bank B thousands of times per day. Instead of settling each individually, the clearing house nets all transactions and banks owe each other only the balance.

nodes.name: Coffee house as information market
nodes.note: Establishment where customers gather to drink coffee and exchange information. Merchants trade information about prices, shipments, and credit. Newspapers available. Becomes centre of financial gossip.

nodes.name: Coined money
nodes.note: Standardised metal coins as medium of exchange and store of value. Rome has perfected this for centuries.

nodes.name: Professional associations (collegia)
nodes.note: Craft guilds and professional societies. Enforce standards, restrict entry, and provide mutual aid. State views them with suspicion.

nodes.name: Commodity exchange and standardised contracts
nodes.note: Market for standardised futures contracts, allowing rapid trading and price discovery. Grading systems ensure all contracts for a good are actually equivalent.

nodes.name: Company town and tied housing
nodes.note: Employer provides housing, food, and goods to workers in a closed economy. Workers cannot leave without losing housing and may be paid in company scrip. Highly profitable but politically dangerous.

nodes.name: Contract law and enforcement
nodes.note: Legal framework for enforcing voluntary agreements. Necessary foundation for all complex commerce.

nodes.name: Copyright and literary rights
nodes.note: Exclusive right to copy a book or written work for a limited time. Gives authors incentive to publish but restricts who can make copies. Requires printing to be valuable.

nodes.name: Customs house and tariff collection
nodes.note: Office at border or port to assess and collect tariffs. Inspectors examine goods to determine their nature and value. Requires clerical staff and standardised procedures.

nodes.name: Department store and general merchandise
nodes.note: Single building selling multiple categories of goods under one roof. Reduces customer search time and allows operators to manage inventory centrally.

nodes.name: Deposit bank and current account
nodes.note: Bank that accepts deposits and allows withdrawal on demand. Not merely storage but active management of customer funds. Requires trust, double-entry records, and systematic procedures.

nodes.name: Directory and business listing
nodes.note: Alphabetical listing of merchants, trades, and professions in a city with addresses. Reduces search costs for consumers. Sellers pay to list themselves. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Discounting and advance payment
nodes.note: A banker buys a future payment at a discount, paying less than the face value today. The difference is the interest charge. Transforms future cash into immediate liquidity.

nodes.name: Double-entry bookkeeping
nodes.note: Every transaction appears twice, once as debit, once as credit. Makes error self-detecting: if debit total does not equal credit total, there is an arithmetic mistake. This is the foundation of trust between owner and manager across distance. Without it, the manager can simply lie.

nodes.name: Contract of employment
nodes.note: Written agreement specifying duties, term, and compensation. Protects both employer and employee and reduces disputes.

nodes.name: Endorsement and negotiability
nodes.note: The holder can sign the back of a bill and pass it to another party. Transforms a personal IOU into a negotiable instrument that can be traded like currency.

nodes.name: Endowed chair and endowment
nodes.note: Wealthy patron donates capital and the income is used to pay a professor. Removes the chair from student fees and allows focus on scholarship rather than teaching revenue.

nodes.name: Factory and integrated production
nodes.note: Single building housing all production steps, with standardised procedures and division of labour. Dramatically increases output per worker and reduces defects.

nodes.name: Ferry and toll crossing
nodes.note: Regular boat crossing operated for a fee. Operator owns boat and landing and extracts rent from every crossing. Profitable if there is no alternative.

nodes.name: Fire insurance
nodes.note: Insurance against fire loss of buildings and goods. Solves the problem of catastrophic unexpected loss. Insurers must pool many risks so that a single event does not bankrupt them.

nodes.name: Fractional reserve banking
nodes.note: Bank lends out most of the deposits it receives, keeping only a fraction in reserve. Multiplies the money supply and increases lending capacity but creates risk if too many depositors demand withdrawal at once.

nodes.name: Futures contract and forward dealing
nodes.note: Agreement to buy or sell a commodity at a fixed price on a future date. Allows farmers to lock in a price and speculators to bet on price changes. Subject to default risk.

nodes.name: Gambling house and gaming establishment
nodes.note: Establishment where customers gamble, with the house taking a cut of all winnings. Highly profitable but attracts violence and is often banned or heavily taxed.

nodes.name: Standing bureaucracy
nodes.note: Professional staff of administrators employed by the state to carry out government functions. Rome has developed extensive bureaucracy.

nodes.name: Guild and monopoly craft
nodes.note: Association of craftsmen with exclusive right to practice the trade in a city. Enforces quality and training standards but restricts competition and raises prices.

nodes.name: Hotel and commercial lodging
nodes.note: Establishment renting rooms to travellers by the night. Includes meals and services. Operates on thin margins but benefits from steady customer flow.

nodes.name: Inn and coaching house
nodes.note: Smaller than hotel, often also a tavern. Provides room and food to travellers and locals alike. Profits from food, drink, and accommodation.

nodes.name: Joint-stock company with permanent existence
nodes.note: Business owned by many shareholders, each owning a fixed fraction. Survives the death of any owner. Allows raising capital from people who do not want to be personally involved in management. Competes directly with the family business model.

nodes.name: Learned society and academic journal
nodes.note: Society of scholars publishing a regular journal of discoveries. Creates peer review and credibility. Charges subscription and creates career incentive for scholars to publish.

nodes.name: Ledger and account books
nodes.note: Permanent record of all accounts, organised by account type. Enables consistent accounting over years and allows auditing.

nodes.name: Lending library and subscription library
nodes.note: Members pay subscription fee to borrow books. Economical because each book is read by many people. Profitable even if each book costs more than any individual would pay. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Life insurance
nodes.note: Insurance against death, paying a benefit to the beneficiary. Requires mortality data to price correctly. Allows families to insure against the death of breadwinners.

nodes.name: Limited liability
nodes.note: Shareholder loses only the money invested, not personal assets. Not a tax dodge. This is what makes a stranger willing to invest in a ship or factory he cannot supervise. Without it, any disaster bankrupts him and he avoids the risk entirely.

nodes.name: Lottery and state gambling
nodes.note: State operates drawing where purchasers win prizes. Profitable because house advantage is high. Paradoxically, state lotteries funded real public works and created public capital.

nodes.name: Mail order catalogue and distance selling
nodes.note: Company publishes catalogue and sends it to customers nationwide. Orders arrive by post and goods ship via mail or carrier. Enables shopping without a store visit.

nodes.name: Marine insurance
nodes.note: Insurance against ship loss. The holder pays a premium and receives compensation if the cargo or vessel is lost. Insurance is not a bet: it is the sale of variance, allowing risk-averse merchants to transfer risk to professional risk-takers.

nodes.name: Maritime loan at high interest
nodes.note: High-interest loan for sea trade, forgiven if cargo is lost to weather. The lender bears the ship loss risk, the high interest compensates.

nodes.name: Permanent market and market law
nodes.note: Regular marketplace with established location, rules, and enforcement. Reduces search costs for buyers and sellers.

nodes.name: Monopoly and exclusive grant
nodes.note: State grants exclusive right to sell a good. Raises prices but guarantees supply. Often granted to extract more tax. Breaks existing merchants' ability to compete.

nodes.name: Mortality table and actuarial mathematics
nodes.note: Systematic data on age at death, allowing calculation of the probability of death at each age. Without this, life insurance premiums are guesses. With it, they are calculated.

nodes.name: Mortgage and real estate credit
nodes.note: Loan secured by real estate, which can be seized if the borrower defaults. Allows the poor to buy land by spreading payment over years.

nodes.name: Museum and public collection
nodes.note: Building housing collections of art, specimens, and antiquities open to the public. Charges admission and attracts tourism. Requires space, climate control, and security.

nodes.name: News agency and wire service
nodes.note: Service collecting news from correspondents and selling it to newspapers via telegraph. Reduces cost of news gathering and allows small papers to compete. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Newspaper as business and subscription
nodes.note: Regular publication reporting news, sold by subscription or single copy. Profitable from subscriptions and later advertising. Attracts literacy and creates information market. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Omnibus and public stage coach
nodes.note: Coach carrying multiple paying passengers on a fixed route. Cheaper than hiring a private carriage. Operates on schedule and shares capacity with strangers. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Paper money and note issue
nodes.note: Central bank issues paper notes redeemable in metal on demand. Solves the portability problem of coined money but introduces counterfeiting risk and requires trust in the issuer.

nodes.name: Patent and exclusive right
nodes.note: State grants exclusive right to make an invention for a limited time. Creates monopoly the state did not previously grant. Incentivises disclosure rather than secrecy, but monopolists often resist.

nodes.name: Patent office and examination
nodes.note: Government body that examines patent applications for novelty and issues letters patent. Requires technical expertise and creates a complete archive of inventions.

nodes.name: Pawnshop and secured loan
nodes.note: Loan in exchange for movable goods as security. If not repaid, the pawnbroker sells the goods. Often the only credit available to the poor. Profits from high interest and sale of forfeited items.

nodes.name: Pension and retirement scheme
nodes.note: Employer or state commits to paying workers income after retirement. Requires huge capital accumulation and actuarial discipline. Creates obligation that survives the employer.

nodes.name: Plantation and large estate agriculture
nodes.note: Large estate specialising in a single commercial crop, worked by many labourers. Often worked by enslaved or semi-enslaved labour. Extremely profitable for the owner, extremely brutal for the labourers.

nodes.name: Printed playing card and card game
nodes.note: Woodcut cards, faster and cheaper than hand-painted. Creates mass market for cards. High profit because cards wear out and players buy replacements.

nodes.name: Post office and mail handling
nodes.note: Office receiving, sorting, and forwarding mail. Centralises handling and creates accountability. Prevents loss and enables tracking.

nodes.name: Postal service as paid business
nodes.note: Regular delivery of letters and small packages for a fee. Requires stations, horses, and staff. Profitable because merchants will pay to guarantee delivery.

nodes.name: Professional examination and licence
nodes.note: State or guild administers written or practical test to certify competence. Prevents unqualified practitioners from harming customers. Restricts entry but creates credible certification.

nodes.name: Professional sport as business
nodes.note: Athletes paid to compete in front of paying audiences. Ticket sales, concessions, and gambling generate revenue. Creates a career outside traditional trades.

nodes.name: Promissory note
nodes.note: Promise by one party to pay a fixed sum to another at a future date. Simpler than a bill of exchange and does not require a third party.

nodes.name: Public debt and government borrowing
nodes.note: State borrows money instead of raising taxes or debasing currency. A state that can borrow can survive temporary deficits and invest in long-term projects without waiting for revenue. A state that cannot borrow must tax harder or debase, both politically costly.

nodes.name: Racecourse and pari-mutuel betting
nodes.note: Track where horses race and spectators place bets. Betters pool money and results are divided. House takes a percentage. Expensive to operate but attracts wealthy betters.

nodes.name: Railway company and rail service
nodes.note: Company operates railroad and charges passengers and freight shippers. Transforms inland transportation but requires massive capital investment and creates monopoly power. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Reinsurance and risk pooling
nodes.note: Insurance for insurance companies. An insurer buys reinsurance to protect against catastrophic losses. Allows insurers to take on larger risks than their own capital supports.

nodes.name: Research institute and endowed laboratory
nodes.note: Institute funded by endowment, focused purely on research without teaching obligation. Attracts top scholars and creates knowledge spillovers to industry.

nodes.name: Restaurant and commercial kitchen
nodes.note: Establishment serving prepared meals to paying customers. Separate from lodging. Requires reliable supply of ingredients and skilled cooks.

nodes.name: Savings bank for small deposits
nodes.note: Bank accepting small deposits from poor people and paying interest. Encourages thrift and provides safe storage. Rare because the overhead of managing thousands of small accounts is high.

nodes.name: Seigniorage and debasement
nodes.note: Profit from issuing new money, the difference between the value of the coin and the value of the metal in it. Tempts rulers to debase currency by reducing metal content. Short-term profit destroys long-term monetary trust.

nodes.name: Share and share transfer
nodes.note: Transferable ownership certificate. Shareholder can sell to another without dissolving the company. Makes capital liquid and allows investment without long commitment.

nodes.name: Partnership (societas)
nodes.note: Contractual partnership between two or more parties to share profits and losses. Legally recognised, but partners remain personally liable.

nodes.name: Postage stamp and paid marking
nodes.note: Adhesive mark proving postage paid. Replaced trust in the post office with prepaid proof. Enables sender to pay instead of recipient. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Standard weights and measures
nodes.note: Approved standard measures held by the state and enforced in markets. Prevents fraud and allows price comparison across merchants and time.

nodes.name: Statistical office and data collection
nodes.note: Office that collects, compiles, and publishes data on trade, prices, production, and population. Enables policy decisions based on facts rather than anecdote.

nodes.name: Stock exchange and organised trading
nodes.note: Permanent marketplace for shares. Allows quick price discovery and liquid exit. Draws wealth from direct business operations into financial markets.

nodes.name: Survey and map as state instrument
nodes.note: Government surveys territory systematically and produces maps. Used for tax assessment, military planning, and engineering projects. Creates baseline for all future development.

nodes.name: Tariff and import duty
nodes.note: Tax on imported goods. Raises revenue and protects local producers from foreign competition. Typically unpopular with consumers.

nodes.name: Tax farming and revenue contracts
nodes.note: State contracts out tax collection to private businessmen. Transfers risk to the contractor in exchange for immediate cash.

nodes.name: Telegraph as commercial service
nodes.note: Companies operate telegraph networks and sell message transmission by the word. Enables rapid long-distance communication of prices and news. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Testament and inheritance law
nodes.note: Formal document disposing of property at death. Creates certainty and allows wealth to be controlled across generations.

nodes.name: Theatre as business
nodes.note: Owner builds theatre and sells admission. Profits from ticket sales, concessions, and occasionally gambling. Attracts crowds and creates employment.

nodes.name: Toll bridge and road toll
nodes.note: Operator builds or repairs a bridge and collects tolls from every user. High initial cost but profitable over decades. Reduces journey time compared to fording. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Totalisator machine and automated payout
nodes.note: Machine that collects bets, calculates odds, and prints tickets. Allows rapid handling of high volume. Can calculate complex betting combinations automatically.

nodes.name: Trade union and workers collegium
nodes.note: Association of workers to bargain collectively with employers. State view with suspicion as a conspiracy in restraint of trade. Wages negotiated by the union are higher than wages negotiated individually.

nodes.name: Trademark and mark of quality
nodes.note: Registered mark that identifies goods of a maker. Prevents confusion and protects reputation. Requires central registry and enforcement against counterfeits.

nodes.name: Trading post and remote store
nodes.note: Store in remote area, often far from competition. High margins because goods are rare locally but operator faces transportation cost and risk.

nodes.name: Tramway and urban rail
nodes.note: Streetcar line within a city, powered by horse or later electricity. Charges passengers and concentrates development along the line. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Trial balance and error detection
nodes.note: Periodic total of all accounts to verify that debits equal credits. Catches errors before they propagate and corrupt future records.

nodes.name: Turnpike trust and road company
nodes.note: Company builds high-quality toll road, collecting tolls to repay investment and fund maintenance. Significantly faster travel time attracts commercial traffic. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: University and degree-granting institution
nodes.note: School awarding degrees that certify learning. Charges tuition but also grants scholarships. Attracts scholars and students and creates local employment.

nodes.name: Usury evasion through legal fiction
nodes.note: Structure a loan as sale with buyback, or as a partnership, to hide the interest. If caught, the lender loses everything and may be punished. Ubiquitous despite the risk.

nodes.name: Usury law and interest regulation
nodes.note: Legal limit on interest rates. Prevents exploitation of desperate borrowers but suppresses lending because lenders cannot be compensated for risk. Regularly evaded through fiction.

nodes.name: Wage and labour payment
nodes.note: Regular payment for labour. Rome pays wages in coin or kind.

nodes.name: Finery forge and the puddling furnace
nodes.note: Cast iron is brittle and useless for anything that must bend. Decarburise it back to wrought iron in a finery, then in a reverberatory puddling furnace where the fuel never touches the metal. Now you have cheap bar iron in quantity, which is the input to everything mechanical. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_1300 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: decarburizing cast iron in puddling furnace at 1300 C requires water-blown blast furnace heat] [SCALED: this is an INDUSTRY, not a demonstration. At 250 tonnes of product a year it consumes about 1,500 tonnes of charcoal annually, derived from the physical ratio in data/world/resources.json rather than guessed. At 0.75 tonnes of charcoal per hectare of coppice per year that is roughly 2,000 hectares of forest under permanent management, which you must own before you light it.]

nodes.name: Buy, train and manumit a technical staff
nodes.note: Buy skilled slaves, teach them, free them, pay them, keep them. Freedmen retain obligation to their patron, can hold property, and ran much of Roman commerce. A paid literate freedman transmits knowledge; a coerced labourer does not. This is both the ethical and the efficient answer. Grants +8 artisans.

nodes.name: Written agricultural treatises and knowledge codification
nodes.note: Codify agricultural knowledge in written treatises: crop rotation schedules, soil types, fertilizer rates, machinery designs, preservation methods. Spreads best practices beyond oral tradition. Requires literacy and sustained scholarship.

nodes.name: Alfalfa (lucerne) cultivation
nodes.note: Perennial legume for permanent meadows; fixes nitrogen, produces 4-6 cuts per season for fodder. Survives winter in warmer regions. Imported from Central Asia; needs good drainage and lime on acid soils. Transforms winter feeding.

nodes.name: Sugar beet cultivation and crystallization
nodes.note: Grow sugar beets in cool northern climates where cane fails. Extract juice, treat with lime and acid to remove impurities (sulfur dioxide helps), evaporate under vacuum, and crystallize. Refinery is capital-intensive. Enables sugar production independent of tropical trade. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.] [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_vac_1torr added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: vacuum pan evaporation essential for consistent sugar crystallization]

nodes.name: Bone meal as phosphate fertilizer
nodes.note: Collect bones from butchers and boil with manure to break them down and create a phosphate-rich mulch. Slower than guano but reliably produced locally. Improves root development and seed formation.

nodes.name: Bottling with cork closure and sealed glass
nodes.note: Store liquids in strong glass bottles, insert cork and secure with wire or cage. Anaerobic storage preserves wine, beer, vinegar. Glass is Roman technology; cork sealing enables long-term aging and transport. Enables wine trade and aging in cellars.

nodes.name: Brewing with hops for flavor and preservation
nodes.note: Add dried hop flowers to boiling wort; the alpha acids bitter and preserve the beer, preventing spoilage. Replaces gruit (herb mixtures). Grew in southern Germany in the 9th century; spread north over centuries. Enables longer storage and transport of beer.

nodes.name: Can opener device for tin cans
nodes.note: Cutting tool with rotating wheel or wedge to pierce and cut can edge, or butterfly handle lever that turns a cutting wheel around the rim. Arrives decades after cans become common. Without it, consumers use knives and hammers.

nodes.name: Canning by Appert's method (heating in sealed glass)
nodes.note: Pack food in strong glass jar, seal with cork and wire, heat in water bath to 95-100 C for 30-60 minutes depending on acid content. Low-acid foods (meats, vegetables) are risky without understanding of clostridium botulinum and its toxin. Works for high-acid foods (pickles, jams) without germ theory. Revolutionary for food security if done carefully.

nodes.name: Cacao
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. One voyage for seed stock, then transplant. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Clover as winter grazing and fodder
nodes.note: Nitrogen-fixing legume sown in fallows or as early spring feed; survives winter in milder regions, providing grazing and supplementary hay. Combines nitrogen restoration with animal fodder. Seed production is key constraint.

nodes.name: Coffee import from Near East and Ethiopia
nodes.note: Import coffee beans from Arabian and Ethiopian merchants. Roast, grind, and brew with hot water. Later becomes urban necessity in coffeehouses. Currently rare and expensive in the Mediterranean. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Cold chain and refrigerated railway shipping
nodes.note: Insulated railway cars with mechanical refrigeration carry fresh meat, dairy, and vegetables hundreds of miles to distant markets. Requires coordination with meatpacking plants, railways, and distribution. Breaks ancient food supply constraints; enables urban growth and meat consumption.

nodes.name: Combine harvester (reaper, thresher, winnower integrated)
nodes.note: Reaper feeds cut grain into threshing drum and winnowing mechanism; discharges bagged grain and straw bales. Steam- or petrol-powered. Requires flat or gentle ground, good visibility, and skilled operators. 20-30 acres per day vs 1 acre hand harvest.

nodes.name: Controlled pollination of crop plants
nodes.note: Hand-pollinate selected plants using brushes to cross desired traits: large seeds with disease resistance, for instance. Works on grains and legumes. Requires understanding flower anatomy and patience; gains compound with pedigree records.

nodes.name: Butter production at scale from dairy cattle
nodes.note: Churn milk in barrel or wooden churn to separate butterfat from buttermilk. Butter stores for months salted in wooden vessels. Higher value than milk for trade. Requires cool cellar and daily production.

nodes.name: Controlled cheese aging and storage
nodes.note: Store cheese wheels in cool caves or cellars; maintain humidity and temperature for months or years. Aged hard cheeses develop flavor and keep indefinitely. Requires careful cave management to prevent mold and rot.

nodes.name: Distillation of spirits and liqueurs
nodes.note: Heat fermented beer or wine in copper alembic with condenser; collect vapors as high-proof spirit. Required copper work and heat control. Spirits store longer than wine and command high prices. Banned in some jurisdictions as luxury and fire hazard.

nodes.name: Drying and concentration of evaporated milk
nodes.note: Heat milk gently in copper pan under partial vacuum (reduces boiling point) or in open pan to evaporate water until thick. Can milk solids are concentrated 2-3 fold. Stores several months in sealed tin. Reconstitutes with water or used directly in cooking. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Enclosure of common land and private farming
nodes.note: Fence and claim private ownership of formerly communal pasture and fields. Allows strategic crop rotation without community approval. Displaces peasants and common folk; generates social resistance. Enables capital-intensive farming but concentrates wealth and land ownership.

nodes.name: Farm as capital enterprise with investment and profit
nodes.note: Treat farming as a business venture: invest capital in land, buildings, machinery, and labor; track costs and revenue; aim for profit rather than subsistence. Requires accounting, written records, and credit access. Transforms peasant farming into an industrial enterprise.

nodes.name: Large-scale fish curing and smoking
nodes.note: Salt-dry fish over winter, then hang and smoke over oak or beech. Produces shelf-stable protein that survives transport. Atlantic cod and herring can be processed at scale by coastal villages. Cheap protein for armies and urban poor.

nodes.name: Freezing food with mechanical refrigeration
nodes.note: Use mechanical refrigeration to freeze meat, fish, and vegetables at -18 C. Frozen foods preserve for months. Thaw and cook before use. Requires reliable electricity or steam power and insulated freezer chambers.

nodes.name: Cylindrical silos for bulk grain storage
nodes.note: Build tall cylindrical brick or wooden towers for grain storage. Pressure from grain weight above excludes insects and rodents. Chutes at bottom for withdrawal. More efficient than rectangular granaries. Enables large centralized storage for grain dole. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Guano import and application as fertilizer
nodes.note: Import bird guano from coastal cliffs or islands (Peru, North Africa) via merchants. Rich in nitrogen and phosphorus; application can double grain yields locally. Expensive, but supply is predictable. Builds dependency on trade and distant supply chains.

nodes.name: Haber process for synthetic ammonia and nitrate
nodes.note: Compress hydrogen and nitrogen at 200 atmospheres over iron catalyst at 400-500 C to synthesize ammonia; oxidize ammonia to nitric acid. Requires high-pressure steel vessels, control systems, and electric power. Enables synthetic fertilizer production at scale but only late in the tree.

nodes.name: Hay making and dry storage
nodes.note: Cut grass at peak nutrition, dry thoroughly in sun and wind, store in dry barn or haybarn. Timing and weather are critical - rain-soaked hay rots or molts. Enables winter feeding of draft animals when pasture is gone. [FIXED after independent audit: hay needs a scythe and a dry barn, both of which Rome has. Crop rotation is unrelated.]

nodes.name: Heavy mouldboard plough with coulter (regional)
nodes.note: Heavy plough with iron coulter, share, and mould board on two wheels, drawn by team of oxen. Turns thick clay sods on cold northern soils where the Mediterranean ard is useless. Expensive and slow but enables fertile northern lands. Do not use on light Mediterranean soils. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Horse-drawn hoe for weeding between rows
nodes.note: Simple cultivator or hoe frame pulled by horse along seed drill rows to cut weeds between plants. Requires plants spaced precisely by the drill. Eliminates hand-hoeing drudgery and allows larger plantings.

nodes.name: Ice harvesting from frozen lakes and rivers
nodes.note: Cut blocks of ice from frozen water with saw and chisel during winter thaw, transport quickly to ice house, layer with sawdust or hay. Most ice melts in transport and storage, requiring multiple harvests per winter. Requires cold climate and labor.

nodes.name: Ice house construction and storage
nodes.note: Build underground or half-underground stone or brick chamber with thick insulation (sawdust, straw, or hay). Roof with thatch and timber. Store blocks of winter ice with straw layers. Temperature stays below freezing even in summer if well-insulated. Enables ice cream and chilled foods.

nodes.name: Trade and logistics of ice transport
nodes.note: Transport harvested ice via wagon or ship to towns 50-100 miles away, insulated with sawdust and straw. Arrive with 30-50% loss. Sells to affluent households and restaurants for drinks and food preservation. High loss but profitable if demand is strong. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Liming of acidic soils
nodes.note: Spread quicklime or slaked lime on clay and peat soils to neutralize acidity and improve drainage. Enables cultivation of marginal northern lands. Effects last 5-10 years; must be repeated. Transform intractable soil into productive land.

nodes.name: Selective breeding of draft and dairy cattle
nodes.note: Breed cattle for strength (draft animals) or milk production (dairy cattle) over many generations. Selective breeding can double milk yield or hauling power. Requires pedigree tracking and patience; gains compound over 5-10 years.

nodes.name: Selective breeding of sheep for wool and meat
nodes.note: Breed sheep for fine fleece and lean meat. Selective breeding improves wool fineness and meat quality over generations. Wool becomes higher value product. Requires pedigree tracking.

nodes.name: Maize
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. One voyage for seed stock. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Malt production from barley and other grains
nodes.note: Soak barley, allow it to germinate, then dry in kiln to stop germination. Malting converts starches to fermentable sugars. Malt stores for months and is essential for brewing consistent beer. Requires cool storage to prevent mold. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. nodes.name: Margarine from refined and hardened vegetable oils
nodes.note: Bubble hydrogen through liquid vegetable oil over nickel catalyst to saturate double bonds and raise melting point. Result resembles butter in texture. Cheaper than dairy butter. Requires understanding of hydrogenation chemistry and high-purity hydrogen.

nodes.name: Mechanical grain reaper
nodes.note: Horse-drawn frame with reciprocating knife blade and conveyor tray delivers cut grain to platform or wagon. Reaps four to six acres per day versus one acre for hand scythe. Requires training and maintenance. Leaves stubble taller than scythe.

nodes.name: Mechanical refrigeration using compression and evaporation
nodes.note: Compress ether or ammonia vapor, cool it with water, then expand through throttle valve to evaporate. Evaporation absorbs heat from a chamber, cooling it to 5-10 C. Requires high-precision pump, copper tubing, and steam power. Toxic if ammonia leaks.

nodes.name: Recognition of nitrogen-fixing legume crops
nodes.note: Understand that legumes (peas, beans, clover, alfalfa) restore soil fertility where grain depletes it; systemize the rotation. Not chemistry, but empirical observation that legume-rich fields grow better grain. Foundation for three-field rotation success.

nodes.name: Pasteurisation of milk and beverages
nodes.note: Heat milk to 63-65 C for 30 minutes or 72 C for 15 seconds, then cool rapidly. Kills spoilage bacteria and pathogens without destroying nutritional value or flavor of fresh milk. Works without germ theory; empirically known to prevent souring and spoilage.

nodes.name: The potato
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. Two to four times the calories per hectare of wheat on poor ground. One voyage, then you grow it forever. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Rice cultivation in paddies
nodes.note: Cultivate rice in water-filled paddies in warm regions with reliable summer irrigation. Requires leveled fields, water control, and careful timing. High yield per acre but demands labor-intensive transplanting. Imported seed and knowledge from Asia.

nodes.name: Roller mill for grain (replacing millstone)
nodes.note: Pairs of hardened steel rollers crush grain more uniformly than stones. Multiple roller pairs reduce grain progressively, producing finer flour with less grit. Can produce white flour by separating bran. Requires precision machining and hardened steel.

nodes.name: White flour from roller milling and bran separation
nodes.note: Run milled flour through bolters (cylindrical silk screens) to separate white endosperm from brown bran. Produces elegant white bread prized in cities. Bran removal discards B vitamins and niacin; prolonged white-flour diet causes pellagra and beriberi. Major population health risk.

nodes.name: Root cellar and cool storage construction
nodes.note: Dig cool underground chamber below frost line with air vents; temperature stays 4-10 C year-round. Stores turnips, apples, onions, potatoes for months. Requires only soil, timber, and patience; enables winter feeding and food security.

nodes.name: Mechanical seed drill
nodes.note: Hopper with rotating cams or gears deposits seed at regular intervals in furrow. Spacing is controllable. Saves 40-60% of broadcast seed waste and improves germination by consistent burial depth. Requires precision woodwork.

nodes.name: Selective breeding with written pedigrees
nodes.note: Record traits of seed plants and breeding animals over generations; select for yield, disease resistance, or size. Pedigree tracking allows avoiding inbreeding and accumulating improvements. Requires literacy and 5-7 year commitment before visible yield gains.

nodes.name: Silage production and fermented fodder storage
nodes.note: Pack fresh grass tightly in pits or wooden silos with salt, exclude air, and let anaerobic bacteria ferment it. Preserves nutrition without sun-drying and works in wet climates. Requires understanding of fermentation and airtight storage design. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs.
