nodes.note: The first thermoplastic. Film base, combs, billiard balls. VIOLENTLY FLAMMABLE and it is what made early cinema so dangerous.

nodes.name: Portland cement
nodes.note: Calcined limestone and clay, ground fine. HONEST NOTE: it is not obviously better than Roman pozzolanic concrete for marine work. Its advantage is consistency and independence from Puteoli.

nodes.name: Charcoal
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. The real ceiling on iron output is forest, not ore.

nodes.name: Sodium nitrate
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE, and also not needed. Bengal saltpetre is on a route Rome already sails and supplied the world's gunpowder for centuries, and nitre beds work anywhere. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Chlorine and bleach
nodes.note: Bleaching powder ends the field-bleaching bottleneck that limited every textile industry, and hypochlorite makes water safe. Also war gas: be careful whom you teach.

nodes.name: Chromium
nodes.note: Aluminothermic or carbon reduction of chromite. Stainless, plating, refractories.

nodes.name: Reinforced concrete
nodes.note: Roman concrete is superb in compression and useless in tension. Steel rod fixes that, and the thermal expansion of steel and concrete happen to match closely enough to work, which is luck rather than design.

nodes.name: Copper (fire refined)
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Not pure enough for good conductors; see cap_pure_4N.

nodes.name: Crucible steel
nodes.note: Homogeneous, slag-free, and the gate on every cutting tool and every lead screw.

nodes.name: Cryolite, or a synthetic fluoride bath
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. Ivigtut in Greenland is the only workable natural deposit, but a synthetic fluoride bath made from your own hydrofluoric acid works, which is what industry moved to anyway. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Synthetic dyes (aniline)
nodes.note: Coal tar to benzene to aniline to mauveine and the rest. Historically this single industry funded organic chemistry, created the first industrial research laboratories, and led directly to pharmaceuticals. Enormously profitable and politically harmless. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_measure_temp added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: coal tar to aniline synthesis involves exothermic reactions needing temperature control]

nodes.name: Emery (Naxos)
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Your abrasive for every ground surface in this document. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Formaldehyde
nodes.note: Catalytic oxidation of methanol from wood distillation. Resins, and the first practical tissue preservative.

nodes.name: Fused quartz
nodes.note: Pure silica worked at 1700 to 2000 C with an oxy-hydrogen flame. Indispensable later: you cannot zone refine germanium in anything that contaminates it. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Galena (lead sulfide)
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS everywhere it mines lead. It is also a working semiconductor, which nobody will suspect for 1800 years.

nodes.name: Borosilicate glass
nodes.note: Low thermal expansion. The difference between a laboratory and a pile of broken retorts. Needs boron; the Larderello fumaroles in Tuscany are inside the Empire, which is a genuinely lucky break if it holds. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_1600 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: borosilicate glass melting at 1650-1700 C]

nodes.name: Lead crystal (flint glass)
nodes.note: High dispersion. Pair it with crown glass and you get the achromatic doublet, which is what makes a compound microscope beat a single bead.

nodes.name: Soda-lime glass
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS and is genuinely good at it, including deliberately decolourised near-colourless glass.

nodes.name: Glycerol
nodes.note: A by-product of soap making that Rome throws away.

nodes.name: Gold
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Las Medulas, and Dacia from 106 AD.

nodes.name: High purity graphite
nodes.note: Acheson process: heat carbon to about 2500 C. Crucibles and boats that do not contaminate what is melted in them, which is exactly what zone refining needs. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Gutta percha
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. Palaquium latex from Malaya, reached by extending east the India route Rome already sails annually. Indian and Malay traders already carry it partway. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Gypsum plaster
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS.

nodes.name: Artificial ice and mechanical refrigeration
nodes.note: Vapour compression with ammonia. Food preservation, meat shipping, brewing year round, and the seed of gas liquefaction and low temperature physics.

nodes.name: Lead
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS in enormous quantity from Britannia and Hispania. Cheap. The only common material that survives hot sulfuric acid.

nodes.name: Leather
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Bellows, seals, gaskets, drive belts.

nodes.name: Quicklime and slaked lime
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Mortar, glass flux, causticising, agriculture.

nodes.name: Linen
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Sailcloth, and the feedstock for rag paper.

nodes.name: Magnesium
nodes.note: Electrolysis of fused chloride. Light alloys, flashlight powder, reducing agent.

nodes.name: Manganese and ferromanganese
nodes.note: Deoxidises and desulfurises steel. Rome already mines the ore as a glass decolouriser without knowing it is a metal.

nodes.name: Mercury
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS from Almaden, an imperial monopoly. Pliny NH 33.118 price-fixes minium at 70 HS per pound.

nodes.name: Natron (sodium carbonate)
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS from Wadi Natrun. IT IS NOT SALTPETRE. This confusion has wrecked more bootstrap plans than any other single error.

nodes.name: Natural rubber
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. Hevea is Amazonian, but Landolphia and Funtumia vines in West and Central Africa yield real rubber and were the basis of a large industry in the 1890s. West Africa is COASTAL SAILING from the Pillars of Hercules and Hanno the Carthaginian did it around 500 BC. You need a voyage down a coast and the knowledge of which vine to tap, not an ocean crossing. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: New World crops
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. These are CROPS, not commodities: you need seed stock once and then you grow them forever. One successful voyage home with potato seed changes the caloric ceiling of European agriculture permanently. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Nickel
nodes.note: Not isolated in antiquity. Coinage, plating, alloy steels, glass-to-metal seals, catalysts.

nodes.name: Nitrocellulose
nodes.note: Guncotton and the base of smokeless powder, celluloid and film. Unstable if badly washed; several early factories destroyed themselves.

nodes.name: Nitroglycerin and dynamite
nodes.note: Absorbed into kieselguhr it becomes handleable. Mining and tunnelling output rises sharply. Also the most likely single thing in this document to kill you and everyone in the building.

nodes.name: Olive oil
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS in industrial quantity. Soap, lighting, quenching, varnish base. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Rag paper
nodes.note: Linen rags, retted, limed, beaten by a water-driven stamper, lifted on a wire mould. Cheaper than papyrus, far cheaper than parchment, and the substrate of everything in the information branch.

nodes.name: Papyrus
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. An Egyptian near-monopoly, which is a strategic reason to make paper.

nodes.name: Parchment
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Durable and dear.

nodes.name: Refined petroleum fractions
nodes.note: Mesopotamian and Caucasian seeps are workable without drilling. Fractionate into naphtha, kerosene, gas oil, lubricants, wax and residue. Kerosene lighting alone pays for the plant.

nodes.name: Platinum
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE. Colombian and Ural placers. The Urals are reachable overland through Scythian and Sarmatian trade without crossing any ocean. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Porcelain and high-fired stoneware
nodes.note: Kaolin plus feldspar at about 1300 C. Chemical ware, electrical insulators, and an extremely profitable luxury export that Europe chased for six centuries.

nodes.name: Pozzolana and hydraulic concrete
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS and it is better in seawater than Portland cement. Do not try to improve it.

nodes.name: Pyrolusite (manganese dioxide)
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS and already uses it as glassmaker's soap without knowing why.

nodes.name: Quinine from cinchona
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE, only Andean. Malaria is endemic around Rome, which makes this worth an ocean crossing by itself. Once you have it, TRANSPLANT it: the Dutch and British both moved cinchona out of Peru and broke the monopoly. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Salt
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS, taxed and strategically controlled. Feedstock for hydrochloric acid and the whole chlor-alkali branch.

nodes.name: Shellac (traded)
nodes.note: REACHABLE BUT DEAR. Indian Ocean trade via Berenice to Muziris, 1 to 3 year lead time. Your best varnish and the only good coil insulation you will have for a century.

nodes.name: Silk (traded)
nodes.note: REACHABLE BUT RUINOUS. Silk Road via Palmyra. Pliny complains of the bullion drain east. Your best early wire insulation.

nodes.name: Silver
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Cupellation from galena.

nodes.name: Stainless steel
nodes.note: Chromium above about 11% forms a self-healing passive oxide. Chemical plant, cutlery, vacuum systems. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.] [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_1600 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: steel with 11% chromium requires 1500-1600 C melting]

nodes.name: Sulfur
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS from Sicily and the Aeolian islands.

nodes.name: Synthetic rubber
nodes.note: YOUR ONLY ROUTE TO RUBBER. Butadiene from petroleum or from alcohol, polymerised. It sits behind a full petrochemical industry, which is why every plan that casually assumes rubber is wrong by about a century.

nodes.name: Tallow
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS. Lubricant for wire drawing and machining.

nodes.name: Tin
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS from Cornwall and Iberia. Expensive, long haul.

nodes.name: High speed and alloy tool steel
nodes.note: Tungsten and chromium carbides that hold an edge red hot. Multiplies every machine tool's output several fold.

nodes.name: Tungsten
nodes.note: Melts at 3422 C, the highest of any metal. Lamp filaments, high speed steel, carbide tooling. Needs the arc furnace or hydrogen reduction of the oxide followed by powder sintering.

nodes.name: Vitriols (iron and copper sulfates)
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS lying in heaps at pyrite mines as a weathering product, and has no idea what it is for. Feedstock for sulfuric acid.

nodes.name: Wool
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS.

nodes.name: Wrought iron (bloomery)
nodes.note: ROME HAS THIS at scale. Noricum is famous for it. Soft, tough, weldable, no useful casting.

nodes.name: Zinc metal
nodes.note: CRITICAL PATH AND ALMOST NOBODY SEES IT. Zinc boils at 907 C, below the temperature at which its ore is reduced, so the metal leaves as vapour and reburns at the furnace mouth. That is exactly why Rome makes brass by cementation and has never seen the metal. Seal the retort and condense downward. No zinc, no voltaic pile, no electricity.

nodes.name: Activated sludge treatment
nodes.note: Microorganism flocs oxidize organic matter; aeration essential; solids separation by settling; sludge recycling; process control critical

nodes.name: Adrenaline isolation
nodes.note: Takamine 1901 isolation; synthetic by 1906; cardiac and vascular effects; hypertensive crisis; added to local anesthetics for vasoconstriction

nodes.name: Agar culture media
nodes.note: Agar is the whole point and it is not obvious: gelatin melts at blood heat and is digested by the very bacteria you are growing, so plates liquefy overnight. Agar from red seaweed sets at 40 C, melts at 85 C and almost nothing eats it, which is why solid plate culture works at all. Mediterranean red algae (Gelidium) are available to Rome.

nodes.name: Anaesthetic machine
nodes.note: Cylinders, regulators, flowmeters, vaporizer, carbon dioxide absorber, reservoir bag, mask and circuit; precise mixing prevents hypoxia

nodes.name: Antitoxin serum therapy
nodes.note: Horse serum; diphtheria and tetanus antitoxins; immediate but transient protection; serum sickness from foreign protein

nodes.name: Appendicectomy
nodes.note: McBurney's point incision; ligation of appendicular artery; stump inversion; early diagnosis critical to prevent perforation and peritonitis

nodes.name: Systematic auscultation
nodes.note: Not just listening but cataloguing: rales, rhonchi, murmurs, clicks; correlation with pathology and prognosis

nodes.name: Autoclave sterilizer
nodes.note: Prevost and Junker's pressure vessel; 120 C at 2 atmospheres; spore kill vs vegetative cell; correct loading and cycles critical

nodes.name: Barbiturate sedatives
nodes.note: Barbital, phenobarbital, pentobarbital; intravenous and oral; dependence and withdrawal; narrow margin between sedation and respiratory depression

nodes.name: Basal metabolic rate measurement
nodes.note: Measured during fasting sleep; oxygen consumption or carbon dioxide production; thyroid function assessment; reproducibility requires strict conditions

nodes.name: Bioassay
nodes.note: In vivo measurement; reproducibility; refinement with statistical design; reduces animal use compared to crude testing

nodes.name: Tissue biopsy
nodes.note: Needle or punch biopsy; immediate fixation; staining and microscopy; diagnosis of malignancy, inflammation, infection without surgical exploration

nodes.name: Blinding in trials
nodes.note: Single blind subject only, double blind subject and investigator, triple blind adds assessor; unblinding for safety; masked capsules and injections

nodes.name: Blood bank and storage
nodes.note: Donor screening and testing; refrigeration at 4 C; citrate anticoagulation; shelf life limitations; coordinated supply for emergencies

nodes.name: Blood glucose measurement
nodes.note: Fasting baseline; response to glucose load; distinction between diabetes and hypoglycemia; Somogyi effect and brittle diabetes

nodes.name: Blood transfusion
nodes.note: Whole blood or separated components; indications for hemorrhage and anemia; citrate anticoagulation; compatibility testing beforehand

nodes.name: Blood typing and cross-matching
nodes.note: Landsteiner's groups; major and minor cross-match; agglutination reactions; hemolytic transfusion reactions from mismatch

nodes.name: Cadaver dissection
nodes.note: Legal cadaver supply from executed criminals and unclaimed poor; religious objections; reveals anatomy without speculation

nodes.name: Caesarean section
nodes.note: Lower segment transverse vs classical vertical; classical not repeated in later pregnancies; perimortem indication when vaginal delivery not safe

nodes.name: Case-control study
nodes.note: Odds ratio approximates relative risk; efficient for rare diseases; recall bias and selection bias risks; faster than cohort

nodes.name: Case record keeping
nodes.note: Standardized form and order; problem list; assessment and plan; longitudinal follow-up; quality of care measure

nodes.name: Case series analysis
nodes.note: Pattern recognition; natural history description; hypothesis generation; no control group; rapid publication possible

nodes.name: Cataract extraction
nodes.note: Intracapsular vs extracapsular; phacoemulsification came much later; post-operative aphakia managed with thick glasses

nodes.name: Catgut suture
nodes.note: Not cat but sheep or horse; prepared from submucosa; caliber standardization; chromic acid treatment for slower absorption

nodes.name: Cell as basic unit of life
nodes.note: Not just observation of cells under lens, but the theory that organisation is cellular throughout, not fibrous or humoral

nodes.name: Child health clinic
nodes.note: Vaccination records; growth monitoring; disease surveillance; screening for developmental delay; accident prevention counseling

nodes.name: Water chlorination
nodes.note: Free and combined chlorine; residual for distribution; trihalomethane formation from organic matter; hypochlorite solution easier than gas

nodes.name: Chromosome and heredity
nodes.note: Direct observation: chromosomes visible at meiosis and mitosis; map genes to chromosome locations

nodes.name: Circulation of the blood
nodes.note: Not that blood moves, but that it circulates: same blood returns to the heart, not consumed, and the quantity is small enough that arterial blood must reach veins via capillaries

nodes.name: Citrate anticoagulation
nodes.note: Citrate binds calcium needed for coagulation cascade; citrate toxicity from massive transfusion; later use in dialysis

nodes.name: Clinical thermometer
nodes.note: Standardized range 35-42 C, mercury bulb, constriction trap to keep mercury in place after withdrawal, readable in one minute

nodes.name: Cohort study
nodes.note: Prospective or retrospective; relative risk calculation; attrition and confounding challenges; expensive but strong evidence

nodes.name: Contact tracing
nodes.note: Case finding and source identification; quarantine placement; cohort management; resource-intensive but effective for containment

nodes.name: Contrast media
nodes.note: Barium swallow for GI tract; urography for urinary system; early iodine compounds for angiography; toxicity and allergic reaction gradually recognized [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Cystoscope
nodes.note: Fenestrated sheath; working channel for instrumentation; direct vision of trigone, ureteral orifices and mucosa

nodes.name: Differential white cell count
nodes.note: Blood smear stained and examined under oil immersion; neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils; left shift in infection

nodes.name: Digestive process
nodes.note: Not just mechanical grinding: chemical transformation by acid and ferments, absorption through intestinal wall

nodes.name: Digitalis glycosides
nodes.note: Withering's empirical observation; positive inotropic and negative chronotropic; narrow therapeutic window; digitalis toxicity from accumulation

nodes.name: DNA as hereditary material
nodes.note: Double helix structure; base pairing; information stored in sequence; DNA replication fidelity

nodes.name: Drug standardisation
nodes.note: Units of activity for biologics like insulin and antitoxin; animal testing for potency; variation in natural products

nodes.name: Electrocardiogram
nodes.note: String galvanometer initially; three standard bipolar leads; later six unipolar; PQRST waves; arrhythmias and ischemia visible

nodes.name: Electroencephalogram
nodes.note: Scalp electrodes; low voltage millivolt signals require vacuum tube amplification; alpha waves at rest; seizure spikes; sleep stages

nodes.name: Surgical electrocautery
nodes.note: Monopolar and bipolar designs; cutting current vs coagulation; minimal tissue damage vs spark coagulation; safety protocols for anesthesia [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Endocrine glands and hormones
nodes.note: Distinction between nervous (electrical) and endocrine (chemical) signaling; hormones as circulating chemical messengers

nodes.name: Rigid endoscope
nodes.note: Early versions for urethra and bladder; later gastroscopy; achromatic objective required; light source separate initially, then coaxial

nodes.name: Endotracheal intubation
nodes.note: Direct vision with laryngoscope; cuffed tube prevents aspiration; IPPV with mechanical ventilation; complications from prolonged intubation

nodes.name: Fluoroscopy imaging
nodes.note: Barium sulfate fluorescence visible in dark; lead glass shielding; carbon arc or tungsten target; image intensification came much later

nodes.name: Food purity legislation
nodes.note: Definition of adulterant; food standards; labeling requirements; enforcement and penalties; detection of substitutes

nodes.name: Frozen section histology
nodes.note: Specimen frozen in cryostat at -20 C; thin sections cut without embedding; rapid staining; intraoperative diagnosis for tumor margins and unexpected findings

nodes.name: Lung gas exchange
nodes.note: The kernel: lungs do not simply absorb blood like a sponge, they exchange gases across a thin barrier

nodes.name: Gastrectomy
nodes.note: For ulcer or malignancy; Billroth I and II anastomoses; blood supply from left gastric, right gastric and gastroepiploic vessels

nodes.name: Gene as unit of inheritance
nodes.note: Gene not mere bead on string but active agent; one gene one enzyme; mutation as change in gene

nodes.name: Haemocytometer
nodes.note: Precisely ruled counting grid; known depth; dilution factor; normal range and interpretation of anemia and polycythemia

nodes.name: Surgical haemostat
nodes.note: Pean, Kelly, mosquito; teeth and serrated jaws; spring handles; ratchet locking; arterial vs venous clamps

nodes.name: Hernia repair
nodes.note: Identification of defect; dissection of sac; return of viscera; fascial layer closure; recurrence common with simple suture alone

nodes.name: Hospital infection control
nodes.note: Hand hygiene; environmental cleaning; isolation precautions; sterilization of equipment; staff education and compliance

nodes.name: Immune system and antibodies
nodes.note: Specific immunity: different pathogens provoke different antibodies; second exposure produces faster response

nodes.name: Insulin extraction
nodes.note: Banting and Best 1921; pancreatic extract; purification; potency standardization in units; subcutaneous injection; insulin shock therapy

nodes.name: Iodised salt
nodes.note: Endemic goiter in iodine-poor regions; iodine content degrades with time; fortification acceptance varies culturally

nodes.name: Isolation hospital
nodes.note: Site isolation and water supply; large grounds for convalescence; design for natural ventilation; segregation by disease

nodes.name: Intravenous saline solution
nodes.note: Isotonic with plasma; no hemolysis; replaces losses from hemorrhage and dehydration; colloid vs crystalloid later debated

nodes.name: Kidney filtration
nodes.note: Not simple sieving; selective reabsorption of useful substances and variable water retention

nodes.name: Laryngoscope
nodes.note: Indirect laryngoscopy: angled mirror reflects light and image back; direct intubation for anesthesia came later

nodes.name: Surgical light source
nodes.note: Carbon arc initially; tungsten filament later; reflector geometry; color temperature; heat dissipation

nodes.name: Local infiltration anaesthesia
nodes.note: Initial cocaine; later procaine and lidocaine; epinephrine added for vasoconstriction and prolonged effect; nerve blocks more selective

nodes.name: Maternal health clinic
nodes.note: Screening for hypertension and proteinuria; dietary advice; postpartum hemorrhage and infection prevention; early detection of problems

nodes.name: Meat inspection
nodes.note: Visual and palpation; tuberculosis, anthrax, trichinosis detection; condemned meat; documentation of inspection

nodes.name: Medical journal publication
nodes.note: Priority claims and knowledge dissemination; peer review for quality; citation tracking; reproducibility and fraud detection

nodes.name: Medical licensing
nodes.note: Qualification standards; examination by peers; legal monopoly; disciplinary power; excludes charlatans but also innovation

nodes.name: Medical statistics
nodes.note: Hypothesis testing; confidence intervals; power calculations; multiple comparison corrections; software automation

nodes.name: Mendelian inheritance laws
nodes.note: Not blending but discrete particles; dominance and recessiveness; 3:1 and 9:3:3:1 ratios in crosses

nodes.name: Microbiology culture technique
nodes.note: Petri dishes with agar; colony morphology; Gram stain; culture identification; antibiotic sensitivity testing

nodes.name: Milk pasteurisation
nodes.note: Low-temperature long-time or high-temperature short-time; kills TB, brucella, campylobacter; spoilage organisms also reduced

nodes.name: Morphine isolation
nodes.note: Serturner's work; crystalline form; injection and oral routes; respiratory depression and addiction risks

nodes.name: Mortality table
nodes.note: Life expectancy calculation; actuarial science; insurance basis; improved sanitation and childhood survival change tables markedly

nodes.name: Mosquito bed net
nodes.note: Simple barrier; treated with insecticide for duration; major malaria control tool; high coverage critical for population effect

nodes.name: Nervous system structure and function
nodes.note: Not simple mechanical tubes but specialized tissue conducting electrical signals; distinction between sensory and motor nerves

nodes.name: Notifiable disease system
nodes.note: Surveillance for outbreaks; data collection; confidentiality protection; rapid reporting for emerging threats

nodes.name: Professional nursing
nodes.note: Nightingale training standards; apprenticeship in hospital; gender issues in recruitment; autonomy vs physician delegation

nodes.name: Ophthalmoscope
nodes.note: Helmholtz's coaxial light path: light source and observer on same axis; mirror with central hole; correct focus requires interpretation

nodes.name: Oral rehydration solution
nodes.note: WHO/UNICEF ORS; glucose-sodium cotransport in small intestine; as effective as IV therapy; salt ratio critical

nodes.name: Orthopaedic internal fixation
nodes.note: Plates, screws and wires; compression plating; timing of mobilization; infection and delayed union complications

nodes.name: Otoscope
nodes.note: Simple conical speculum plus lens; not just view but teach recognition of cerumen, infection, perforation, light reflex

nodes.name: Deep tank fermentation
nodes.note: Aeration and agitation; temperature and pH control; foaming control with silicone; corn steep liquor as nitrogen source; yield improvement over years

nodes.name: Freeze-drying penicillin
nodes.note: Vacuum and low temperature sublimation; water removal; stable powder form; reconstitution before injection; crystal structure preservation

nodes.name: Penicillin cultivation
nodes.note: Penicillium notatum on culture plates; broth fermentation; antibiotic activity in filtrate; scaling to deep tank fermentation

nodes.name: Percussion technique
nodes.note: Auenbrugger's method: tapping chest produces different notes over fluid, solid, air; requires training to distinguish

nodes.name: Pharmacopoeia
nodes.note: Prescription reference; legal authority; assurance of composition and quality; updated as new drugs appear and old ones refined

nodes.name: Improved pit latrine
nodes.note: Containment of fecal matter; prevention of contamination of water and food; ventilation for odor and fly prevention

nodes.name: Placebo control
nodes.note: Ethical constraints: cannot use placebo when proven treatment exists; placebo effect real but separate from pharmacological effect

nodes.name: Plant chemistry extraction
nodes.note: Solvent selection; concentration; crystallization; identity verification; standardization of final product

nodes.name: Plaster cast immobilization
nodes.note: Calcined gypsum and water; heat of hydration; padding for comfort; split cast to accommodate swelling; window for skin inspection

nodes.name: Quinine isolation
nodes.note: Pelletier and Caventou isolation; crystal form; bitter taste led to tonic water; cinchonism from high doses; synthetic substitutes later developed

nodes.name: Randomised controlled trial
nodes.note: Gold standard for efficacy evidence; eliminates selection bias; requires large sample sizes; protocol registration and monitoring critical

nodes.name: Self-retaining retractor
nodes.note: Balfour, Weitlaner designs; arms with adjustable blades; ratchet or screw adjustments; frees assistant for other duties

nodes.name: Salicylate and aspirin
nodes.note: Willow bark traditional; salicin to salicylate to acetylation; Bayer's aspirin; anticoagulant effect discovered later

nodes.name: Sand filtration
nodes.note: Biofilm layer (schmutzdecke) removes particles and pathogens; slow rate; microorganism breakthrough possible; pre-treatment needed

nodes.name: Separate sewage collection
nodes.note: Storm overflows during rain; prevents plant overload; but combined systems cheaper; infiltration and inflow challenges

nodes.name: Skin grafting
nodes.note: Full thickness vs split thickness; donor site must heal; vascularization of graft; autograft only option early; allograft rejection

nodes.name: Sphygmomanometer
nodes.note: Riva-Rocci cuff and column: cuff inflated until radial pulse disappears, pressure read from mercury manometer, deflation to systolic and diastolic points

nodes.name: Spinal anaesthesia
nodes.note: Bier and Corning puncture; level of blockade; hypotension and bradycardia; post-dural puncture headache; advantages over general for lower surgeries

nodes.name: Spirometer
nodes.note: Dry or water-sealed bell; volume displaced; obstructive vs restrictive pattern recognition

nodes.name: Methylene blue staining
nodes.note: Gram and acid-fast stain modifications; vivid blue color; bacteria and WBC visible; Ehrlich's discovery

nodes.name: Stethoscope
nodes.note: Laennec's tube: stiffened paper initially, then wood; acoustic coupling transforms inaudible vibrations to audible without stethoscope being nearly as gross as hands on chest

nodes.name: Streptomycin isolation
nodes.note: Waksman's screening; first effective TB drug; ototoxicity and renal damage at high doses; resistance development in monotherapy

nodes.name: Sulphonamide drugs
nodes.note: Domagk's work; competitive antagonism of para-aminobenzoic acid; Prontosil red dye prodrug; broad spectrum but streptococcal resistance

nodes.name: Sterile drape
nodes.note: Towels and sheets arranged in layers; fenestration to expose only site; edges kept moist to prevent microbial wicking

nodes.name: Surgical glove
nodes.note: Halsted's gloves: latex not yet vulcanized properly so degraded; talc powder inside for donning; protective not just of patient but of surgeon

nodes.name: Surgical gown
nodes.note: Initially ordinary cotton; later white linen for visibility of blood; design prevents microbial shedding from body; sleeves fully extended

nodes.name: Surgical facemask
nodes.note: Initially cloth; later gauze in layers; protection of surgical field from oral and nasal flora; not protection of wearer

nodes.name: Synthetic suture
nodes.note: Nylon monofilament; less inflammation than catgut; does not dissolve; surgical silk still used for specialized purposes

nodes.name: Thyroid hormone extract
nodes.note: Desiccated thyroid tissue; later synthetic thyroxine; monitoring with BMR or TSH absent; potency variability

nodes.name: Thyroidectomy
nodes.note: Iodine preparation to reduce vascularity; recurrent laryngeal nerve identification; hypoparathyroidism from inadvertent gland removal; thyroid storm crisis

nodes.name: Surgical tourniquet
nodes.note: Bloodless field enables fine dissection; time limit critical to prevent tissue necrosis; cuff pressure above systolic; Esmarch exsanguination

nodes.name: Skeletal traction
nodes.note: Pin or wire through bone; pulleys and weights; femoral traction for hip fracture; weeks of bedrest; skin care critical

nodes.name: Tuberculin test
nodes.note: Mantoux test: intradermal injection of purified protein derivative; delayed hypersensitivity reaction; induration size interpretation; active vs latent TB

nodes.name: Urinalysis
nodes.note: Specific gravity, pH, protein, glucose, ketones, bilirubin; crystals and casts under microscope; infection indicated by bacteria and white cells

nodes.name: Cholera vaccine
nodes.note: Killed phenol-treated organisms; mucosal immunity weak with injected vaccine; oral rehydration more life-saving than vaccination

nodes.name: Diphtheria toxoid
nodes.note: Formalin-detoxified toxin retains immunogenicity; more effective than killed organism; Schick test for immunity status

nodes.name: Pertussis vaccine
nodes.note: Whole cell killed vaccine; high fever and local reaction; acellular vaccine much later; maternal antibodies in infant protection

nodes.name: Plague vaccine
nodes.note: Killed bacillus; variable efficacy; antiplague serum more immediately useful; vector control reduces need for vaccination

nodes.name: Rabies vaccine
nodes.note: Pasteur's nerve tissue vaccine; duck egg culture later; post-bite series; timing critical before symptom onset

nodes.name: Smallpox vaccine
nodes.note: Jenner's cowpox observation; lymph from pustule; arm-to-arm transfer; lyophilization for storage; eradication by vaccination

nodes.name: Tetanus toxoid
nodes.note: Formalin inactivation of toxin; effective but slower than antitoxin; booster doses maintain immunity; wound prophylaxis combination with antitoxin

nodes.name: Typhoid vaccine
nodes.note: Heat-killed or chemical inactivation; partial protection; revaccination needed; enteric fever still endemic in poor sanitation

nodes.name: Yellow fever vaccine
nodes.note: 17D strain attenuation; long-lived immunity; dengue and other flaviviruses cross-protect partially; vector control still needed

nodes.name: Vector control
nodes.note: Mosquito, flea, louse identification; breeding site destruction; chemical insecticides; resistance development

nodes.name: Vital registration system
nodes.note: Legal proof of identity; cause of death requires physician; population denominator for rates; undercount in poor regions

nodes.name: Vitamin A and deficiency
nodes.note: Night blindness and xerophthalmia from deficiency; provitamin A in beta-carotene; hypervitaminosis A toxicity; fortification of milk

nodes.name: Vitamin B1 thiamine
nodes.note: Beriberi from deficiency; rice bran source; wet vs dry beriberi; Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome in alcoholism

nodes.name: Vitamin B12 cobalamin
nodes.note: Pernicious anemia from intrinsic factor deficiency; injected when oral absorption fails; only animal source; methylmalonuria in deficiency

nodes.name: Vitamin C ascorbic acid
nodes.note: Scurvy from deficiency; citrus and fresh fruit source; wound healing impaired; role in infection and immunity

nodes.name: Vitamin D cholecalciferol
nodes.note: Rickets from deficiency; cod liver oil source; sun exposure activation; secondary hyperparathyroidism in deficiency

nodes.name: Wassermann test
nodes.note: Antibodies in syphilitic serum fix complement; addition of sensitized RBC shows hemolysis or lack thereof; false positives in lupus and atypical pneumonia

nodes.name: X-ray radiography
nodes.note: X-ray tube, transformer for high voltage, cooling, filtration for soft rays, photographic plate exposure time; fluoroscopy followed

nodes.name: Amputation and prosthetics
nodes.note: Rapid limb removal to prevent gangrene. High mortality from shock and infection. Prosthetics of wood and leather follow for dignity and limited function.

nodes.name: Antitoxin and serum therapy
nodes.note: Serum from horses immunized with toxin. Diphtheria antitoxin reduced mortality from 50% to 20%. Anaphylaxis kills 1 in 1000. Passive immunity is temporary.

nodes.name: Aqueducts and public latrines
nodes.note: Rome has abundant clean water and sewage separation. This infrastructure is mature and the foundation for any public health improvement.

nodes.name: Asepsis, antisepsis, and steam sterilization
nodes.note: Asepsis: prevention of contamination. Antisepsis: chemical disinfection. Steam sterilization beats carbolic spray because it kills spores, not just surface germs. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_measure_temp added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: steam sterilization and high-pressure steam processing require temperature monitoring]

nodes.name: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid)
nodes.note: Acetylation of salicylic acid (from willow bark). Safer than salicylate because absorbed slowly. Reduces fever, pain, inflammation. Bayer trademark. [FIXED after independent audit: acetylation needs acetic anhydride, from acetic acid via wood distillation. Nitric acid was wrong and has been removed.]

nodes.name: Autoclave for steam sterilization
nodes.note: Sealed vessel with high-pressure steam at 120 C for 15 minutes sterilizes instruments. Requires precision engineering; leaks render it useless. [FIXED after independent audit: the heat rung was redundant with the high pressure steam prerequisite.]

nodes.name: Blood groups and transfusion
nodes.note: ABO typing discovered 1900. Before this, transfusion killed 1 in 5 from agglutination. Citrate prevents clotting. Saves haemorrhage victims.

nodes.name: Bone setting
nodes.note: Reduction and splinting of fractures. Success depends on immobility for weeks; infection is the main hazard.

nodes.name: Cataract couching
nodes.note: Displacement of opaque lens via a hollow needle, an ancient Roman technique. The rev is patient fees.

nodes.name: Clinical thermometer
nodes.note: Mercury in glass with fixed point at 37 C. Temperature tells severity of infection. Fever is sometimes the body fighting infection.

nodes.name: Case control and randomised controlled trials
nodes.note: Case control: backward look at exposure. Fast and cheap. Randomised controlled trial: random assignment to treatment or placebo, prospective, blind. Eliminates bias but takes years. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Cocaine from coca
nodes.note: NOT UNOBTAINABLE, only Andean. The first effective local anaesthetic. See data/world/geography.json for where it is and what reaching it costs.

nodes.name: Dentistry and high-speed drill
nodes.note: Electric motor driving high-speed burr removes decay and drills for filling. Eliminates hand-cranked slowness and pain.

nodes.name: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
nodes.note: Electrodes on chest and limbs, galvanometer recording heart's electrical activity. Detects arrhythmias and infarction. Requires stable power and shielded wiring.

nodes.name: Endoscope
nodes.note: Tube with lens at the far end, mirror to reflect light. Inspection of bladder, urethra, rectum. Illumination by candlelight makes diagnosis difficult.

nodes.name: Epidemiology, statistics, and vital registration
nodes.note: John Snow mapped cholera deaths (1854); they clustered around one well. Data beats theory. Vital registration (births, deaths, cause) is the denominator. Null hypothesis testing reveals truth.

nodes.name: Ether, chloroform, and nitrous oxide anaesthesia
nodes.note: Diethyl ether (first 1846) is explosive and irritates airways. Chloroform (1847) is smoother but causes cardiac arrhythmias in 1 per 3000. Nitrous oxide is safest but partial. Pain-free surgery is a miracle.

nodes.name: Forensic medicine and autopsy
nodes.note: Autopsy to establish cause of death. Time of death, toxicology, physical evidence. The state pays well for conviction support.

nodes.name: Bacterial culture and Gram staining
nodes.note: Petri's shallow agar dishes allow colonies to grow. Gram staining distinguishes by cell wall: crystal violet for gram-positive, red for gram-negative. Guides antibiotic choice. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_measure_temp added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: bacterial culture growth requires precise temperature control of incubation medium]

nodes.name: Handwashing protocol (Semmelweis)
nodes.note: Handwashing and instrument cleaning between autopsy and delivery. Maternal mortality dropped from 18% to 1% in Vienna 1847. The physician who discovered this was committed to an asylum.

nodes.name: Herbal pharmacy (Dioscorides Materia medica)
nodes.note: Dioscorides' Materia medica describes 600+ plants. Effective for many uses: willow bark for pain, elderflower for fever. The physician's reference work.

nodes.name: Hospital as an institution with records
nodes.note: Permanent structure with wards, admission records, diagnosis, treatment, outcome. Allows tracking disease patterns and training the next generation.

nodes.name: Hypodermic syringe and hollow needle
nodes.note: Glass or silver barrel with accurately bored needle. Intravenous injection becomes possible. Contamination of the needle kills; strict asepsis required.

nodes.name: Insulin extraction and purification
nodes.note: Extract from porcine pancreas, crystallize, purify. Banting and Best 1921. Before insulin, diabetes is death. Now: life and productivity.

nodes.name: Legal protection for physicians
nodes.note: Imperial edict: physicians who follow established methods are not liable for death. This requires establishing consensus on best practice.

nodes.name: Ligature over cautery for haemostasis
nodes.note: Tying off vessels with linen before cutting. Slower than cautery but less tissue damage and no scar contracture. Requires training to isolate arteries.

nodes.name: Medical education and cadaver dissection
nodes.note: Formal curriculum: dissection of cadavers, demonstration, case study. Rome forbids human dissection; physicians must apprentice illegally or learn abroad.

nodes.name: Microscopy in pathology with histology
nodes.note: Aniline dyes from coal tar make cells visible for the first time. Methylene blue, carmine, safranin stain bacteria and tissue. Identifies cancer, tuberculosis, syphilis. Beautiful dependency on the chemical branch.

nodes.name: Nursing as a trained profession
nodes.note: Formal training programme for nurses. Florence Nightingale proved competent nursing cuts mortality by half. The profession becomes medicine's backbone.

nodes.name: Nutrition, deficiency diseases, and vitamins
nodes.note: Scurvy (vitamin C), rickets (vitamin D), beriberi (thiamine), pellagra (niacin), goitre (iodine). Iodised salt eliminates endemic goitre. Vitamin concept emerges from analytical chemistry.

nodes.name: Antiseptic obstetrics and incubator
nodes.note: Handwashing before delivery, clean gowns, sterile towels. Puerperal fever drops from 25% to 2%. Incubator for prematurity: warm box with temperature control increases survival from 10% to 40%.

nodes.name: Obstetric practice
nodes.note: Manual assistance, podalic version, ergot to hasten delivery. Maternal mortality is 1-2%; assistance often makes it worse.

nodes.name: Ophthalmoscope
nodes.note: Mirror and lens to view the retina. Reveals aneurysms, cotton-wool spots, diabetic changes. Requires skilled assembly. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: lens and mirror optics require precision grinding]

nodes.name: Opium and mandrake tinctures
nodes.note: Poppy and mandrake extracts in oil, applied topically or given orally. Dosing is unpredictable; overdose causes death or stupor.

nodes.name: Penicillin extraction and purification
nodes.note: Penicillium mold produces beta-lactam antibiotic. Deep-tank fermentation and chromatography extraction are industrial operations. HONEST: this is not bedroom chemistry.

nodes.name: Quarantine, clean water, and sewage
nodes.note: Isolation of sick (quarantine). Filtration removes suspended matter. Alum coagulant precipitates colloids. Chlorination kills pathogens. Sewage separation and S-bend traps prevent backflow.

nodes.name: Saline and fluid resuscitation
nodes.note: Isotonic salt solution administered intravenously. Restores blood volume and prevents shock. Simpler and saves more lives than transfusion.

nodes.name: Spectacles and refraction testing
nodes.note: Ground lenses with trial frame testing. Corrects myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism, presbyopia. One of medicine's easiest wins.

nodes.name: Sphygmomanometer (blood pressure cuff)
nodes.note: Cuff inflated by hand, releasing air while watching mercury and listening to pulse. Requires precision machining and a mercury barometer.

nodes.name: Sterile technique
nodes.note: A complete ritual: sterile drapes, fields, gowns. No cross-contamination. Requires training and discipline. One careless move ruins everything.

nodes.name: Stethoscope and percussion
nodes.note: A rolled tube of paper or wood detects heart and breath sounds. Tapping the chest reveals fluid or consolidation. Simple but requires training to interpret.

nodes.name: Sulfonamides (sulfanilamide)
nodes.note: First broad-spectrum antibiotic 1935, derived from aniline dyes. Inhibits bacterial folate synthesis. Saves millions from streptococcal and gram-negative infections. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_measure_temp added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: sulfonation with concentrated acid is exothermic and requires careful temperature management]

nodes.name: Surgical gloves and mask
nodes.note: Linen gloves and mask tied over mouth and nose. Blocks droplets and protects patient. Cloth gloves absorb blood and require frequent changing. Rubber gloves are unobtainable.

nodes.name: Good surgical instrument kit
nodes.note: Rome already has reliable bronze and iron surgical blades, forceps, and spatulas. This is the baseline.

nodes.name: Trepanation
nodes.note: Drilling into the skull to relieve pressure or expel evil spirits. Infection and death are common; Rome will pay for emergency cases.

nodes.name: Vaccination: variolation to attenuated vaccines
nodes.note: Variolation: pus from smallpox pustule (0.5-2% death). Cowpox: Jenner's insight, much safer. Pasteur: heat or chemical attenuation for rabies, anthrax, cholera. Toxoids (diphtheria, tetanus) are safest. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Military field hospital (valetudinaria)
nodes.note: Permanent structure with wards, built adjoining barracks. The state mandates these for legions. Clean water, drainage, and isolation of contagion cut mortality by half.

nodes.name: Vector control and drainage for malaria
nodes.note: Malaria is endemic to Rome's marshes. Quinine is UNOBTAINABLE. Drainage of standing water eliminates mosquito breeding. Laborious but works.

nodes.name: Wound suturing
nodes.note: Linen thread with bronze needle, removing thread after 2-3 weeks. Works well for clean wounds.

nodes.name: X-ray imaging
nodes.note: Cathode ray tube generating X-rays to expose plates. Reveals fractures and foreign bodies. HONEST WARNING: repeated exposure causes burns and cancer. Protection is inadequate.

nodes.name: Secure mercury supply
nodes.note: Almaden is an imperial monopoly, so this is a political node before it is a technical one. Mercury gives you barometers, the Sprengel pump, mirrors and the first hard vacuum humans have ever had. Quantity sized for programme needs, not for trade: 400 kg of cinnabar yields roughly 300 kg of mercury, which is ample for barometers, thermometers, Sprengel pumps and a mirror works. Cinnabar is priced from Pliny NH 33.118. CORRECTION: this no longer requires the imperial mining concession. Cinnabar is traded across the Empire as the pigment minium and you can simply buy it and retort it yourself. The concession buys you BULK mercury cheaply, which matters later for mirrors and pumps, and it is a separate problem from getting your first kilogramme. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Acetylene from calcium carbide
nodes.note: Heat coke and lime to 2000 C in an electric furnace to make calcium carbide, then mix with water and collect the acetylene gas. The carbide reacts violently with water so the generator must be robust and well-designed or it leaks. Acetylene is unstable and cannot be pressurized above 2 atmospheres without risk of explosion, so it must be dissolved in acetone in a porous mass (a carbide lamp cartridge) for transport. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.] [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_3000 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: calcium carbide at 2000 C in electric furnace; current prerequisite insufficient]

nodes.name: Annealing and recrystallization
nodes.note: Heat work-hardened metal to a dull red and cool slowly. Atoms rearrange into stress-free grains and the metal becomes soft and ductile again. Must not overheat or grains grow coarse and the metal becomes brittle. The window is narrow—a difference of 50 degrees C makes the difference between a good anneal and scrap. Requires experience to recognize the right color.

nodes.name: Arc welding with electrode
nodes.note: Strike an arc between a consumable electrode and the work. The arc melts both the electrode and the parent metal; electrode metal and flux coat the weld pool. Much faster than oxy-acetylene and less sensitive to wind. Requires a DC power supply and reliable electrical grid. The flux coating prevents oxidation and lowers the melting point of the surface oxide, so the weld pools together instead of balling up.

nodes.name: Basic lining and the phosphorus problem
nodes.note: Bessemer's acid lining cannot remove phosphorus because both are acidic. Most European ores carry phosphorus which makes the steel cold-short (brittle when cold). Thomas and Gilchrist discovered that a basic (limestone) lining does remove phosphorus as slag, but it eats lining fast and requires obsessive maintenance. This one fact cost Bessemer years and made British iron obsolete until solved.

nodes.name: Blasting with black powder and dynamite
nodes.note: Drill a hole, tamp black powder down with sand, light a fuse. The explosion fractures the rock around it. Later, dynamite (nitroglycerin absorbed in kieselguhr) replaced powder: more powerful, more stable, but far more hazardous. The critical skill is calculating the powder quantity and hole depth to maximize fragmentation without wasting powder or causing a flyrock accident. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Chill casting and directional solidification
nodes.note: Insert copper or iron plates (chills) into the mold where you want fast cooling. Fast cooling refines grain and suppresses segregation. Works only if you understand that large grains are weak and fine grains are strong. The chill must be positioned precisely or it creates stress concentrations.

nodes.name: Continuous casting and ingot casting
nodes.note: Pour molten steel into an iron mold and let it cool into an ingot, then break the mold away. Continuous casting pulls the ingot from the mold as it sets, which reduces segregation and avoids the pipe (voiding) that ruins large ingots. The trick is copper-alloy molds that resist sticking and heat cycling.

nodes.name: Converter furnace for steel
nodes.note: Blast compressed air through molten iron-carbon; exothermic oxidation of silicon and carbon raises temperature while generating heat. Brittle and rapid—if the converter tips or the air supply fails during a heat, you have a disaster of molten metal on the floor. Speed and low labour cost per ton is the payoff. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_1600 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: molten iron oxidation furnace reaches 1600-1700 C]

nodes.name: Cupola furnace for iron casting
nodes.note: A small tall furnace that melts scrap and pig iron for casting into sand moulds. Much hotter than an open hearth because the stack draft is strong. The problem is contamination from coke ash unless you use charcoal and then your fuel bill is punishing. Solves small-batch casting need cheaply. [FIXED after independent audit: it was tier 1 while depending on the blast furnace, which is a major independent metallurgical leap.]

nodes.name: Deep drawing and pressing dies
nodes.note: Press a flat metal sheet with a die into a deep cup shape in a single stroke. The metal must be annealed and soaped to prevent sticking and tearing. Multiple draws with annealing between are needed for very deep cups. The challenge is uniform thickness—the metal flows unevenly and thin spots tear or wrinkle. Needs precision dies and pressure control.

nodes.name: Deep shaft sinking techniques
nodes.note: Going deeper than 200 meters requires support sets (timber or steel frames), continuous pumping of inflow water, adequate ventilation at depth, and precise control of powder charges to avoid enlarding the hole. The pressure of overlying rock increases shear stress on timbering. Major collapses are common. The time to sink a shaft grows non-linearly with depth—doubling depth more than quadruples time.

nodes.name: Die casting and hot chamber casting
nodes.note: Inject molten zinc or aluminum into a hardened steel die at high speed under high pressure. Cool rapidly and eject. Produces dimensionally consistent parts at high volume. The die cost is enormous and only amortizes over thousands of parts. Porosity from trapped gas is the chronic defect—degassing the metal before injection is essential.

nodes.name: Drawn tube production
nodes.note: Anneal a tube, coat with soap as lubricant, draw it through a die on a water-powered wire draw to reduce diameter and thicken walls uniformly. Much slower than rolling but gives excellent surface finish and precise dimensions. The soaped tube must be perfectly round or it jams in the die. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: wire-drawing die precision and resulting surface finish]

nodes.name: Drop hammer for heavy forging
nodes.note: Raise a heavy hammer by water power to a fixed height and drop it. The impact force is proportional to the weight and drop height. Allows forging of massive pieces that hand hammering cannot touch. The anvil must be buried deep in earth to absorb the recoil or the whole forge building shakes apart.

nodes.name: Dry sand molding for fine castings
nodes.note: Allow the mold to dry completely and fire it in a kiln to vitrify the clay bond. Produces precise smooth castings with clean surfaces. Much slower than green sand, the kiln step adds time and fuel cost. Used for fine machine parts, gears, and weapons where surface finish matters. Defects like scabs are less common than in green sand.

nodes.name: Dynamite and modern explosives
nodes.note: Three times more powerful than black powder per unit mass and much more reliable. Nitroglycerin is unstable and prone to detonation from shock, so it is absorbed in diatomite to stabilize it. Dynamite revolutionized mining and tunneling but also killed thousands during its development. A single accident in handling or storage is catastrophic. Must be stored separately from fuses and primers. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electro-refining for high-purity copper
nodes.note: Impure copper as the anode, pure copper cathode, in a sulfuric acid bath. Current causes impure copper to dissolve; pure copper plates out on the cathode; impurities settle as anode slime. Removes gold and silver efficiently, which is both a blessing (refining) and a problem (recovering those valuable metals from the slime takes more work). Produces 99.99 percent pure copper.

nodes.name: Electroplating and coating
nodes.note: Pass current through a solution of metal salt with the object as the cathode and a pure metal anode. Metal ions migrate to the cathode and deposit as a coating. Works only with a pure metal anode that dissolves at the same rate as plating proceeds. The deposit quality depends on current density and bath chemistry—too fast and it is rough and porous, too slow and it is slow and expensive.

nodes.name: Extrusion and the extrusion press
nodes.note: Push hot metal through a shaped die with a hydraulic press. The die mouth narrows, so the pressure rises enormously and plastic flow follows the die shape. Makes complex hollow sections impossible to roll or draw. Temperature is critical: too cold and the metal cracks, too hot and the die erodes. Each shape needs its own die, so tooling cost is high.

nodes.name: Fatigue testing and fracture mechanics
nodes.note: Cyclic loading of a specimen kills machines that passed static tests. A defect that lies dormant under steady load will grow under cyclic stress until the component fails suddenly. The S-N curve (stress vs cycles to failure) shows the safe stress limit below which fatigue is negligible. This is why railway axles must be inspected and discarded after a certain mileage even if they still look sound.

nodes.name: Fire assay for ore grade
nodes.note: Heat crushed ore in a cupel with lead, the base metals oxidize and are absorbed into the cupel, leaving a bead of precious metals. Works only if you understand that lead's affinity for impurities is the trick, and must be done at scale to check ore grade before large smelts. The assayer is the gatekeeper.

nodes.name: Froth flotation ore concentration
nodes.note: Grind ore to powder, mix with water and a collector chemical that makes valuable mineral surfaces hydrophobic. Bubble air through; mineral clings to bubbles and floats, waste sinks. This is non-obvious: you are separating by surface chemistry, not density. It transforms marginal ores into viable ones and is the one process that changed the definition of ore grade in the 20th century. Needs constant chemical supply.

nodes.name: Galvanizing with zinc coating
nodes.note: Dip clean iron into molten zinc. Zinc bonds metallurgically to iron and protects it from rust. The zinc-iron interface layer is hard and brittle; if you bend the bar sharply right after galvanizing it spalls and exposes the iron. Needs a pickling step with acid to remove rust and oxide before the dip, and flux (powdered chloride) to prevent oxidation of the zinc. [FIXED after independent audit: molten zinc is about 450 C, nowhere near a blast furnace. Zinc metal was also listed twice.]

nodes.name: Green sand molding for casting
nodes.note: Damp sand mixed with clay is packed around a wooden pattern and fired gently to harden the mold without drying it out completely. The trapped water flashes to steam when molten metal enters, creating a small gap and preventing fusion. Cheap and fast but produces rough castings. Rome has this baseline method.

nodes.name: Hardenability and alloy steel design
nodes.note: Adding chromium, nickel, molybdenum, or vanadium increases the depth to which a steel can be hardened. Thick bars that quench-harden only to the surface need alloy addition to harden through. Hardenability is separate from hardness—a hard steel is not necessarily hardenable to depth. Engineers design alloys to achieve both the hardness and the through-hardening needed for large bearings and gears.

nodes.name: Hardness testing and Rockwell scale
nodes.note: Press a hardened indenter (diamond pyramid or steel ball) into the metal under a known load, measure the impression size. Larger impressions mean softer metal. Rockwell scale standardizes the test so results are comparable across labs. Fast and non-destructive, so useful for acceptance testing. Gives a single number but does not reveal structure or ductility.

nodes.name: Hydraulic press and accumulator
nodes.note: A pump driven by steam fills a cylinder with oil; the incompressible oil presses a ram with immense steady force. An accumulator (air-charged vessel) smooths pulsation and stores energy. Pascal's law means a small pump can generate large forces through a large piston. The limit is seal quality and pipe strength; if oil leaks you lose pressure instantly. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: pressure seal quality and pipe strength require file and gauge precision machining]

nodes.name: Investment casting and lost wax
nodes.note: Carve fine details in wax, embed in clay and sand, fire to melt and drive out the wax, pour molten metal into the cavity. Results in intricate castings with no parting lines. Rome has this for jewelry. For large castings it becomes expensive in wax and labor but the precision is unmatched. The name investment refers to the clay-sand shell that receives the investment. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: Jigging and gravity separation
nodes.note: Shake crushed ore in a slurry in a funnel-bottomed box; dense ore sinks, waste rock suspends and overflows. The real work is tuning the shake frequency and water flow—too fast and you lose ore, too slow and waste carries through. This becomes faster and cheaper than hand sorting at scale.

nodes.name: Mannesmann piercing for seamless tube
nodes.note: Two conical rolls rotating towards each other pierce a heated bar and push the center material outward. Sounds impossible but works because the material is plastic when hot and the geometry of the rolls forces flow. The innovation is recognizing that the centerline is in pure tension and will fail there, opening a hole. This is a non-obvious geometric fact.

nodes.name: Metallography: polishing, etching and microscopy
nodes.note: Polish a section of steel to mirror smoothness, etch with dilute acid to reveal grain boundaries and phases, look through a microscope. The microstructure tells you if the heat treatment worked, if the segregation is acceptable, if cracks are present. This single instrument—the microscope—transformed metallurgy from craft to science. No expensive equipment needed: a microscope and an etchant are sufficient.

nodes.name: Mine pumping systems
nodes.note: Use water power to drive a Cornish engine or a Newcomen atmospheric engine, then a force pump lifts water from the lowest level. Deep mines fill with water faster than hand bailing can remove it. The pumping plant is the largest single capital expense of a deep mine—without it, you cannot go deeper than about 100 meters. The pump must run constantly during operations.

nodes.name: Normalizing for uniformity
nodes.note: Heat to redness and cool in still air. Not as soft as full annealing but grain is fine and uniform. Normalizing after forging relieves working stress and prepares the metal for hardening or final machining. The open air cooling means no fuel cost for the cool-down phase. Used after every significant deformation to reset the structure.

nodes.name: Open hearth furnace and scrap recycling
nodes.note: A large reverberatory basin where you can melt pig iron, scrap, and iron ore together at controlled temperatures. Much slower than a converter but gives you time to remove impurities chemically. The furnace can recycle scrap and burnt parts that a converter wastes. Fuel cost is higher but flexibility is the gain.

nodes.name: Ore dressing: crushing and hand sorting
nodes.note: Breaking ore by hand and gravity-separating visible rich and waste rock is unchanged since antiquity. The skill is recognizing which rock will pay: this is entirely empirical and learned from the ground itself. Rome needs labour, not invention.

nodes.name: Oxy-acetylene welding and brazing
nodes.note: A flame from acetylene and oxygen burning at 3000 K melts both the filler rod and the parent metal, joining them. Works on steel, copper, and aluminum. The flame is small and precisely controllable, so you can weld thin sheet or repair castings. Safety requires careful regulator tuning: reverse flow into acetylene generator causes explosion. The acetylene supply infrastructure is the bottleneck.

nodes.name: Iron-carbon phase diagram as scientific knowledge
nodes.note: Map the regions of phase stability as a function of temperature and carbon content. Shows transformation temperatures (critical points where austenite, ferrite, cementite appear or vanish). This transforms blacksmith's empirical heat-color craft into predictable science. The diagram is the foundation of all intelligent steel making; without it you are working blind even if your hands are skilled.

nodes.name: Pneumatic rock drill
nodes.note: A small piston driven by compressed air strikes a hardened bit repeatedly against rock, advancing into the hole while the operator rotates it slightly between blows. Drills much faster than hand drilling with hammer and chisel. The air compressor must be driven by steam and the hose is heavy and expensive. Enables deep blast holes that hand drilling never could achieve, transforming mining efficiency.

nodes.name: Powder metallurgy and sintering
nodes.note: Tungsten cannot be melted and cast (melting point 3420 C). The only path to a tungsten object is: powder, press into a shape under high pressure, then sinter (heat just below melting at high temperature in a hydrogen atmosphere) to bond the particles. This is the sole way to make tungsten into anything usable. The sintered part is porous and brittle until you press it again.

nodes.name: Quenching media and quench crack prevention
nodes.note: Cool speed determines hardness: fast quench in water is maximum hardness but causes cracks, slow quench in oil is lower hardness but safer. The quench crack forms because the surface hardens and shrinks while the core is still hot and soft, creating tensile stress. Brine quenches faster than water. Control of temperature drop rate is the art. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Rail mill production
nodes.note: Roll steel billets into the precise section and straightness demanded by railways. Straight track depends on rails within tolerance. The section mill can produce the profile but the end straightness and the weld joint (joining two rails end-to-end) are where most waste happens. Needs close process control and sorting of bad rails.

nodes.name: Resistance welding and spot welding
nodes.note: Clamp the work between two copper electrodes and pass current through it. Resistance heating melts a small zone where the overlap is, forming a weld nugget. Works only on sheet metal and thin stock. No filler, no gas, fast and clean. The electrodes must be soft copper with high conductivity or they overheat and wear. Spot welding revolutionized automotive body assembly.

nodes.name: Reverberatory furnace
nodes.note: The charge sits on the hearth, flames from a separate firebox bounce off an arched roof and melt the metal. Fuel never touches the charge—this is the crucial difference from a blast furnace. Enables puddling and copper refining because slag does not contaminate with coke ash. The roof must be shaped right or it cracks under thermal shock.

nodes.name: Reversing rolling mill
nodes.note: Motor reverses direction between passes. Steel goes through in one direction, emerges, is turned, fed back through in the opposite direction. Allows many passes at speed without the labour of flipping. Electric motor with reversing controller is essential; a steam engine cannot reverse fast enough without danger.

nodes.name: Roasting and calcining ore
nodes.note: Heat ore in an open pile to drive off volatile sulfur and water, and to crack the rock for easier reduction. Many sulfide ores cannot be smelted without roasting first; the roast fumes are toxic. Needs a scholar to understand empirical craft proportion or roasters waste half their ore. [FIXED after independent audit: the word stoichiometry is anachronistic for a tier 1 node; Richter is 1792. Ancient roasters worked by craft knowledge.]

nodes.name: Safety lamps and mine ventilation
nodes.note: A closed lamp with a wire gauze that absorbs heat from a methane flame, cooling it below the ignition point, so the flame does not ignite the gas in the mine but you can still see the methane by the color change. Water-driven ventilation fans push air into the mine through one shaft while another shaft lets stale air escape. Both are essential: the lamp tells you gas is present, the ventilation dilutes it to safe levels.

nodes.name: Section mill for rails and beams
nodes.note: Rolls are shaped to press the bar into a desired section: I-beam, T-rail, angle iron. Each pass uses different rolls, so the bar gradually forms. Temperature control is critical because the metal must be plastic enough to flow into the roll valleys without tearing. Very high forces mean the rolls must be backed by strong housings or they will sag and kill accuracy.

nodes.name: Spectroscopic assay of metals
nodes.note: Excite a metal sample with an electric spark and analyze the light with a spectroscope. Each element produces specific lines; the intensity tells you concentration. Fast and requires minimal sample preparation. Can be done in the foundry during a heat to verify alloy composition before pouring. The spark gap must be precisely positioned and the spectroscope aligned or results scatter wildly.

nodes.name: Steam hammer for precision forging
nodes.note: Steam cylinder pushes the hammer down instead of dropping it. You control force and speed with the steam valve, not gravity, so you can forge delicate shapes without cracking. Far more work per hour than a drop hammer. The hazard is that steam can fail suddenly and the hammer drops uncontrolled; strong dies and guides are essential.

nodes.name: Tempering and temper color chart
nodes.note: Heat hardened steel to a lower temperature to relieve quench stress and reduce brittleness. The temperature is judged by the surface oxide color: pale straw, brown, dark blue. Too low a temper leaves it brittle, too high softens it too much. Color tempering is a visual art that has been refined over centuries. The temper color chart is portable and teachable knowledge.

nodes.name: Tensile testing and the testing machine
nodes.note: Grip a specimen in a powered machine, pull it apart, measure the load and elongation. Plot load vs elongation to find yield strength, ultimate strength, and elongation to failure. The testing machine must pull at constant rate with a load cell accurate to 1 percent or the data is worthless. This data is the only way to verify that specifications are being met; without tests you cannot know if a batch of steel is good.

nodes.name: Three-high rolling mill
nodes.note: Three rolls arranged so the middle roll reverses between passes. Bar goes down between bottom and middle, then back up between middle and top, then down again. Doubles throughput without a reversing mechanism. The middle roll is under enormous load from both sides and must be extraordinarily hard or it will deflect and produce bad gauging.

nodes.name: Tin plate production
nodes.note: Electroplate iron sheet with tin or dip into molten tin. Tin is non-toxic and corrosion-resistant, so tinned steel is ideal for food storage. The tin coating must be continuous or rust starts at the pin-holes. Electroplated tin plate is thinner and cheaper than dipped; dipped is thicker but more durable. The difference is in the tin-iron bond strength. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_heat_0700 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: molten tin dipping at 232 C within pottery kiln range]

nodes.name: Trip hammer and water-driven forge hammer
nodes.note: A cam on a water wheel shaft lifts a heavy hammer, then the cam releases it and gravity and the impact do the forging work. Much faster than hand hammering and the work is uniform. The key is that the head must be hard iron or the repeated impact will deform it; case-hardening is necessary to survive. Rome has this; it is the foundation of heavy forge work.

nodes.name: Tube mill and seamless tube production
nodes.note: A seamless tube that holds pressure is the only solution for hydraulics and high-pressure steam. Mannesmann's innovation: two rotating conical rolls pierce the center of a heated bar as it passes between them, then a sizing mandrel expands the hole and the formed tube to size. Requires precise balance and speed control; one roll wobble ruins the batch. The seamless tube transformed high-pressure technology.

nodes.name: Two-high rolling mill
nodes.note: Two iron rolls, one fixed, one movable, crush hot steel bar between them. The bar emerges thinner and longer. Needs rolls of sufficient hardness and a power source that does not stall under load—cast iron rolls are barely adequate and shatter under shock; hardened steel rolls are better but hard to make. The steel must be hot enough to flow without cracking. Getting the temperature, roll gap, and feed speed in balance is an art.

nodes.name: Water-powered ore stamp mill
nodes.note: Cam-driven stamps powered by a water wheel crush ore in a mortar far faster than hand crushing. The bottleneck is the cam and the hardness of the iron stamp-heads. Needs high-carbon iron or case-hardened steel. This is where labour-displacement troubles the guild.

nodes.name: Winding engine and mine shaft hoisting
nodes.note: A steam engine driving a large reel with steel wire rope hoists ore and workers from depth. The rope must be wire, not hemp, or it breaks under load and falls into the shaft. The brake must hold the maximum load suspended or a rope failure is a catastrophe. Regular inspections for wear and fraying are essential; a frayed rope is a widow-maker.

nodes.name: Wire rod rolling mill
nodes.note: A series of small oval and round rolls progressively thins a bar into coiled wire rod, which is then drawn to final size. The wire emerges hot and coils as it cools. The speed is high—modern mills run at meters per second—so you need strong power and excellent roll material or the rolls will crack and scatter pieces. A single roll failure at speed can cause line shutdown for a day.

nodes.name: Adhesive bonding
nodes.note: Used for wood and leather. Not for metal under load. Gap-filling is possible but joint is only as strong as the adhesive.

nodes.name: Air gauge
nodes.note: Compressed air flows through a restrictive jet into the bore. Pressure is read on a gauge. Size is inferred from pressure. Fast and non-contact; used for 100 percent inspection. Settable to 0.01 mm.

nodes.name: Anodising
nodes.note: Aluminum is the anode; oxide layer grows into the metal. Thickness is 0.01 to 0.1 mm. Can be dyed. Hardness is high; wear resistance is good.

nodes.name: Arbor
nodes.note: A shaft held in the spindle, stepped to fit different cutter bores. Runout at the cutter is critical. Often uses a tapered nose for indexable tools.

nodes.name: Arc welding with bare electrode
nodes.note: Arc melts both electrode and base metal. Metal oxides form and contaminate the weld. Bare weld is porous and brittle. Later, coated electrodes cover this defect.

nodes.name: Arc welding with coated electrode
nodes.note: Flux shields the arc and produces a slag that protects the molten metal. The slag is chipped off after cooling. Weld is stronger and less porous than bare electrode.

nodes.name: Moving assembly line
nodes.note: The line speed is set by the slowest station. Balance is critical; idle stations waste capacity. Ford introduced this for automobiles; it requires complete standardisation.

nodes.name: Automatic screw machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um to cut the control cams accurately. MAKES cap_tol_100um and sometimes cap_tol_10um. Once programmed by the cam, runs untended. Setup time is days. Scrap rate from cam error is the problem.

nodes.name: Bill of materials
nodes.note: Exploded from drawings. Used for procurement and assembly. Must be updated when design changes. One assembly may contain hundreds of parts.

nodes.name: Blueprint process
nodes.note: Original is drawn on translucent linen. Contact print on blueprint paper produces white lines on blue. Copies are made at copying house. One master feeds 50 machines.

nodes.name: Brazed tool tip
nodes.note: Brazing carbide tips directly to steel has a thermal expansion mismatch that causes failure. The invention is using a brass layer that stretches to absorb the difference without cracking.

nodes.name: Brazing
nodes.note: Filler melts at 900-1000 C but does not melt the base metal. Strong joint by wetting and capillary action. Flux is essential to remove oxides.

nodes.name: Broaching machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (tool precision). MAKES cap_tol_100um on internal shapes. Keyways, splines, and complex internal profiles in one stroke. The broach pulls through the hole; each tooth cuts 0.1 mm. High force, one pass only.

nodes.name: Buffing and polishing
nodes.note: Final finish for inspection or appearance. Removes fine scratches. Does not correct form errors. Labor-intensive; operator skill affects consistency.

nodes.name: Cam lobe profile cutting
nodes.note: Cams control the sequence of operations. Profile error of 0.1 mm causes misfeeds or collisions. Cutting is slow; inspection by optical comparator is essential.

nodes.name: Carbon steel cutting tools
nodes.note: Carbon steel, hardened and tempered blue, works to about 500 C tool face before softening catastrophically. Mushet steel adds tungsten and vanadium to push this to 600 C, but is expensive and brittle.

nodes.name: Cemented carbide
