nodes.note: Tungsten carbide is hard at 1500 C. Cobalt binder keeps it from shattering. The tooling is not steel: it is ceramic sintering, which demands vacuum furnace or inert atmosphere. Cost is ten times HSS, but speed gain is five times and tool life is infinite until breakage.

nodes.name: Centreless grinder
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (wheel axes alignment). MAKES cap_tol_10um. The workpiece floats between the wheels, supported only by grinding pressure. No setup needed; feed parts in continuously. Taper control is by tilting the regulating wheel.

nodes.name: Change order
nodes.note: Customer-driven or engineering-discovered. Each change is approved, costed, and scheduled. Affects inventory, work in progress, and tools. Traceability is recorded.

nodes.name: Chip formation
nodes.note: The invention is understanding that metal removal is a shear process at the tool face, not a crushing. Built-up edge is a protective phenomenon, not a defect. Chip curl and control is geometry, not magic.

nodes.name: Cold riveting
nodes.note: Cold is weaker than hot but faster. Used for thin sheet and small fasteners. Die must be tight or the rivet head is deformed.

nodes.name: Collet chuck
nodes.note: Collet grip depends on taper angle and pull distance. A 5-degree taper holds round bar within 0.01 mm runout. Spring back in the sleeve means one pull distance only.

nodes.name: Comparator
nodes.note: A lever and pivot system magnifies dial motion 10 or 100 fold. Reads 0.001 mm easily. Used for quality inspection and machine calibration. Sensitivity requires a light touch.

nodes.name: Compound die
nodes.note: The blank punch and trim punch are on one ram; the strip is pierced and blanked simultaneously. Pressure must be balanced or the part shifts and the hole is off-center.

nodes.name: Control chart
nodes.note: Plotted means and ranges show when process is drifting. Samples of five parts, measured every hour. Chart is hand-drawn. When average moves outside control limits, stop and adjust. Saves scrap.

nodes.name: Core box
nodes.note: Cores are made separately, baked, and dropped into the mould cavity. The core box defines the core shape; precision here determines hole accuracy. Cores are more expensive than sand.

nodes.name: Cutting fluid
nodes.note: Oil cools and lubricates the chip and tool. Tallow smokes less but is slower. Water-based emulsion is dangerous because it causes sudden tool failure, but is cheaper. The right choice depends on the material and speed.

nodes.name: Cutting speed and feed
nodes.note: Speed is not instinctive: go too fast and the tool melts, too slow and it wears by diffusion. The rule is empirical and depends on tool material, workpiece material, and coolant. Taylor measured hundreds of cuts to find the relationship.

nodes.name: Cylindrical grinder
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (spindle, workhead and tailstock centers). MAKES cap_tol_10um easily and cap_tol_1um with practice. The workpiece rotates between centers; the wheel traverses along it. Roundness depends on center alignment.

nodes.name: Deep drawing press
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (punch and die precision, blankholder pressure). MAKES drawn shells. The blankholder prevents wrinkling in the flange. The die and punch must be polished to reduce friction.

nodes.name: Dial indicator
nodes.note: Lever and pinion mechanism converts 0.01 mm motion to one full rotation of the dial. Used to check runout, alignment, parallelism. Repeatability is 0.01 mm but linearity is poor past range.

nodes.name: Die set
nodes.note: Guide posts and bushings keep punch and die aligned. Clearance between punch and die is the specification. Die sets are modular; the press changes only the top and bottom dies.

nodes.name: Dimensioning and tolerancing conventions
nodes.note: Defines basic size, deviation, fit type. All operators read from the same playbook. Reduces ambiguity that causes scrap.

nodes.name: Dividing engine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (worm pitch, wheel bore). MAKES cap_tol_100um on gear blanks. Accurate gear generation depends on indexing precision. Once calibrated, divisions repeat exactly.

nodes.name: Drawing office
nodes.note: One source of truth. Drawings are issued to shop floor only after approval. Changes are tracked. Library of standard parts. Three draftsmen can support 200 workers.

nodes.name: Drop hammer
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die alignment, frame rigidity). MAKES die tolerance. No precision mechanism; it is all gravity and inertia. The frame must be massive to avoid vibration.

nodes.name: Electroplating
nodes.note: Cathode is the part; anode is the coating metal. Current and duration control thickness. Nickel is 0.02 mm, chromium is 0.01 mm. Pre-cleaning is critical. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Enamelling
nodes.note: Enamel powder is dusted or sprayed onto the part, then heated to 700-900 C. Shrinkage mismatch causes cracking if not managed. Appearance is high gloss.

nodes.name: Engine lathe
nodes.note: An engine lathe NEEDS cap_tol_10um to build itself (lead screw, spindle bearings). Once built, it MAKES cap_tol_100um easily and cap_tol_10um with care. The spindle is the constraint: runout comes from bearing play and spindle sag.

nodes.name: Escapement lever mechanism
nodes.note: Holds position between strokes, advances one station per cycle. Timing must be precise or the next tool collides with work. Spring return must be repeatable.

nodes.name: Extrusion press
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die precision, container alignment). MAKES extruded sections. The workpiece is forced through a shaped die. Temperature control is critical; too cold and it breaks, too hot and it flows unpredictably.

nodes.name: Flash butt welding
nodes.note: Two parts are brought together under pressure. Current causes localized melting and expulsion. Parts are then upset together. Used for end-to-end joints in rails and tubes.

nodes.name: Flux
nodes.note: Borax is best for braze and forge. Rosin is used for electronics. Salt is crude but works. Flux residue must be cleaned or it causes corrosion.

nodes.name: Forge welding
nodes.note: Borax flux prevents oxidation. Pieces must reach the same temperature or the joint will crack. Skill is high; success rate for large joints is 70 percent.

nodes.name: Forging press
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die precision). MAKES forgings to die shape. Stroke and pressure must be repeatable. The dies heat from forging; life is limited.

nodes.name: Four-jaw chuck
nodes.note: Four independent jaws are turned by hand-tightened keys. Setup is slower but concentricity can be dial-indicated to 0.01 mm. Better for irregular workpieces.

nodes.name: Galvanising
nodes.note: Hot-dip is cheap but uneven. Thickness is 0.05 to 0.1 mm. Flux must be used to prevent oxidation in the bath. Parts are shaken to remove excess.

nodes.name: Gear grinding machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle, index). MAKES cap_tol_1um on tooth flanks. Used to grind gears after hardening. Heat-treat distortion is corrected. Tooth surface is smooth, low noise.

nodes.name: Gear hobbing machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle sync, index precision). MAKES cap_tol_100um on gears. The hob is a worm gear; as it turns, the workpiece indexes automatically. Tooth form is a spiral, not a straight line.

nodes.name: Gear shaper
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (runout, index precision). MAKES cap_tol_100um on gears. The cutter is shaped like a gear; it reciprocates in mesh with the workpiece. Slower than hobbing but simpler, better for internal gears.

nodes.name: Go/no-go gauge
nodes.note: Two gauges: one that must fit, one that must not. Simpler than a micrometer, faster on the floor. Accuracy is binary, not analog. Used for inspection at the machine.

nodes.name: Height gauge
nodes.note: Measures height above a flat surface to 0.1 mm. Used with an angle plate to check dimensions on irregular parts. Needs a flat reference surface.

nodes.name: Honing machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (bore precision before honing). MAKES cap_tol_1um. Honing follows grinding to correct distortion and improve finish. The stone conforms to bore geometry; pressure and stone grade control stock removal.

nodes.name: Horizontal jig borer
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um. MAKES cap_tol_10um. Better for deep holes because the spindle sits level and chips fall freely. Symmetry is harder to hold because the bar cantilevered is longer.

nodes.name: Horizontal milling machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um. MAKES cap_tol_100um easily. The horizontal spindle reaches into deep pockets. Face milling and end milling on the same machine. Simpler than universal mill, less flexible.

nodes.name: Hot riveting
nodes.note: Rivet is heated red-hot, inserted into aligned holes, and upset by a hammer or press. Stronger than cold riveting. Skill is needed to heat correctly without burning.

nodes.name: High speed steel research
nodes.note: The invention is empirical: tool steel with tungsten, molybdenum, vanadium and cobalt, heated red-hot then air-cooled in a specific way. Cuts three times faster than Mushet, holds hardness to 1000 C. Taylor and White took years of trial and measurement to find the window.

nodes.name: High speed steel tools
nodes.note: At HSS speed, traditional cast-iron machines shake and tool holders break. A whole infrastructure must rebuild: more rigid machines, more balanced spindles, better bearings. The bottleneck is not the tool, it is the platform.

nodes.name: Hydraulic press
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (seal precision, valve lands). MAKES large force over small displacement. Leakage is the killer; seals must be tight and piston rod concentricity within 0.1 mm.

nodes.name: Indexable insert
nodes.note: The breakthrough is geometric: chipbreaker geometry cast into the carbide die itself. When one edge dulls, rotate the insert. No resharpening. Tool room cost drops to nearly zero.

nodes.name: Indexing head
nodes.note: A worm and wheel drive indexed by a pin in a circle of holes. Divisions are exact; an 80-tooth wheel and 40-tooth worm gives 160 positions. Universal heads tilt for helical work.

nodes.name: Internal grinder
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (spindle, wheel runout). MAKES cap_tol_10um and cap_tol_1um with care. The wheel spins at high speed inside a bore. Clearance is tight. Used for hardened bearing bores and cylinder walls.

nodes.name: Inventory and reorder point
nodes.note: Reorder point accounts for lead time and usage rate. Too high and money is tied up. Too low and production stops. Manual ledger is slow; calculation is simple arithmetic.

nodes.name: Japanning
nodes.note: Traditional for machinery. Two or three coats, each baked. Provides protection and appearance. Slower than painting but harder finish.

nodes.name: Lapping machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (initial precision). MAKES cap_tol_100nm on flat surfaces and mirrors. Lapping removes only 0.001 mm per hour. Used for optical flats and gauge blocks. The operator checks progress by interference bands.

nodes.name: Magnetic chuck
nodes.note: For grinding and milling only; the piece must be magnetic steel. Flat magnetic chucks hold to within 0.05 mm runout. Switching on and off takes seconds.

nodes.name: Maintenance department
nodes.note: Scheduled oil changes, bearing checks, belt replacement. Machine breakdowns are catastrophic; prevention is cheaper. Daily rounds by maintenance crew. Spare parts are stockpiled.

nodes.name: Mandrel
nodes.note: A simple tapered shaft; the workpiece bores are pressed onto it. Runout depends on bore tolerance and taper fit. Expanding mandrels use a tapered sleeve inside the bore.

nodes.name: Casting mould
nodes.note: The mould is made of compacted sand held in a flask. A pattern is pressed into the sand and withdrawn, leaving a cavity. The core sits inside and defines internal holes.

nodes.name: Multi-spindle automatic
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um for spindle indexing and cam cutting. MAKES cap_tol_100um. Six pieces in work at once means sixfold throughput. The spindles must run in exact synchrony or they jam and break.

nodes.name: Mushet steel tooling
nodes.note: Air-hardens without quenching. Holds hardness to 600 C, double the speed of carbon steel. The speed gain does not come free: breakage is higher and geometry must be precise.

nodes.name: Optical comparator
nodes.note: Illuminated workpiece cast onto ground glass at 50x magnification. Check holes, threads, edge radius, form. Accuracy is limited by light diffraction. Used for tool inspection and quality audits. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Orthographic projection and drawing conventions
nodes.note: Top, front, side views show all dimensions needed. Operator does not interpret; numbers are clear. Standardization means a drawing from one factory is readable anywhere.

nodes.name: Oxy-acetylene welding
nodes.note: Melts steel and fills the gap with filler rod. Speed and quality depend on flame control. Overheating causes carbon loss and brittleness. Cooling rate must be slow or cracks form.

nodes.name: Painting
nodes.note: Surface preparation is 80 percent of quality. Dust must be removed. Paint thickness should be even. Multiple coats improve coverage and durability.

nodes.name: Pattern and shrinkage allowance
nodes.note: Iron shrinks about 0.5 percent as it cools. The pattern is made 0.5 percent larger. Brass shrinks 0.3 percent. If the pattern is wrong, every casting from it is wrong.

nodes.name: Phosphating
nodes.note: Chemical conversion coating, 0.001 to 0.01 mm. Improves paint adhesion and rust resistance. Produces distinctive gray or tan surface. Fast process.

nodes.name: Pickling
nodes.note: Iron parts are soaked in acid after heat-treat or forge. Scale dissolves. Temperature and time control removal rate. Parts must be rinsed immediately or they rust.

nodes.name: Piece rate payment
nodes.note: Worker is motivated to speed production. Quality must be monitored separately. Disputes over rate fairness are common. Requires accurate timekeeping and inspection.

nodes.name: Planer
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (bed flatness and alignment). MAKES cap_tol_100um easily. The workpiece is fixed and the tool head moves over it. For surfaces larger than a shaper can reach.

nodes.name: Plug gauge
nodes.note: Two plugs: one slightly smaller (go), one slightly larger (no-go). The hole must accept the go and reject the no-go. Simple and fast.

nodes.name: Press brake
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die parallelism). MAKES bend angles to die specification. Springback depends on material and thickness. A mechanical stop on the ram controls bend depth.

nodes.name: Production schedule
nodes.note: Balances demand, inventory, machine loading, and worker availability. Changes mid-month cause chaos. Lead time is built in. Revision cycle is weekly or monthly.

nodes.name: Profile milling machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (follower accuracy). MAKES cap_tol_100um. A tracer head follows a template or master while the cutter follows. Cam lobes, turbine blades, gear teeth. Setup is slow, production is fast.

nodes.name: Progressive die
nodes.note: The strip indexes one station per stroke: blank, pierce, draw, trim, form. One operator feeds stock. Setup is expensive but production is fast and scrap is low.

nodes.name: Punch press
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die precision, table flatness). MAKES holes to die tolerance. Punches must be hardened and precisely ground. Clearance between punch and die is critical for clean holes.

nodes.name: Quality department
nodes.note: Separate from production to avoid bias. Audits process at machines and in receiving. Finds root causes of defects. Reports to management. Drives continuous improvement.

nodes.name: Radial drill
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (spindle runout). MAKES cap_tol_100um. One operator can drill dozens of holes in a large casting without moving the casting. The radial arm means the spindle can reach anywhere.

nodes.name: Rake and clearance angles
nodes.note: Rake reduces cutting force and heat; clearance allows the tool to enter without rubbing. The tradeoff is tool strength. Geometry alone saves 30 percent power and doubles tool life.

nodes.name: Resistance seam welding
nodes.note: Rollers rotate and advance at synchronised speed, pulsing current. Creates a sealed seam. Used for tanks and pipes. Overlap of nuggets makes the seam.

nodes.name: Resistance spot welding
nodes.note: Two copper electrodes clamp the sheet. High current for 0.1 seconds melts a nugget. Electrodes must be cooled between welds. Timing and pressure are critical. Used for mass-produced sheet parts.

nodes.name: Ring gauge
nodes.note: Two rings: one slightly larger (go), one slightly smaller (no-go). The shaft must fit the go and be rejected by the no-go. Worn hand tools are checked this way.

nodes.name: Roll former
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (roll concentricity). MAKES formed sections to roll profile. Multiple roll stations bend progressively. The feed rate and roll gap control the final shape.

nodes.name: Rotary table
nodes.note: A heavy cast table with T-slot and dial. Worm and wheel indexing or continuous servo drive. Used for large castings and forgings where an indexing head cannot reach.

nodes.name: Sampling inspection
nodes.note: Specified sample size and acceptance number. If defects exceed limit, reject the lot. Faster than 100 percent inspection. Risk is quantified: alpha and beta errors.

nodes.name: Sand blasting
nodes.note: Cheaper than shot. Faster removal of rust and scale. Health hazard from silica dust. Nozzle wears quickly. Surface finish is rougher.

nodes.name: Sawing machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (blade tension, guide precision). MAKES no precision requirement. The saw must not deflect or wander. A dull blade generates heat and burns the cut.

nodes.name: Shaper
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (table flatness, side clearance). MAKES cap_tol_100um. Uses a single-point tool in a long stroke, slower than milling but simple. The table must move in a dead-flat plane or surfaces will be concave.

nodes.name: Shearing machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (blade clearance, table flatness). MAKES straight edges. The blade angle prevents shock. Clearance between blades must be exact or the shear is rough.

nodes.name: Shot blasting
nodes.note: Shot is recirculated. Removes scale and rust. Creates compressive stress in the surface, improving fatigue life. Expensive equipment but fast cleaning.

nodes.name: Silver soldering
nodes.note: Joint is stronger than soft solder and more ductile than braze. Used for jewelry, instruments, and small precision parts. Gap must be 0.1 mm.

nodes.name: Sine bar
nodes.note: Tilting a sine bar sets an angle precisely using shim stack height and trig. Checks angular tolerances. Cylinders must be ground concentric and parallel to 0.01 mm.

nodes.name: Slotter
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um. MAKES cap_tol_100um. Vertical stroke cuts keyways, T-slots, and internal keyways that a shaper cannot reach. The stroke must be perfectly vertical.

nodes.name: Snap gauge
nodes.note: Two adjustable anvils on a spring handle. Fast inspection of diameters, widths, thicknesses. Feel is everything; training is needed for reproducibility.

nodes.name: Soft soldering
nodes.note: Filler wets and fills the joint. Weak in shear but adequate for plumbing and sheet-metal seams. Flux prevents oxidation. Must be cleaned after soldering or corrosion occurs.

nodes.name: Spinning lathe
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (spindle runout). MAKES pressed forms, no precision requirement. The workpiece rotates at low speed; the artisan uses a hand tool and stake to flow the metal. Skill and timing are everything.

nodes.name: Standard hour
nodes.note: If standard is 100 pieces per hour and a worker makes 120, efficiency is 120 percent. Used to pay piece rates fairly. Rates must be updated when methods change.

nodes.name: Stellite tools
nodes.note: Cast at high temperature as a powder-sintered alloy. Harder than HSS but more brittle. Holds hardness to 1200 C. Used for roughing where speed matters more than tool life.

nodes.name: Submerged arc welding
nodes.note: Wire feed is automatic; flux is poured on. Arc is invisible beneath the flux. Very clean; minimal spatter. Used for large structural welds. Quality is high but equipment is complex.

nodes.name: Superfinishing machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (initial bore). MAKES cap_tol_100nm on cylinder walls and bearing journals. The stone vibrates in place while the bore rotates slowly. Surface finish becomes mirror-smooth.

nodes.name: Surface grinder
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (spindle runout, bed flatness). MAKES cap_tol_10um easily and cap_tol_1um with care. The workpiece rides on a chuck. Wheel dresses itself or is dressed manually. Parallelism is automatic.

nodes.name: Thread gauge
nodes.note: Checks both pitch and form. Go and no-go rings or plugs. Thread gauges are more expensive than plug or ring gauges because the form must be cut exactly.

nodes.name: Three-jaw chuck
nodes.note: The scroll is a spiral groove; rotating the key slides all three jaws in or out simultaneously. Concentricity is within 0.1 mm. Jaw inserts are replaceable.

nodes.name: Time study
nodes.note: Multiple runs, average cycles. Normal pace and foreign elements identified. Accounts for fatigue and personal time. Builds the standard hour.

nodes.name: Tolerance and limit system
nodes.note: Basic, deviation, upper limit, lower limit. Fits are loose, normal, tight. Code them once in a standard book. Every drawing references the book. Variation is managed by tolerance, not by selection.

nodes.name: Tool and cutter grinder
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (fixtures, wheel trueness). MAKES cap_tol_100um on tools. The fixture holds the tool at the correct angle for rake, clearance, flank relief. Critical for tool sharpening because geometry is not forgiving.

nodes.name: Tool room
nodes.note: Tools are issued by requisition, returned by EOD. Sharpening is scheduled. Inventory is by category. One tool room supports 50 machines.

nodes.name: Tumbling
nodes.note: Media is ceramic or steel balls. Slow but gentle. Burrs and sharp edges are removed. Edge radius increases by 0.2 mm. Batch size must be large for economy.

nodes.name: Turret lathe
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um and cap_tol_100um. MAKES cap_tol_100um reliably. The turret lets one worker load stock and walk away for a complex sequence: bore, face, part off, repeat. Each job needs a new setup, which takes hours.

nodes.name: Universal milling machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle, table travel). MAKES cap_tol_100um and cap_tol_10um with care. The table can be tilted, the spindle can be vertical or horizontal, the arbor can be extended. Dozen operations without setup.

nodes.name: Upsetter
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (station precision). MAKES headed bolts to tolerance. Wire is fed, cut, and headed in one machine. The header dies close around the wire and the ram rises through them.

nodes.name: Vertical jig borer
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle runout, XY precision). MAKES cap_tol_10um. Used to bore holes in jigs and tooling to high precision. The table must move in a straight line within 0.01 mm over a metre.

nodes.name: Vertical milling machine
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um. MAKES cap_tol_100um. Better sightlines than horizontal. Pockets and cavities are simpler because the tool is directly above. Less powerful than horizontal for heavy cuts.

nodes.name: Wire drawing bench
nodes.note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die concentricity). MAKES round wire to diameter tolerance. The die must be hard and the wire must be annealed between draws or it breaks. Emeritus is the traditional die material.

nodes.name: Work study
nodes.note: Observation identifies unnecessary motion. Methods are redesigned. Work is simplified so skill requirements drop and training is faster. Productivity gains of 20 to 40 percent.

nodes.name: Micrometer, verniers, gauge blocks, go/no-go gauges
nodes.note: Measurement precedes manufacture. Publish your standards and distribute copies of the master gauges to every workshop you fund, or your parts will not interchange between cities.

nodes.name: Compound microscope with achromatic objective
nodes.note: Do not build this before the bead microscope. A bad compound instrument is worse than a good single lens, which is exactly why van Leeuwenhoek won for fifty years. Needs lead flint glass for the achromatic doublet.

nodes.name: Aerial camera
nodes.note: Fixed camera in aircraft or balloon taking photographs of landscape. Analysts study prints for enemy positions. Repeatable, accurate, less vulnerable than observers to small arms fire.

nodes.name: Aerial reconnaissance
nodes.note: Aircraft or balloon observing enemy positions, calculating range and bearing. Transmits by telephone or radio to artillery. Enables fire beyond line of sight.

nodes.name: Aircraft carrier
nodes.note: Warship with flight deck and aircraft. Replaces battleship as capital ship. Range and lethality determined by aircraft, not guns. Naval battles fought by planes beyond visual range.

nodes.name: Aircraft catapult
nodes.note: Steam-powered shuttle accelerates aircraft to flying speed in short distance. Allows heavier aircraft and full fuel loads. Enables launch with bomb and fuel load from moving ship.

nodes.name: Ammunition standardisation
nodes.note: Single cartridge specification across all rifles in army. Simplifies supply, enables ammunition interchange. Same powder, bullet, brass for all units. Doubles logistics efficiency.

nodes.name: Anti-aircraft gun
nodes.note: Rapid-fire gun on rotating mount with high elevation angle. Feeds ammunition by belt. Requires predictor to aim ahead of aircraft. Effective only in large numbers. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Anti-tank ditch
nodes.note: Wide, deep ditch impassable to tanks. Steep sides prevent crossing. Requires sappers to bridge. Labor-intensive but effective when combined with mines and gun positions.

nodes.name: Armoured car
nodes.note: Light armoured vehicle on wheels. Faster and lighter than tank, requires good roads. Carries machine gun and crew. Suited for reconnaissance and internal security.

nodes.name: Armoured cruiser
nodes.note: All-steel hull with partial belt armour. Fast enough to catch merchant ships, heavily armed. Cruises distant stations. Loses to battleship in combat but cheaper to build.

nodes.name: Armoured cupola
nodes.note: Rotating steel dome houses gun and protects crew. Face-hardened armour resists artillery shells. Allows 360-degree fire. More expensive per gun than casemate.

nodes.name: Arrester wire
nodes.note: Steel cables across deck, aircraft hook catches wire to slow landing. Hydraulic or spring damping prevents jerking pilots. Enables landing on pitching flight deck in seconds.

nodes.name: Arsenal and interchangeable manufacture
nodes.note: The arsenal and interchangeable manufacture of small arms - Enfield rifles from Woolwich, Springfields from Springfield Armory, Mausers from Oberndorf. Jigs and fixtures ensure parts fit any rifle. Enables mass replacement of damaged weapons.

nodes.name: Artillery carriage
nodes.note: Timber frame with wheels and trail spike. Cradle holds trunnions, allows elevation and traverse. Must be robust enough for road movement and firing stresses. Becomes larger with more powerful guns.

nodes.name: Artillery piece
nodes.note: Cannon cast in bronze or iron, requires sustained 1300 C furnace and careful cooling. Replaces trebuchets. Wall-battering capability becomes political.

nodes.name: Artillery shell
nodes.note: Hollow iron sphere filled with black powder and fitted with fuse. Bursts on impact. Different from solid shot, extends damage area beyond direct hit. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: ASDIC
nodes.note: Acoustic sonar using ultrasonic waves. Detects submarine by echoes. Requires trained operator to interpret. Revolutionary for anti-submarine warfare. Makes surface ships able to find and attack submerged vessels. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Atomic bomb
nodes.note: The atomic bomb as a single node with an honest statement: requires the isotope separation and reactor programme it needs and the fact that it is the one node in this tree whose use is a mass atrocity. Hiroshima and Nagasaki killed 150,000-200,000 civilians, mostly instantly. Nuclear weapons end conventional warfare through deterrence. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Ballistic rocket
nodes.note: Liquid or solid fuel rocket follows ballistic trajectory. Reaches targets beyond artillery range. Difficult to intercept in flight. Changes strategic targeting doctrine. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Barbed wire
nodes.note: Steel wire with sharp barbs, strung between posts. Cheap to produce and deploy. Impedes infantry advance and creates predictable fire zones. Dominant defensive obstacle.

nodes.name: Bastion
nodes.note: Angled stone structure jutting from wall allows cannon to fire along curtain, eliminating dead ground. Acute angle makes it harder to breach. Replaces round tower.

nodes.name: Battlecruiser
nodes.note: Battleship guns and armour but faster by sacrificing belt thickness. Intended to outrun battleships while catching cruisers. Vulnerable in battle when facing fully-armoured opponents.

nodes.name: Belt feed system
nodes.note: Cloth or steel belt carries linked rounds to feed mechanism. Eliminates magazine changes, extends firing duration. Enables crew-served weapons with sustained fire roles. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Bolt-action rifle
nodes.note: Rotating bolt with cam-operated locking, opened and closed by hand lever. Repeats rapidly and runs within tolerances. Becomes the dominant rifle design because it is simple, robust, and fast. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Bomb, general purpose
nodes.note: Streamlined iron casing with explosive charge and impact fuse. Falls from aircraft. Fragmentation pattern and crater size depend on casing thickness and bursting charge.

nodes.name: Bomb sight
nodes.note: Optical and mechanical system for calculating bomb release point. Accounts for altitude, airspeed, wind, and gravity. Mechanical computers solve ballistics equations. Dramatically improves accuracy.

nodes.name: Bomber aircraft
nodes.note: Larger aircraft carrying bomb load and defensive guns. Requires fighter escort against enemy fighters. Strategic bombing campaign against factories and cities. Needs radar and navigation aids.

nodes.name: Breech block
nodes.note: Wedge or interrupted thread closes rear of barrel for breech-loading. Sliding or screw-in designs differ in speed vs seal. Requires precision tolerances to prevent gas leakage and chamber rupture. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Breech-loading rifle
nodes.note: Loading from the rear of the barrel eliminates need for ramming. Soldier can load from prone position or behind cover. Triples sustained fire rate and changes infantry tactics from advance to entrenchment. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Metallic cartridge
nodes.note: Brass case contains powder, primer, and bullet in one unit. Self-contained; does not leak or absorb moisture. Requires precision manufacture but enables reliable rapid fire. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Paper cartridge
nodes.note: Powder and ball wrapped in paper tube, carried at the hip. Quadruples loading speed compared to separate powder horn and pouch. Transformation of fire rate through ammunition packaging. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Casemate
nodes.note: Vaulted gunroom inside fortification, protected by stone and concrete. Guns fire through embrasures. Protects crew from enemy fire while operating guns. Becomes standard in 19th century.

nodes.name: Centrefire primer
nodes.note: Percussion compound in center of cartridge base, struck by firing pin rather than edge. Enables breech block design and rapid mechanical operation. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Chain Home radar network
nodes.note: The chain home idea - distributed radar stations reporting to central control centre which directs fighters. Early warning gives time to scramble interceptors. Won the Battle of Britain. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Chlorine gas weapon
nodes.note: Chlorine and phosgene and mustard as weapons with an honest note on what they did - chlorine gas released upwind of trenches. Causes choking and lung damage. Casualties and demoralisation disproportionate to deaths. Introduced April 1915. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Mustard gas
nodes.note: Blistering agent that damages skin and mucous membranes. Oily liquid, persists in soil and clothing. Casualties mount over days as soldiers do not realise exposure until burns appear. Deadliest chemical of the war. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Phosgene gas
nodes.note: More toxic than chlorine. Causes pulmonary oedema, soldiers drown in fluid from their own lungs. More difficult to detect by smell, lulls victims into complacency. Called cocainised gas by soldiers. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Concrete fortification
nodes.note: Portland cement concrete resists artillery better than stone and is cheaper. Can be cast in place quickly. Allows reinforcement by iron bars or steel. Modern fortifications are mostly concrete.

nodes.name: Conscription and reserve
nodes.note: Conscription and the reserve - compulsory military service produces trained reserve of millions. Mobilised in 1914, European armies grew from 2 million to 15 million within months. Trench warfare consumes manpower at unsustainable rates.

nodes.name: Cordite
nodes.note: Nitrocellulose extruded into stick form with petroleum jelly as binder. Consistent burn rate, no dust, stores without separation. British standard ammunition propellant. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Corned gunpowder
nodes.note: Corning is what makes gunpowder work at all. Smaller, denser granules with better ingredient distribution burn faster and generate higher pressure. The critical step between unreliable and practical.

nodes.name: Cryptanalysis
nodes.note: Breaking enemy ciphers by systematic analysis. Enigma machine broken by Polish and British cryptanalysts. Ultra intelligence shortened war by years. Single intelligence source changes strategic decision-making.

nodes.name: Depth charge
nodes.note: Explosive charge in steel canister, detonated by pressure fuse at set depth. Attacks submarines that cannot be reached by gun. Concussion in water is highly destructive.

nodes.name: Destroyer
nodes.note: Fast ship designed to hunt and destroy torpedo boats. Carries torpedoes itself and some artillery. Becomes primary fleet escort ship. Designed to counter the threat it was born from.

nodes.name: Dive bomber
nodes.note: Aircraft that dives steeply to release bomb at low altitude for accuracy. High g-forces on pilot and aircraft structure. Accurate against small targets like ships. Effective against tactical targets.

nodes.name: Dreadnought
nodes.note: The dreadnought and the all-big-gun idea - uniform main battery, all secondary guns removed. Higher speed than previous battleships, longer range artillery. Made all earlier battleships obsolete.

nodes.name: Face-hardened armour
nodes.note: Hardened steel face with tough steel back. Impact on hardened face shatters projectile while backing absorbs energy. Lighter than solid plate for same protection.

nodes.name: Field telephone
nodes.note: Telephone for battalion and company command. Connects front line to artillery. Enables real-time adjustment of fire. Requires cable laying and maintenance under fire. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Fighter aircraft
nodes.note: Fast manoeuvrable aircraft with multiple guns. Engages enemy aircraft in combat. Requires skilled pilot training and logistics. Control of airspace determines ground tactical options.

nodes.name: Fire control computing
nodes.note: Mechanical calculator using differential gears solves ballistic equations. Predicts future position of moving target, accounts for wind. Enables engagement of fast warships. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Fire control director
nodes.note: Central control station receives rangefinder and compass data, calculates firing solution for multiple guns. Synchronizes fire from battery. Naval ships use this to hit moving targets. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Flamethrower
nodes.note: Pressurised tank of burning petroleum with ignition system. Sprays flame 30-40 meters. Clears trenches and bunkers. Operator vulnerable during reload. Demoralising effect exceeds practical damage. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Flintlock mechanism
nodes.note: Flint held in cock strikes steel frizzen, sparks fall into priming pan. More reliable than wheel lock, simpler than both, dominant by 1700. Enables fast aimed fire. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Forward observer
nodes.note: Soldier at front observes and communicates adjustments by telegraph or radio. Allows gunners to fire without line of sight. Feedback loop enables rapid correction.

nodes.name: Quick match
nodes.note: Sulfur accelerates burn rate reliably. Enables faster priming sequences and synchronized multi-gun barrages in artillery. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Slow match
nodes.note: Saltpetre-soaked cord burns at a steady rate, allowing a musketeer to ignite the touchhole without a spark steel. The slow match tether extends to modern range.

nodes.name: Artillery fuse designs
nodes.note: Time fuse burns at set rate to burst in air, percussion fuse detonates on impact, mechanical fuse uses spring striker. Fuse choice determines how shell fragments are distributed. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Gas mask
nodes.note: Charcoal filter and glass eyepieces allow breathing filtered air. Early models inadequate against phosgene and mustard. Better filters developed by 1916. Makes chemical gas less decisive. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: General staff
nodes.note: Permanent peacetime cadre of professional military planners. Plans campaign strategy, logistics, and mobilisation. Prussian innovation copied by all great powers.

nodes.name: Glacis
nodes.note: Sloped ground in front of fortification. Denies attacker cover and lets defenders fire down. Attackers climbing upslope are exposed. Cheap to construct compared to stone walls.

nodes.name: Guided bomb
nodes.note: Bomb with radio receiver and control surfaces. Radio operator in aircraft steers bomb to target. Dramatically increases accuracy. Operator must see bomb fall, limited by smoke and darkness.

nodes.name: Machine gun synchroniser
nodes.note: The machine gun synchroniser is why it is a genuinely clever piece of timing. Mechanical cams or hydraulic valve time gun fire to gaps in propeller blades. Allows firing through propeller without damage.

nodes.name: Gunpowder foundation
nodes.note: ROME ALREADY HAS THIS. Saltpetre, charcoal, sulfur mixed in open vessels. Unreliable, separates in transport, cannot sustain rapid fire.

nodes.name: Half-track vehicle
nodes.note: Wheels in front for steering, tracks in rear for power. Lighter than tank but terrain-capable. Carries troops or specialised equipment. Faster than tracked vehicle on roads.

nodes.name: High explosive shell
nodes.note: Bursts by impact detonator rather than burning fuse. Nitroglycerin or dynamite inside creates pressure wave that demolishes fortifications. Changes fortification design completely. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Howitzer
nodes.note: Intermediate angle gun between mortar and cannon. Longer range than mortar, higher angle than gun. Breech loading enables fast fire. Becomes dominant field artillery. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: IFF system
nodes.note: Identification Friend or Foe - radar transponder in aircraft responds to interrogation. Allows ground radar to distinguish friendly from enemy aircraft. Eliminates tragic friendly fire incidents. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Incendiary bomb
nodes.note: Bomb filled with burning petroleum or white phosphorus. Ignites buildings and structures. Scattered from aircraft in quantity. Creates firestorms in wooden-built cities. Destroys civilian housing.

nodes.name: Incorporating mill
nodes.note: Water-powered wet incorporation of ingredients at scale. High explosion risk during operation and storage, hence remote location requirement and danger premiums for workers.

nodes.name: Indirect fire
nodes.note: Gun crew calculates aim without seeing target, firing over obstacles and terrain. Requires forward observer to report and adjust. Tripled effective range of artillery.

nodes.name: Ironclad
nodes.note: Wooden hull with iron plate bolted to sides, steam-powered. Immune to cannon fire from other wooden ships. Requires dock infrastructure for repair. 1860 revolution in naval warfare.

nodes.name: Jet fighter aircraft
nodes.note: Gas turbine jet engine replaces piston and propeller. Much higher speed and altitude capability. Requires more fuel per hour but outpaces propeller-driven fighters completely.

nodes.name: Lever-action rifle
nodes.note: Lever under stock cycles bolt and chambers round. Allows fast fire from shoulder without bolt manipulation. Preferred for practical shooting because dominant hand never leaves grip. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Logistics as discipline
nodes.note: Scientific study of supply, transportation, and distribution. Quantity calculations, transportation networks, storage facilities. Armies succeed or fail on logistics more than tactics.

nodes.name: Machine gun, gas-operated
nodes.note: Taps gas from barrel rear to drive piston. More controllable than recoil operation, runs cooler. Becomes preferred design for sustained fire roles because cooling load is lower. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Machine gun nest
nodes.note: Reinforced position for machine gun with interlocking fields of fire. Gun crew protected by concrete and guns. Key to trench defense. Can hold line with few troops.

nodes.name: Machine gun, recoil-operated
nodes.note: Recoil of firing cycle works the bolt. Bolt cycles faster than hand can move, enabling sustained fire. Requires cooling and ammunition supply. Changes tactics from cavalry to entrenchment. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Magazine
nodes.note: Spring-loaded box stores cartridges and feeds them upward to chamber. Enables rapid fire without manual feeding. Magazine design determines whether rates of fire double or triple. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Matchlock mechanism
nodes.note: Serpentine arm holds lit slow match and pivots into touchhole by trigger lever. Simpler and cheaper than wheel lock, becomes dominant for musketeers because ammunition availability matters more than convenience. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Minesweeper
nodes.note: Small vessel with dragging equipment or electromagnetic coil to detonate mines safely. Wooden hull to minimize magnetic signature. Essential for protecting shipping lanes and fleet movement.

nodes.name: Minie ball
nodes.note: Conical lead projectile with hollow base. Skirt expands under powder gas to grip rifling, then sheds when leaving barrel. Combines ease of loading with stability from rifling. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Mortar
nodes.note: Short barrel on fixed pivot fires at high angle over walls. Simplest gun, most robust, slowest. Chamber is conical. Low muzzle velocity means it does not need recoil control.

nodes.name: Napalm
nodes.note: Jellied petroleum that sticks to skin and burns. Developed late in World War 2. Continues burning after impact, causing severe burns. Area denial weapon that fills woods and buildings. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Naval mine
nodes.note: Buoyant sphere or cylinder containing explosive charge, triggered by contact or electrical current. Sinks ships silently. Danger persists after war ends. Forces careful navigation of coastal waters.

nodes.name: Observation balloon
nodes.note: Tethered balloon holding observer above battlefield. Sees enemy movement and artillery target locations. Vulnerable to artillery and aircraft. Telephone line to ground crew.

nodes.name: Operational research
nodes.note: Scientific analysis of military operations to optimise doctrine and tactics. Statistical study of aircraft attrition rates, convoy losses, and radar effectiveness. Improves resource allocation.

nodes.name: Percussion cap
nodes.note: Mercury fulminate in small copper cup detonates reliably when struck by hammer. Replaces flint-spark with chemical ignition, enabling breech-loading and faster fire. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Periscope
nodes.note: Tube with prisms that allows viewing from below water surface. Enables targeting while submerged. Right-angle optics crucial for practical submarine attack. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Pillbox
nodes.note: Low concrete bunker with gun ports, designed to be nearly immune to artillery. Garrison of 4-6 can hold for hours. Difficult to assault frontally due to wide fields of fire.

nodes.name: Plate armour against firearms
nodes.note: Plate armour against firearms and why it lost - musket balls penetrate at medium range, weight exceeds cavalry endurance, cavalry becomes less viable. By 1700, infantry with muskets dominates armoured cavalry.

nodes.name: Powder mill
nodes.note: Water-powered pounding mills for consistent granule production at scale. First application of water power to military supply.

nodes.name: Proximity fuse
nodes.note: Radio tube in shell detects reflected signal from aircraft, triggers detonation at closest approach. Creates lethal radius without direct impact. Transforms air defense effectiveness. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Radar
nodes.note: Radiofrequency pulses detect aircraft at distance. Cathode ray tube display shows bearing and range. Enables detection through clouds and darkness. Changes air defence from visual tracking to radar guidance. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Railway timetable mobilisation
nodes.note: The railway timetable as mobilisation instrument - detailed train schedules transport armies to frontier in days. Prussia mobilised in 14 days in 1866. Russian delays in 1914 cost the war. Coordination of five mobilisation timetables impossible without telegraph.

nodes.name: Range table
nodes.note: Computed tables show elevation and powder charge for distance. Eliminates trial-and-error ranging. Based on ballistic equations. Single table distributed to hundreds of guns.

nodes.name: Rangefinder
nodes.note: Optical stereo matching measures distance to target. Baseline typically 1-2 meters. Accuracy within 100 meters at 10 km. Enables first-shot hits. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Ravelin
nodes.note: Detached angled structure in front of curtain with its own garrison. Allows firing from front and sides, makes breaching the main wall harder. Additional layer of defense.

nodes.name: Recoil mechanism
nodes.note: The recoil mechanism is what lets a gun stay aimed between shots, which multiplies rate of fire far more than any improvement to the barrel. Hydraulic and spring system absorbs energy smoothly. French 75 mattered because it was the first truly quick-firing gun. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Revolver
nodes.note: Rotating cylinder with six chambers. Simple mechanical operation, requires no magazine. Cylinder indexing requires precision tolerances. Sidearm of choice for cavalry and officers. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Rifling
nodes.note: Helical grooves in barrel impart spin to projectile, stabilizing flight and improving accuracy beyond 100 yards. Cost in barrel wear and loading complexity offset by lethal accuracy at range. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Self-loading pistol
nodes.note: Recoil or blowback operates slide to cycle bolt. Magazine holds 8-10 rounds. More complex than revolver but faster reloading. Becomes standard military sidearm after 1900. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Self-propelled gun
nodes.note: Artillery gun mounted on tracked chassis with armour. Mobile fire support that travels with infantry. Protects gun crew from machine gun fire. Becomes main fire support vehicle.

nodes.name: Serpentine powder
nodes.note: Incorporates ingredients into granules by pounding with water, forming a paste that dries into grains. Granules separate less during transport and handling than loose powder.

nodes.name: Shrapnel shell
nodes.note: Filled with lead balls and black powder, bursts in air by time fuse before ground impact. Sprays projectiles over area. Designed by Henry Shrapnel, becomes primary anti-personnel load. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Signals intelligence
nodes.note: Interception and analysis of enemy radio transmissions. Direction finding locates transmitter positions. Traffic analysis reveals unit movements and intentions without decrypting messages.

nodes.name: Sloped armour
nodes.note: Angled armour plate increases effective thickness and deflects projectiles. Provides same protection with less weight than vertical plate. Requires improved cast or welding techniques.

nodes.name: Smokeless powder
nodes.note: Nitrocellulose burns in stages, producing higher pressure without black powder's smoke. Higher velocity, longer range, less fouling in the bore. Shifts tactical range from 300 to 1000 yards. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Sponson
nodes.note: Gun mounting on side of tank hull, projecting outward. Provides wider firing arc than turret alone. Early tanks use multiple sponsons with different ammunition types.

nodes.name: Submarine
nodes.note: Submerged vessel powered by battery or diesel engine. Surfaces to attack or recharge. Difficult to detect and counter. Single submarine can sink fleet carriers. Changes naval strategy fundamentally.

nodes.name: Tank
nodes.note: Tracked armoured vehicle with gun turret, powered by petrol or diesel engine. Crosses trenches, immune to machine gun fire. Requires logistics supply line. Enables breakthrough tactics.

nodes.name: Tank turret
nodes.note: Rotating armoured structure housing gun, rotates independent of hull. Allows aiming without turning vehicle. Requires internal ring and bearings. Becomes standard by 1920.

nodes.name: Torpedo
nodes.note: Cylindrical vessel with explosive warhead, propelled by steam engine or compressed air. Destroys capital ships below waterline where armour is thin. Makes battleships vulnerable to small boats.

nodes.name: Torpedo boat
nodes.note: Small fast steam-powered boat carrying torpedoes. Fast approach under cover of night, fire and withdraw. Cheap compared to battleships, forces capital ships to operate in fleet formations.

nodes.name: Torpedo tube
nodes.note: Pressurized cylinder that launches torpedo using compressed air or water pressure. Must eject cleanly without tilting torpedo. Used in ships and submarines.

nodes.name: Trace italienne
nodes.note: The bastion answers the cannon because a round tower has dead ground at its foot where attackers hide, and an angled bastion does not. Low angled walls cannot be battered. Defense trades height for firepower.

nodes.name: Track system
nodes.note: Linked metal plates forming endless belt around wheels. Distributes weight over large area, enabling crossing soft ground and obstacles. Reduces ground pressure compared to wheels.

nodes.name: Trench
nodes.note: Ditch protecting infantry from machine gun fire and artillery. Requires drainage and reinforcement with wood or concrete. Labor-intensive but fast to construct. Becomes primary infantry defense after 1900.

nodes.name: Trunnion
nodes.note: Horizontal pins on barrel sides that rest in cradle to support gun at any angle. Enables elevation adjustment and absorption of recoil. Precursor to the carriage system.

nodes.name: Turret traverse mechanism
nodes.note: Powered gear system rotates turret. Hand cranks for manual, hydraulic or electric for faster operation. Speed of turret traverse determines engagement capability.

nodes.name: War college
nodes.note: Educational institution teaching military science and strategy to officers. Studies history, tactics, logistics. Produces doctrine and fosters professional culture.

nodes.name: Water jacket
nodes.note: Water-filled steel sleeve around barrel dissipates heat. Allows sustained fire for hours instead of minutes. Adds weight and complexity but multiplies practical sustained rate of fire. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Wheel lock mechanism
nodes.note: Spring-driven spinning wheel strikes flint or pyrite against steel frizzen to generate sparks. Eliminates need for slow match and frees hands, but mechanism is complex and expensive. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Wireless set
nodes.note: Portable radio transmitter-receiver for unit command. Eliminates need for telephone cables. Message delay and security risk compared to telephone. Becomes standard by 1940. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Mineral concessions and access to imperial mines
nodes.note: Mercury (Almaden) and much else is an imperial monopoly. Halves the cost of all ore and metal inputs thereafter.

nodes.name: Tin-mercury amalgam plate mirrors
nodes.note: Roman mirrors are small, dark and mostly polished bronze or lead-backed glass. A true plate mirror is a luxury good with an obscene margin. Mercury vapour will poison your workers; ventilate, rotate them, and do not let them eat in the shop.

nodes.name: Motors, transformers, alternating current
nodes.note: Laminate the cores or eddy currents will eat your efficiency and cook the iron. Three-phase and transformers make distribution possible, which is what turns a workshop generator into a grid. CALENDAR FLOOR is set by diffusion, not by construction: the economy needs roughly a generation to train the trades, form the capital and build the suppliers. Money cannot buy this down. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: laminated cores require thin consistent sheets for efficiency]

nodes.name: Age hardening: precipitation hardening in aluminum-copper alloys
nodes.note: Wilm's 1906 accident: naturally aged aluminum-copper alloy (duralumin) hardened slowly over days. Solution heat-treat above 500C dissolves copper; quench traps supersaturated phase; aging at room or moderate temperature precipitates ultra-fine copper particles, hardening dramatically. Explains why old rivets on aircraft got harder.

nodes.name: Alumina: high-purity aluminum oxide ceramic
nodes.note: Bauxite refined to Al2O3, pressed and fired to 1600-1800C. Melting point 2072C. Used for refractory linings, catalyst supports, crucibles. High purity enables translucent alumina (later). Pre-1950 mostly opaque and dense. Excellent thermal shock resistance.

nodes.name: Aluminum alloy series: systematic development of wrought alloys
nodes.note: 2xxx (Cu-hardened), 3xxx (Mn), 5xxx (Mg), 6xxx (Mg-Si), 7xxx (Zn). Each series has dozens of alloys. Post-1920 systematic alloy development by Alcoa, Hydro, others. Property database built. 7075 (high-strength) came late 1930s. Cold work and heat treatment sequences optimized.

nodes.name: Amalgamation: extracting precious metals with mercury
nodes.note: Mercury dissolves gold and silver; panning, shaking table, or mill rotors coat ore with Hg. Later heating drives off Hg and recovers metal. Spanish New World silver (Potosi) relied on this for 300 years. Toxic and inefficient on low-grade ore, displaced by cyanide.

nodes.name: Annealing: controlled heating and slow cooling to soften and relieve stress
nodes.note: Heating steel to just below critical temperature, holding, then slow cooling in furnace. Allows recrystallization and grain growth; softens cold-worked metal. Permitting in blacksmithing ancient; systematic control with thermometers by 1850.

nodes.name: Austenite formation by heating iron-carbon above critical temperature
nodes.note: Steel heated above A3 temperature (800-900C) transforms to austenite, a high-carbon solid solution of iron. The iron-carbon phase diagram is the map: austenite is the single-phase region where carbon is soluble. Quenching from austenite traps high-carbon at low temperature - martensite.

nodes.name: Babbitt: tin-antimony-copper bearing alloy for journal bearings
nodes.note: Babbitt (1839) patented this bearing alloy: soft at surface, hard at back. Tin-rich alloy (80%+ Sn) poured over steel back; low friction, easy to run in. Critical for railway and steam engine main bearings. Composition varied; high-tin babbitt was superior but expensive. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Ball mill: cylindrical mill with steel balls for fine grinding
nodes.note: Rotating cylinder half-full of steel balls; ore enters one end, grinds as balls tumble, exits other end. Produces fine (-200 mesh) powder for flotation or leaching. Scale from lab to 50+ ton/hr industrial. Post-1890 adoption; became bottleneck, then standard. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Basic Bessemer converter for steel from iron-ore matte
nodes.note: Steel converter lined with magnesia/limestone removes phosphorus by forming phosphate slag that floats. Bessemer process (1856) used acid linings and failed on phosphorus; Thomas-Gilchrist (1878) basic lining solved high-phosphorus iron. Enabled use of minette ore and domestic iron worldwide.

nodes.name: Bell metal: high-tin bronze for resonance
nodes.note: 80% Cu, 20% Sn. High tin content increases brittleness but improves acoustic resonance. Casting is critical: pouring temperature, cooling rate affect tone. Bell founders kept recipes secret; quality varied wildly. Scientific understanding came late (1800s). [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Bone china: high-firing ceramic with calcined bone
nodes.note: China clay mixed with calcined animal bone (ash) and feldspathic material. Fired to 1200-1250C. Whiter, stronger, more translucent than porcelain. English invention (Spode, ~1794). More durable than porcelain; popular for tableware. Competitive pricing vs. true porcelain.

nodes.name: Brinell hardness test: measuring hardness by indentation size
nodes.note: Forcing a hardened ball into material under fixed load; hardness is load divided by indentation surface area. Brinell (1900) developed it; simple and non-destructive (vs. tensile test). Becomes less accurate for very hard materials; superseded by Vickers.

nodes.name: Britannia metal: tin-copper-antimony, tin-spoon alloy
nodes.note: 90%+ tin with copper and antimony hardening. Whiter than pewter, harder, silvered or plated for tableware. Named to appeal to empire (1830s+). Competitive with silver plate. Reheating and recasting similar to type metal. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Carborundum (silicon carbide): ultra-hard ceramic for abrasives
nodes.note: Fusing silica and carbon at 2200C (arc furnace) produces SiC. Acheson (1891) discovered this. Extremely hard (9.5 Mohs), melting point 2700C. Used for grinding wheels, cutting tools, crucibles. Brittle; sintered parts used. Major post-1900 industrial abrasive.

nodes.name: Carburising: enriching surface carbon content by heating in carbon-rich medium
nodes.note: Low-carbon steel in contact with charcoal at 900-950C; carbon diffuses 1-3mm deep. Quenching produces hard case over tough core. Blister steel technique adapted; allows use of wrought iron for tools. Medieval armor makers knew this; systematic use 1600s+.

nodes.name: Cement varieties: Portland and alternatives for construction
nodes.note: Cement types: Portland (high strength, rapid set), white, blast furnace (slag-based), pozzolanic (ash-based). Kiln temperature 1450C; clinker ground fine. Hydration strength develops over weeks-months. Composition (lime, silica, alumina ratios) determines properties. Industrial kiln design critical.

nodes.name: Charpy impact test: measuring toughness by pendulum impact
nodes.note: Notched specimen hit by swinging pendulum; energy absorbed measured by height of rebound. Shows brittle vs. ductile transition with temperature. Charpy (1901) developed it for ship steel; reveals low-temperature brittleness of high-carbon steels and cold-worked materials.

nodes.name: Chromite brick: chromium-iron refractory for extreme duty
nodes.note: Chrome ore sintered and pressed into bricks. Resistant to both acidic and alkaline slag; best all-around refractory. Expensive. Used for premium zones in steelmaking furnaces. Melting point >1800C. Late development (1920s+) for critical applications.

nodes.name: Chromium from chromite ore
nodes.note: Chromite (FeO.Cr2O3) requires aluminothermic reduction; carbon reduction produces brittle chromium carbide, not ductile metal. The 1900s Goldschmidt process made chromium practical. Chromium is critical to stainless steel but extraction was slow. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Classifier: hydraulic or mechanical separation by particle size
nodes.note: Spiral or cone classifier uses settling rate in water to sort particles. Fine material overflows; coarse returns to mill. Recirculating load optimization improves efficiency. Spline (cone) classifier most common. Automatic return control (no human adjustment needed once set). [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Cobalt metal from smaltite and erythrite
nodes.note: Cobalt ores (arsenides and carbonates) must be roasted to destroy arsenic before reduction. The reduced metal is brittle; the discovery is that repeated roasting and reduction cycles improve malleability. German smalt production inadvertently separated cobalt this way. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Constantan: copper-nickel thermocouple wire with stable EMF
nodes.note: 55% Cu, 45% Ni. Thermoelectric properties stable with time; paired with copper for thermocouple. Seebeck effect exploited for temperature measurement. Developed ~1880s for precision thermometry. High electrical resistance.

nodes.name: Copper converter: blowing air through molten matte
nodes.note: Oxidizing blown air through copper matte burns out iron and sulfur, concentrating copper. Bessemer converter adapted to copper work; timing and oxygen control are critical. Later electric furnaces did this better but converter was dominant 1870-1920.

nodes.name: Copper metal by electrowinning from leached ore
nodes.note: Leach copper ore in sulfuric acid or use converter blister copper in spent electrolyte; electrowinning deposits ultra-pure copper cathode. Impurities settle as anode slime (source of gold, silver, selenium). Energy-intensive but produces superior purity. Porphyry copper ores (low grade, high volume) demand this technology. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Copper smelting in reverberatory furnace
nodes.note: Reverberatory furnace reflects flame off the roof onto ore; no direct contact with fuel. Reduces fuel consumption by half vs. earlier open hearth. The flame path control is the innovation; adopted widely 1700-1800 for both copper and tin.

nodes.name: Creep testing: measuring time-dependent deformation at elevated temperature
nodes.note: Holding constant load at high temperature; measuring deformation over hours or days. Metals deform slowly under stress even below yield point. Essential for high-temperature engines, turbines, boilers. Andrade (1910s) studied primary, secondary, tertiary creep regimes.

nodes.name: Crusher: jaw and cone crushers for initial ore size reduction
nodes.note: Jaw crusher uses reciprocating plate; cone crusher rolls against conical surface. Reduces 30cm ore to 5cm. Blake jaw crusher (1858) standard. Powered by steam belt drives. Multiple stages and careful gradation optimize later flotation. Capacity tens of tons/day per unit. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Cyanidation: leaching gold and silver with CN solution
nodes.note: Cyan solutions form soluble gold-cyano and silver-cyano complexes; heap leaching extracts low-grade ore (0.1-1 g/ton). Displacement by zinc powder recovers precious metals. Soluble in 1880s; industrial scale in South Africa 1900+. Replaced amalgamation for low-grade ores.

nodes.name: Dredging: mechanical extraction of ore from sediment and water
nodes.note: Bucket dredges or suction dredges excavate placer deposits. Onboard sluice separates ore. Alluvial tin, gold, diamonds recovered. Post-1890s adoption for marine and riverine deposits. Capital-intensive but high volume. Environmental impact later recognized. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Drifting: horizontal tunneling along ore seams
nodes.note: Following ore body laterally. Less energy than shaft sinking. Ventilation and slope critical to drain water. Rock drill advent (1870s) accelerated. Timber support and bolt pattern evolved with experience. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Ductile (nodular) cast iron: spheroidal graphite for strength and ductility
nodes.note: Adding magnesium or cerium to molten iron forces graphite into spheroids instead of flakes. Tensile strength rivals steel, ductility far exceeds grey iron. Post-1945 development accelerated; by 1950 becoming commercial. Cooling and thermal treatment control structure.

nodes.name: Duralumin: aluminum-copper, age-hardened aircraft alloy
nodes.note: Wilm's 1906 discovery: 4% Cu in aluminum, solution-treated, then naturally ages over days to weeks. Strength increases 200%. Enables lightweight aircraft (Fokker, early Junkers). Alloy composition closely guarded. Susceptible to stress-corrosion cracking.

nodes.name: Dye penetrant inspection: revealing surface cracks in all materials
nodes.note: Penetrating colored or fluorescent liquid into surface cracks, wiping surface, then developer powder highlights cracks. Works on non-magnetic materials (aluminum, stainless). Developed 1940s; became standard post-WW2 for aircraft inspection.

nodes.name: Earthenware: low-fired, porous ceramic for everyday use
nodes.note: Clay fired to 1000-1150C. Porous (absorbs water); quick to make and glaze. Terracotta tradition ancient. Medieval and later earthenware (faience) decorated and glazed. Lead glaze toxic but durable. Still competitive with stoneware for decorative ware.

nodes.name: Electrorefining: purifying crude metal via anode dissolution
nodes.note: Crude metal as anode dissolves selectively; pure metal plates on cathode. Impurities less noble than the metal sink as anode slime; impurities more noble do not dissolve. Copper, nickel, lead all purify this way. Wollaston and others developed it; became essential by 1900. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Elinvar: nickel-steel for elastic constant independence from temperature
nodes.note: Elastic modulus constant with temperature (unlike normal metals). Guillaume (1920s) developed this for watch balances and precision springs. Requires careful composition control and heat treatment. Complex metallurgy; few suppliers.

nodes.name: Fatigue testing: measuring S-N curve and stress-life endurance
nodes.note: Cyclically loading specimen until fracture; plotting stress vs. number of cycles to failure. Wohler (1850s) began this; revealed that failure occurs below ultimate strength if cycled. Machine development (rotating beam, hydraulic) enabled systematic study. Critical for railways and machinery.

nodes.name: Froth flotation: separating sulfide ore minerals by hydrophobic bonding
nodes.note: Finely ground ore suspended in water with collector (xanthate); air bubbles preferentially attach sulfides via hydrophobic interaction. Froth overflows carrying ore; tailings sink. Replaces heavy metals gravity separation. Patented Elmore (1899); became standard 1900-1920 for copper, lead, zinc.

nodes.name: German silver (nickel silver): copper-nickel-zinc without silver
nodes.note: 60-65% Cu, 15-20% Ni, 20% Zn. White color and tarnish resistance like silver without cost. Chinese paktong (nickel alloy) known since 1200s; European 'German silver' ~1820s. Plated with sterling silver; competed with Sheffield plate.

nodes.name: Glass fiber: fine filaments for insulation and reinforcement
nodes.note: Drawing molten glass into fine fibers; bundling and binding with resin. Excellent insulation, low density, fire resistant. Industrial production ~1930s (Owens Corning). Pre-1950 mostly laboratory and premium applications. Binding technology critical. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Grain size control: understanding how grain size affects mechanical properties
nodes.note: Fine grains improve impact strength and ductility; coarse grains improve high-temperature strength. Grain size controlled by austenitizing temperature and cooling rate. Metallography (etching and microscopy) revealed grain structure; Hall-Petch relation became clear by 1950.

nodes.name: Grey cast iron: graphite-rich iron for castings
nodes.note: 2-4% C, graphite particles (flakes) in ferrite/pearlite matrix. Lower melting point than steel (1200C), flows well. Graphite acts as internal lubricant; machinable. Weak in tension (brittle), strong in compression. Cylinder blocks, engine beds, pipes. Cooling rate controls structure.

nodes.name: Gunmetal: copper-tin-zinc alloy for cannons and bearings
nodes.note: 90% Cu, 9% Sn, 1% Zn (approximate). Stronger than pure bronze, better for pressure vessels and bearings. Bell makers used similar alloys; gunmetal formalization came with artillery demand. Redeemed scrap metal by adjusting composition.

nodes.name: Hadfield manganese steel: work-hardening steel for severe impact
nodes.note: 11-14% Mn, 1% C. Austenitic, very tough, hardens tremendously under impact (work hardening). Used for railway switches, crusher jaws, military armor. Hadfield (1880s) patent; microstructure was mysterious (austenite + brittle carbides plus transformation). Weldable with difficulty.

nodes.name: High speed steel (HSS): tungsten-molybdenum-vanadium tool steel
nodes.note: 18-4-1 (W-Mo-V-Co) formula typical. Taylor-White (1900) discovered that high-speed steel can cut steel at 100+ m/min (vs. 20 for carbon steel). Hardness retained above 600C. Red-hard alloy. Quenching and tempering critical; superseded by carbides but still used.

nodes.name: Hydraulic mining: washing ore and overburden with water pressure
nodes.note: High-pressure water from elevated reservoirs erodes gold placer deposits (California, 1870s). Nozzles direct flow. Sluices recover gold. Environmentally destructive (sediment); banned in sensitive areas by 1880s. Efficient but limited to near-surface, unconsolidated deposits. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Induction furnace for high-quality alloy steel
nodes.note: AC current through a coil induces eddy currents in metal charge, heating without fuel. No fuel impurities, better composition control. Developed ~1900; expensive until WW1 demand drove production. Allows vacuum melting alloys later.

nodes.name: Induction hardening: localized heating by eddy currents for rapid quenching
nodes.note: High-frequency AC through a coil heats steel to austenite temperature in seconds; quench water immediately cools it. Only selected areas harden (gear teeth, bearing races). Eliminates distortion from long heating. German development ~1910; became standard by 1930.

nodes.name: Invar: nickel-iron for low thermal expansion
nodes.note: 35-36% Ni, 64-65% Fe. Thermal expansion near zero around room temperature. Guillaume (1896) discovered this; critical for precision instruments (standards, pendulums). Used for surveying chains and scientific apparatus. Expensive and difficult to machine.

nodes.name: Izod impact test: vertical notched-bar impact measurement
nodes.note: Similar to Charpy but different specimen geometry and impact geometry. Izod (1903) developed it as competitor to Charpy. Both reveal toughness; Charpy became more standard. Different results due to specimen constraint; both useful for comparison.

nodes.name: Jackhammer: portable pneumatic pick for ore breaking
nodes.note: Lighter and more portable than mounted drill. One or two workers operate. Air hose supply from central compressor. Reduces fatigue and increases productivity 5-10x compared to hand picks. Post-1900 adoption widespread. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Laminated glass: bonded layers for shatter resistance
nodes.note: Glass sheets bonded with cellulose nitrate or acetate interlayer. Shatters but does not fall apart. Triplex patent (1909). Used for aircraft and automotive safety. Post-WW1 adoption. Adhesive layer must remain flexible and optically clear. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Chemical leaching: dissolving ore in sulfuric or nitric acid
nodes.note: Heap or vat leaching dissolves ore in acid solution (CuSO4 for copper, FeSO4 for others). Solid residue filtered; solution concentrated and metal recovered by displacement or electrolysis. Industrial scale for copper, nickel from laterite by 1920. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Lead glass (flint glass): high-refractive-index optical glass
nodes.note: Lead oxide 30-40% increases refractive index and reduces dispersion (makes white light). Enables precision lenses without excessive aberrations. Heavy and dense; toxic if mishandled. English development (18th century); craft closely guarded. Grinding and polishing critical. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Magnesite brick: magnesia refractory for basic furnaces
nodes.note: Dead-burned magnesite (MgO sintered at 1600C+) pressed into bricks, refired to 1700C+. Resists alkaline slag. Critical for basic converter, open hearth. Expensive and fragile. Requires careful handling and furnace design to avoid spalling.

nodes.name: Magnesium alloys: weight reduction with controlled corrosion
nodes.note: Magnesium 2/3 density of aluminum, 1/3 steel. Alloying with aluminum, zinc, manganese improves strength; beryllium suppresses grain growth. Difficult casting (pyrophoric, needs argon protection). Limited commercial use before 1940. Post-WW2 demand for aerospace grew applications.

nodes.name: Magnesium metal from seawater and mineral salts
nodes.note: Magnesium is isolated by precipitating MgCl2 from seawater as Mg(OH)2, dissolving in HCl, then electrolyzing molten magnesium chloride (fused salt electrolysis). Dow process (1916) made electrolytic extraction practical. Earlier, magnesium came from Epsom salt reduction - tiny scale. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Magnetic particle inspection: revealing surface and near-surface defects
nodes.note: Magnetizing part and applying ferrous particles; defects distort field and trap particles, revealing crack patterns. Non-destructive, fast, inexpensive. Developed 1920s; by 1930s standard for forgings and welds. Only works on ferromagnetic materials.

nodes.name: Malleable cast iron: annealed white iron, ductile
nodes.note: White iron reheated to 900C for 50+ hours; carbon atoms aggregate into graphite nodules, cementite dissolves. Matrix becomes ferrite (soft); dramatic ductility increase. Expensive process but enables casting complex shapes that must survive impact (automotive, machinery).

nodes.name: Manganese metal from pyrolusite
