nodes.note: Chemical treatment slows combustion, essential for children's wear and upholstery, various formulations with durability challenges

nodes.name: Flax cultivation and fibre
nodes.note: Long bast fibres from flax plant, strongest vegetable fibre, linen production base, Mediterranean and European cultivation

nodes.name: Flyer: the earliest spinning frame component
nodes.note: U-shaped guide of twisted metal, draws fibre at constant rate while imparting twist, basis of all frame spinning before the ring frame

nodes.name: Fountain pen: reservoir writing
nodes.note: Internal ink reservoir and feed system, iridium or gold nib, Waterman patent 1884 creates commercial success, transforms business writing

nodes.name: Friction match: white phosphorus tip
nodes.note: White phosphorus mixed with oxidiser at stick tip, ignites spontaneously in air, dangerous but widespread in 19th century

nodes.name: Fulling: cloth densification
nodes.note: Mechanical or chemical treatment matts fibres, shrinks and densifies cloth, essential for wool cloth, water-powered fulling mills

nodes.name: Gilling: parallel alignment after combing
nodes.note: Two finely-toothed combs slide over fibres held in roller nips, removes remaining short fibres and duplicates combing process

nodes.name: Glass fibre: silica filament
nodes.note: Fine glass filaments drawn from melt, high strength and temperature resistance, industrial applications in 1930s [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Gramophone: sound recording reproduction
nodes.note: Needle-vibration pickup playing wax cylinder or disc, horn amplification, emerges in 1890s and becomes major consumer product

nodes.name: Hackling: combing and grading fibres
nodes.note: Pins set in flat boards, four grades of hecklers pull fibre through progressively finer pins, separates long line from short tow

nodes.name: Heddle: warp thread carrier and riser
nodes.note: Metal or string loop holding warp thread, rises and falls to create shed, hand production in early looms

nodes.name: Hemp cultivation and fibre
nodes.note: Similar to flax, coarser and stronger, rope and canvas use, European cultivation common

nodes.name: Hook and eye: wire fastener
nodes.note: Hand-formed wire hook and eye loop, traditional closure, essential for corsets and men's breeches

nodes.name: Jacquard cards: pattern storage and control
nodes.note: Punched cards laced together, each row represents one pick, hole position controls hook, complex patterns require hundreds of cards

nodes.name: Jacquard head: automatic pattern control
nodes.note: Each warp thread on independent hook, punched cards control individual hooks, enables arbitrary patterns, complex and expensive

nodes.name: Jigsaw puzzle: dissectable picture
nodes.note: Printed image on wood or cardboard, hand-sawed or die-cut into interlocking pieces, emerges in 18th century as education and entertainment

nodes.name: Jute cultivation and fibre
nodes.note: Indian river plant, coarse bast fibre, cheap and fast-growing, bagging and carpet use, emerges as industrial fibre in 19th century

nodes.name: Lasting machine: shoe fitting
nodes.note: Pneumatic or mechanical clamps pull upper leather over wooden last, tension nails sole attachment, eliminates hand work

nodes.name: Latch needle: self-contained knit mechanism
nodes.note: Self-closing latch eliminates spring requirement, lighter pressure, enables higher gauge and finer yarns, invention transformed knitting

nodes.name: Let-off: warp feed control
nodes.note: Brake on warp beam, maintains constant tension as yarn unwound, keeps warp on take-up synchronized

nodes.name: Lockstitch: two-thread interlocking
nodes.note: Needle loop interlocks with bobbin loop, requires precise timing and tension, most important sewing machine invention

nodes.name: Mass-produced soap: standardised bars
nodes.note: Standardised formulation and cutting, wrapped and branded, Procter and Gamble transforms soap into mass-market good

nodes.name: Mercerising: caustic treatment
nodes.note: Caustic soda under tension swell and align cotton fibres, increases lustre and dye uptake, becomes permanent feature of premium cotton

nodes.name: Milling: extended fulling
nodes.note: Continued fulling process, creates thick dense cloth, especially for woollen fabrics and felt-like handle

nodes.name: Mirror: reflective glass surface
nodes.note: Mercury backing silvered glass, produced in quantity by medieval period, tin-amalgam backing emerges as alternative

nodes.name: Mohair: angora goat fibre
nodes.note: Turkish angora goat fibre, lustrous and strong, luxury use, Istanbul region monopoly until late 19th century

nodes.name: Mothproofing: insect resistance
nodes.note: Toxic treatment repels moths, essential for wool storage, formulations including arsenic compounds, durability limited

nodes.name: Spinning mule: draw-twist-wind
nodes.note: Carriage moves in and out, spindles move back and forth, intermittent action allows finer yarns than ring frame, handcraft for winding, steam-powered versions still require skill

nodes.name: Needle: sewing implement
nodes.note: Polished iron or steel with eye, essential tool before sewing machines, hand-forged labour-intensive

nodes.name: Nylon 6,6: polyamide synthesis
nodes.note: First fully synthetic fibre from petroleum, extraordinary durability and elasticity, DuPont patented 1935, launched 1940

nodes.name: Overlock: edge-covering stitch
nodes.note: Multiple threads bind over edge, prevents fraying and seals edge, specialist machines emerge in 1890s

nodes.name: Paper bag: folded container
nodes.note: Kraft paper folded and glued, bottom gussets for capacity, replaces cloth sacks for retail goods

nodes.name: Paper pattern: home sewing pattern
nodes.note: Printed pattern pieces and instructions, mass-market product, Butterick patterns emerge in 1860s, enables home dressmaking

nodes.name: Paperclip: bent wire fastener
nodes.note: Wire bent into overlapping loops, simple but effective, mass production by 1900s enables cheap office supplies

nodes.name: Pattern grading: multi-size scaling
nodes.note: Master patterns scaled to multiple sizes, essential for ready-to-wear, ratio grading becomes standard practice

nodes.name: Pencil: graphite and clay mixture
nodes.note: Ground graphite and clay mixed and fired, Conté and others develop proportions and hardness grades

nodes.name: Permanent press: wrinkle resistance
nodes.note: Resin cross-linking sets cloth shape, major innovation in 1930s-1940s, requires formaldehyde chemistry and heat treatment

nodes.name: Picking: mechanical shuttle propulsion
nodes.note: Rotating cam drives picker sticks that strike shuttle, replaces hand throwing, enables power loom and higher speeds

nodes.name: Pin: sewing fastener
nodes.note: Drawn wire with point and head, hand-made labour-intensive process, medieval production by thousands

nodes.name: Printed playing card: mass-produced game
nodes.note: Hand-painted precedes printing, printing press enables mass production, stiff card and artistic design

nodes.name: Polyester: terylene synthesis
nodes.note: Polyethylene terephthalate condensation, extremely versatile, crease resistance, ICI developed pre-1950 but mass production post-war

nodes.name: Postcard: prepaid correspondence
nodes.note: Thin card with pre-printed postage, emerges as cheap alternative to letters, mass-produced by 1870s

nodes.name: Press stud: snap fastener
nodes.note: Four-piece metal fastener, ball and socket interlock, emerges in late 19th century, easier than buttons for infant wear

nodes.name: Block printing: carved design application
nodes.note: Hand-carved wooden blocks with raised design, dipped in dye and stamped repeatedly, high labour for design creation

nodes.name: Roller printing: engraved cylinder application
nodes.note: Engraved copper roller applies pattern continuously, replaces block printing, enables fine detail and high speed, expensive engraving [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Screen printing: mesh stencil application
nodes.note: Silk or other mesh with photographic emulsion stencil, squeegee forces dye through, emerges in 1920s for fine art and textile printing [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Radio set: wireless receiver entertainment
nodes.note: Crystal set or valve receiver and loudspeaker, mass production transforms home entertainment, major emergence in 1920s

nodes.name: Raising: fibre napping
nodes.note: Rotating cylinder with teasel or wire brushes teases fibre ends to surface, mechanical replacement for hand teasel

nodes.name: Ramie cultivation and fibre
nodes.note: Asian bast fibre, fine and strong, China and India production, difficult processing limits adoption

nodes.name: Rayon by acetate: cellulose acetate
nodes.note: Cellulose acetate spun directly, not regenerated cellulose, safer and easier than cupro, emerges in 1920s

nodes.name: Rayon by cupro: copper-ammonia process
nodes.note: Cellulose in copper-ammonia complex spun through air, smoother than viscose, excellent silk-like lustre, emerges in 1890s

nodes.name: Rayon by nitration: cellulose nitrate
nodes.note: Cellulose nitrate dissolved and extruded, first artificial fibre, flammable and unstable, replaced by safer cupro rayon

nodes.name: Rayon by viscose: alkali-carbon disulfide process
nodes.note: Most important rayon process, versatile and scalable, controls properties by coagulation bath, dominant by 1920s

nodes.name: Razor blade: replaceable steel cutting
nodes.note: Stamped and honed thin steel blade, consumable product, razor-blade business model generates recurring revenue

nodes.name: Ready-to-wear: mass-produced garments
nodes.note: Factory-made garments in standard sizes, replaces bespoke tailoring for most consumers, emerged mid-19th century in America

nodes.name: Resist dyeing: pattern preservation
nodes.note: Wax or paste mask areas of cloth before dyeing, creates patterns through negative space, includes batik and tie-dye

nodes.name: Retting of flax and hemp fibres
nodes.note: Water or dew retting breaks down pectin binding fibre to woody core, controlled fermentation in standing water

nodes.name: Ring frame: the dominant spinning geometry
nodes.note: Traveller slides on fixed ring, spindle rotates below, continuous yarn formation, allows higher speeds and finer counts, gradually displaced cap frame from 1870s

nodes.name: Rope laying: strand twisting
nodes.note: Three or more yarns twisted together, fundamental construction, creates rope from fibre strands

nodes.name: Ropemaking machine: mechanised twisting
nodes.note: Rotating frames twist strand into rope, water-powered mills standard, enables continuous production

nodes.name: Roving frame: fibre attenuation and twist
nodes.note: Rollers at progressively faster speeds attenuate fibres, flyer imparts twist, produces roving ready for spinning frame

nodes.name: Rubber soles: vulcanised footwear
nodes.note: Vulcanised rubber soles reduce cost and improve water resistance, attached by cements or nailing, increasingly common from 1890s

nodes.name: Safety match: controlled ignition
nodes.note: Phosphorus on match strip, ignition requires friction on box strip, much safer than friction matches, Swedish invention 1844

nodes.name: Safety razor: guarded blade shaving
nodes.note: Thin steel blade held in guard, Gillette patent 1901, replaceable blade and guard system, transformed male grooming

nodes.name: Scouring: removal of grease and soil
nodes.note: Hot alkali bath removes natural oils and dirt, essential preparatory step for dyeing and bleaching, caustic or soap-based

nodes.name: Screw cap: threaded closure
nodes.note: Threaded metal cap screws onto grooved bottle neck, reusable and reversible, evolves from wood to plastic

nodes.name: Scutching: breaking fibres from woody core
nodes.note: Scutching board and wooden scutcher blade beat retting fibre to separate long bast fibres from brittle woody break, crude mechanisation with flails

nodes.name: Selvedge: woven cloth edge
nodes.note: Finished edge from shuttle reversing, tighter weave than body, essential for quality cloth, achieved by plain weave turn-around

nodes.name: Sericulture: silk production
nodes.note: Silkworm rearing and cocoon processing, stifling and degumming, labour-intensive, Chinese and Indian expertise

nodes.name: Sewing machine: domestic version
nodes.note: Human-powered treadle or hand crank, complex motion conversion, Singer and others dominated market, transformed home sewing

nodes.name: Sewing machine: industrial version
nodes.note: Steam or electric powered, higher speeds and heavier fabrics, multiple machines linked by belts, factory standard from 1870s

nodes.name: Shaft: harness frame assembly
nodes.note: Wooden frame holding heddles, multiple shafts create different shed patterns, basic hand loom has four shafts for tabby and twill

nodes.name: Shampoo: hair cleansing liquid
nodes.note: Liquid soap formulation specifically for hair, emerges in early 20th century, mass production and branding key factors

nodes.name: Shearing: precision cutting
nodes.note: Stationary blade against rotating grooved drum cuts pile uniformly, produces velvet and pile fabrics

nodes.name: Shed: warp separation for pick insertion
nodes.note: Opening between warp threads for shuttle passage, basic concept behind all weaving machines

nodes.name: Mechanised shoemaking: factory production
nodes.note: Chain of specialized machines and workers, division of labour, higher speed and lower cost, emerged in America mid-1800s

nodes.name: Shuttle: weft carrier and timing
nodes.note: Pointed boat-shaped carrier holding bobbin, travels through shed, must be timed to stop at selvage, critical for loom speed

nodes.name: Silk: cultivated fibre
nodes.note: Protein fibre from silkworm cocoon, continuous filament, lustrous, expensive, Asian production trademarked

nodes.name: Singeing: flame removal of nap
nodes.note: Open flame across cloth surface burns fine fibres, produces smooth finish, replaces hand holding over candle with continuous flame

nodes.name: Sizing systems: body measurement standardisation
nodes.note: Standard body measurements and fit models, crucial for mass production, significant variation by country and manufacturer

nodes.name: Sliver: card output and sliver can
nodes.note: Coiled card output into sliver can, preparatory to drawing frame, loose strand of carded fibres with no twist

nodes.name: Spectacle frame: eye support structure
nodes.note: Horn or metal frame holding optical lenses, nose bridge and arms, emerged in medieval period with mass production in 1800s

nodes.name: Splitting: leather layering
nodes.note: Separating hide into grain and buff layers, enables utilisation of full hide, requires sharp hand knives or mechanical blade

nodes.name: Stapler: metal wire fastener machine
nodes.note: Lever mechanism bends staple through papers, powered by hand, emerges in late 1800s as office automation

nodes.name: Stocking frame: hosiery machine
nodes.note: Reciprocating needles hold loops, springs pull down, needles rise to throw loop, produces high-quality hosiery, skilled operator control

nodes.name: Take-up: woven cloth winding
nodes.note: Graduated drum winds woven cloth at controlled rate, compensates for warp tension, prevents bunching

nodes.name: Temple: cloth width maintenance
nodes.note: Expanding frame with sharp points, maintains woven cloth width against warp tension, prevents draw-in

nodes.name: Throstle: continuous drawing and twist
nodes.note: Ring frame with spindle speed matched to roller draft, fully continuous, better for coarser counts than mule, easier to automate than mule

nodes.name: Tin can: sealed metal container
nodes.note: Rolled and soldered tin plate, preserves food and other goods, mass production from 1810s onwards

nodes.name: Tin toy: stamped metal plaything
nodes.note: Stamped and lithographed tin plate toy, jointed or wheeled, German and Japanese production emerges in late 1800s

nodes.name: Toothbrush: hair bristle cleaning
nodes.note: Natural bristles set in wooden handle, Chinese technology known early, mass production in Europe from late 1800s

nodes.name: Tube for toothpaste: extrudable container
nodes.note: Collapsible metal tube with sealed cap, contents extruded by squeezing, enables portable toothpaste

nodes.name: Twist insertion control
nodes.note: Twist multiplier, turns per inch, balances strength and handle, S and Z directions, critical knowledge for spinner

nodes.name: Vacuum flask: thermal insulation
nodes.note: Double-walled glass with vacuum between, reflective surfaces, Thermos trade name, emerges in 1900s for portable hot beverages

nodes.name: Vegetable tanning: oak bark curing
nodes.note: Tannins from oak bark bind to collagen, slow process taking months, produces supple and durable leather, traditional method

nodes.name: Warp knitting: sheet production
nodes.note: Multiple yarn guides feed warp-wise, creates sheet fabric instead of tube, less stretch than weft knitting, high speed possible

nodes.name: Warp sizing: fibre stiffening
nodes.note: Starch or other binder applied to warp, increases abrasion resistance and stiffness, essential for high-speed weaving

nodes.name: Warping mill: warp thread length setting
nodes.note: Large wheel and pegs set warp length and thread count, critical for accurate cloth dimensions

nodes.name: Watch case: portable timepiece housing
nodes.note: Protective case for pocket watch, brass with decorative engraving or gold cases, industrial production emerges in 1800s

nodes.name: Waterproofing: moisture resistance
nodes.note: Oil or wax coating repels water, essential for outdoor wear, reduces breathability, various formulations tested in early 20th century

nodes.name: Wild silk: non-cultivated production
nodes.note: Silk from wild moth cocoons, shorter filament and darker colour, Tussar and Muga silks from India and China

nodes.name: Wool: sheep fibre
nodes.note: Protein fibre from sheep, natural crimp and elasticity, warmth and moisture absorption, Mediterranean and Northern European production

nodes.name: Worsted: combed wool yarn
nodes.note: Combed long-staple wool, smooth and strong, fine suiting yarns, English West Country specialty from medieval period

nodes.name: Zip fastener: metal hook closure
nodes.note: Interlocking metal teeth on two tapes, slider engages hooks, invented in 1890s but refined in 1920s for widespread adoption

nodes.name: Define and publish standard length, mass, time and temperature
nodes.note: Do this before writing any other recipe down. Every number in your corpus is meaningless to posterity without it. Make master standards in bronze, in triplicate, deposited in three cities.

nodes.name: Sprengel mercury pump and high vacuum
nodes.note: THE cheap shortcut of the endgame. Falling mercury drops each trap a slug of gas and carry it out. No pistons, no seals, no tolerances, and it reaches pressures good enough for discharge tubes and lamps using nothing but glass tubing and mercury. It skips the whole precision-machining prerequisite that a piston pump would impose. Add a McLeod gauge, which is the same trick in reverse, to know what you have achieved.

nodes.name: Diode, triode, and the first amplifier
nodes.note: Glass-to-metal seals need matched thermal expansion (Dumet wire) or they crack; getters finish the vacuum after sealing. A working amplifier transforms every instrument you own and is the practical precondition for doing sensitive semiconductor measurements at all. CALENDAR FLOOR is set by diffusion, not by construction: the economy needs roughly a generation to train the trades, form the capital and build the suppliers. Money cannot buy this down. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_vac_1e6 added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: triode and amplifier require very high vacuum to prevent arcing and ensure long tube life]

nodes.name: Voltaic pile
nodes.note: Trivially cheap once zinc metal exists, and utterly impossible before it. This is why zinc is on the critical path and why almost every plan misses it. Continuous current for the first time in history, and everything electrical follows. It needs copper DISCS, not fine insulated wire, so it does not wait on the wire-insulation node.

nodes.name: Overshot wheels, millponds, leats, line shafting
nodes.note: Rome already has this (Barbegal, 16 wheels). What is missing is applying it to anything other than grinding grain. Put the bellows, the stamps, the paper mill, the boring mill and the lathe on the same shaft. [AUDIT: this node does not declare the capability rung it needs. An automated pass once inferred one, and an independent review found that EVERY inferred rung it sampled was wrong, so all of them were reverted. The gap is left visible on purpose: a missing prerequisite you can see beats a wrong one you cannot.]

nodes.name: First workshop and laboratory
nodes.note: On navigable water. With a walled yard, a separate furnace shed downwind, and a door onto the street so that witnesses can see you are not conjuring.

nodes.name: Publish an accurate world map and sailing directions
nodes.note: Nearly free, immediately impressive, militarily and commercially valuable, and hard to call magic. Present as compiled from Indian and Chinese merchant reports. Ptolemy's Geography is c. 150 AD, so you are 50 years early, which is credible rather than miraculous.

nodes.name: Zinc smelting at industrial scale, with flue dust collection
nodes.note: Zinc earns its own way as brass, galvanising and batteries. Its second and hidden purpose is that germanium concentrates in the flue dust of zinc smelters, at the parts-per-thousand level in the dust against 1.6 ppm in the crust. Design the flues for dust collection from the first furnace or you will rebuild them later. CALENDAR FLOOR is set by diffusion, not by construction: the economy needs roughly a generation to train the trades, form the capital and build the suppliers. Money cannot buy this down. [SCALED: this is an INDUSTRY, not a demonstration. At 1500 tonnes of product a year it consumes about 18,000 tonnes of charcoal annually, derived from the physical ratio in data/world/resources.json rather than guessed. At 0.75 tonnes of charcoal per hectare of coppice per year that is roughly 24,000 hectares of forest under permanent management, which you must own before you light it.]

nodes.name: Zinc metal by downward distillation
nodes.note: CRITICAL PATH, and nobody guesses it. Zinc boils at 907 C, below the temperature at which calamine is reduced, so the metal leaves as vapour and reburns at the furnace mouth. That is precisely why Rome makes brass by cementation and has never seen the metal. Seal the retort and condense downward, as at Zawar. Without this there is no good voltaic pile, and without a pile there is no electricity. It is also your realistic germanium source, twice over. [SCALED: this is an INDUSTRY, not a demonstration. At 20 tonnes of product a year it consumes about 240 tonnes of charcoal annually, derived from the physical ratio in data/world/resources.json rather than guessed. At 0.75 tonnes of charcoal per hectare of coppice per year that is roughly 320 hectares of forest under permanent management, which you must own before you light it.]

nodes.name: Zone refining to one part in 1e9
nodes.note: The specific trick that makes semiconductors possible at all. Most impurities prefer the liquid, so a narrow molten zone dragged along an ingot sweeps them to one end; repeat and the purity compounds. Nothing else reaches these levels. It needs a tube furnace, a quartz or graphite boat, a hydrogen or inert atmosphere, and a way to move a heater slowly and repeatably, which is why it waits on motors. [REVIEWED: prerequisite(s) cap_measure_temp_hi, cap_tol_10um added by a reviewer working node by node. Reason: dragging molten zone requires high-temperature pyrometry at melting point and slide rest precision for heater control]
